units.leftText: This is the vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem that Isaiah son of Amoz saw during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
units.rightText: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

units.leftText: Listen, O heavens, and give ear, O earth, for the LORD has spoken: “I have raised children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against Me.
units.rightText: Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth; for Jehovah hath spoken: I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me.

units.leftText: The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master’s manger, but Israel does not know; My people do not understand.”
units.rightText: The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master’s crib; but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.

units.leftText: Alas, O sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a brood of evildoers, children who act corruptly! They have forsaken the LORD; they have despised the Holy One of Israel and turned their backs on Him.
units.rightText: Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evil-doers, children that deal corruptly! they have forsaken Jehovah, they have despised the Holy One of Israel, they are estranged and gone backward.

units.leftText: Why do you want more beatings? Why do you keep rebelling? Your head has a massive wound, and your whole heart is afflicted.
units.rightText: Why will ye be still stricken, that ye revolt more and more? the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.

units.leftText: From the sole of your foot to the top of your head, there is no soundness— only wounds and welts and festering sores neither cleansed nor bandaged nor soothed with oil.
units.rightText: From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and fresh stripes: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with oil.

units.leftText: Your land is desolate; your cities are burned with fire. Foreigners devour your fields before you — a desolation demolished by strangers.
units.rightText: Your country is desolate; your cities are burned with fire; your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.

units.leftText: And the Daughter of Zion is abandoned like a shelter in a vineyard, like a shack in a cucumber field, like a city besieged.
units.rightText: And the daughter of Zion is left as a booth in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city.

units.leftText: Unless the LORD of Hosts had left us a few survivors, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah. Meaningless Offerings
units.rightText: Except Jehovah of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, we should have been like unto Gomorrah.
leftNotes: 1:9 LXX had left us descendants
1:9 Cited in Romans 9:29|ROM 9:29*

units.leftText: Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom; listen to the instruction of our God, you people of Gomorrah!
units.rightText: Hear the word of Jehovah, ye rulers of Sodom; give ear unto the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrah.

units.leftText: “What good to Me is your multitude of sacrifices?” says the LORD. “I am full from the burnt offerings of rams and the fat of well-fed cattle; I take no delight in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats.
units.rightText: What unto me is the multitude of your sacrifices? saith Jehovah: I have had enough of the burnt-offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he-goats.

units.leftText: When you come to appear before Me, who has required this of you— this trampling of My courts?
units.rightText: When ye come to appear before me, who hath required this at your hand, to trample my courts?

units.leftText: Bring your worthless offerings no more; your incense is detestable to Me. New Moons, Sabbaths, and convocations— I cannot endure iniquity in a solemn assembly.
units.rightText: Bring no more vain oblations; incense is an abomination unto me; new moon and sabbath, the calling of assemblies,—I cannot away with iniquity and the solemn meeting.

units.leftText: I hate your New Moons and your appointed feasts. They have become a burden to Me; I am weary of bearing them.
units.rightText: Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hateth; they are a trouble unto me; I am weary of bearing them.

units.leftText: When you spread out your hands in prayer, I will hide My eyes from you; even though you multiply your prayers, I will not listen. Your hands are covered with blood.
units.rightText: And when ye spread forth your hands, I will hide mine eyes from you; yea, when ye make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood.

units.leftText: Wash and cleanse yourselves. Remove your evil deeds from My sight. Stop doing evil!
units.rightText: Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil;

units.leftText: Learn to do right; seek justice and correct the oppressor. Defend the fatherless and plead the case of the widow.”
units.rightText: learn to do well; seek justice, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.
leftNotes: 1:17 Or and encourage the oppressed

units.leftText: “Come now, let us reason together,” says the LORD. “Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow; though they are as red as crimson, they will become like wool.
units.rightText: Come now, and let us reason together, saith Jehovah: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

units.leftText: If you are willing and obedient, you will eat the best of the land.
units.rightText: If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land:

units.leftText: But if you resist and rebel, you will be devoured by the sword.” For the mouth of the LORD has spoken. The Corruption of Zion
units.rightText: but if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword; for the mouth of Jehovah hath spoken it.

units.leftText: See how the faithful city has become a harlot! She once was full of justice; righteousness resided within her, but now only murderers!
units.rightText: How is the faithful city become a harlot! she that was full of justice! righteousness lodged in her, but now murderers.

units.leftText: Your silver has become dross; your fine wine is diluted with water.
units.rightText: Thy silver is become dross, thy wine mixed with water.

units.leftText: Your rulers are rebels, friends of thieves. They all love bribes and chasing after rewards. They do not defend the fatherless, and the plea of the widow never comes before them.
units.rightText: Thy princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves; every one loveth bribes, and followeth after rewards: they judge not the fatherless, neither doth the cause of the widow come unto them.

units.leftText: Therefore the Lord GOD of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, declares: “Ah, I will be relieved of My foes and avenge Myself on My enemies.
units.rightText: Therefore saith the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, Ah, I will ease me of mine adversaries, and avenge me of mine enemies;

units.leftText: I will turn My hand against you; I will thoroughly purge your dross; I will remove all your impurities.
units.rightText: and I will turn my hand upon thee, and thoroughly purge away thy dross, and will take away all thy tin;

units.leftText: I will restore your judges as at first, and your counselors as at the beginning. After that you will be called the City of Righteousness, the Faithful City.”
units.rightText: and I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called The city of righteousness, a faithful town.

units.leftText: Zion will be redeemed with justice, her repentant ones with righteousness.
units.rightText: Zion shall be redeemed with justice, and her converts with righteousness.

units.leftText: But rebels and sinners will together be shattered, and those who forsake the LORD will perish.
units.rightText: But the destruction of transgressors and sinners shall be together, and they that forsake Jehovah shall be consumed.

units.leftText: Surely you will be ashamed of the sacred oaks in which you have delighted; you will be embarrassed by the gardens that you have chosen.
units.rightText: For they shall be ashamed of the oaks which ye have desired, and ye shall be confounded for the gardens that ye have chosen.

units.leftText: For you will become like an oak whose leaves are withered, like a garden without water.
units.rightText: For ye shall be as an oak whose leaf fadeth, and as a garden that hath no water.

units.leftText: The strong man will become tinder and his work will be a spark; both will burn together, with no one to quench the flames.
units.rightText: And the strong shall be as tow, and his work as a spark; and they shall both burn together, and none shall quench them.

units.leftText: This is the message that was revealed to Isaiah son of Amoz concerning Judah and Jerusalem:
units.rightText: The word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.

units.leftText: In the last days the mountain of the house of the LORD will be established as the chief of the mountains; it will be raised above the hills, and all nations will stream to it.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in the latter days, that the mountain of Jehovah’s house shall be established on the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it.

units.leftText: And many peoples will come and say: “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will teach us His ways so that we may walk in His paths.” For the law will go forth from Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And many peoples shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of Jehovah, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of Jehovah from Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Then He will judge between the nations and arbitrate for many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will no longer take up the sword against nation, nor train anymore for war. The Day of Reckoning
units.rightText: And he will judge between the nations, and will decide concerning many peoples; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning-hooks; nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.

units.leftText: Come, O house of Jacob, let us walk in the light of the LORD.
units.rightText: O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk in the light of Jehovah.

units.leftText: For You have abandoned Your people, the house of Jacob, because they are filled with influences from the east; they are soothsayers like the Philistines; they strike hands with the children of foreigners.
units.rightText: For thou hast forsaken thy people the house of Jacob, because they are filled with customs from the east, and are soothsayers like the Philistines, and they strike hands with the children of foreigners.

units.leftText: Their land is full of silver and gold, with no limit to their treasures; their land is full of horses, with no limit to their chariots.
units.rightText: And their land is full of silver and gold, neither is there any end of their treasures; their land also is full of horses, neither is there any end of their chariots.

units.leftText: Their land is full of idols; they bow down to the work of their hands, to what their fingers have made.
units.rightText: Their land also is full of idols; they worship the work of their own hands, that which their own fingers have made.

units.leftText: So mankind is brought low, and man is humbled — do not forgive them!
units.rightText: And the mean man is bowed down, and the great man is brought low: therefore forgive them not.

units.leftText: Go into the rocks and hide in the dust from the terror of the LORD and the splendor of His majesty.
units.rightText: Enter into the rock, and hide thee in the dust, from before the terror of Jehovah, and from the glory of his majesty.

units.leftText: The proud look of man will be humbled, and the loftiness of men brought low; the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.
units.rightText: The lofty looks of man shall be brought low, and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down, and Jehovah alone shall be exalted in that day.

units.leftText: For the Day of the LORD of Hosts will come against all the proud and lofty, against all that is exalted— it will be humbled—
units.rightText: For there shall be a day of Jehovah of hosts upon all that is proud and haughty, and upon all that is lifted up; and it shall be brought low;

units.leftText: against all the cedars of Lebanon, lofty and lifted up, against all the oaks of Bashan,
units.rightText: and upon all the cedars of Lebanon, that are high and lifted up, and upon all the oaks of Bashan,

units.leftText: against all the tall mountains, against all the high hills,
units.rightText: and upon all the high mountains, and upon all the hills that are lifted up,

units.leftText: against every high tower, against every fortified wall,
units.rightText: and upon every lofty tower, and upon every fortified wall,

units.leftText: against every ship of Tarshish, and against every stately vessel.
units.rightText: and upon all the ships of Tarshish, and upon all pleasant imagery.
leftNotes: 2:16 Or every ship of trade

units.leftText: So the pride of man will be brought low, and the loftiness of men will be humbled; the LORD alone will be exalted in that day,
units.rightText: And the loftiness of man shall be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men shall be brought low; and Jehovah alone shall be exalted in that day.

units.leftText: and the idols will vanish completely.
units.rightText: And the idols shall utterly pass away.

units.leftText: Men will flee to caves in the rocks and holes in the ground, away from the terror of the LORD and from the splendor of His majesty, when He rises to shake the earth.
units.rightText: And men shall go into the caves of the rocks, and into the holes of the earth, from before the terror of Jehovah, and from the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake mightily the earth.

units.leftText: In that day men will cast away to the moles and bats their idols of silver and gold — the idols they made to worship.
units.rightText: In that day men shall cast away their idols of silver, and their idols of gold, which have been made for them to worship, to the moles and to the bats;

units.leftText: They will flee to caverns in the rocks and crevices in the cliffs, away from the terror of the LORD and from the splendor of His majesty, when He rises to shake the earth.
units.rightText: to go into the caverns of the rocks, and into the clefts of the ragged rocks, from before the terror of Jehovah, and from the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake mightily the earth.

units.leftText: Put no more trust in man, who has only the breath in his nostrils. Of what account is he?
units.rightText: Cease ye from man, whose breath is in his nostrils; for wherein is he to be accounted of?

units.leftText: For behold, the Lord GOD of Hosts is about to remove from Jerusalem and Judah both supply and support: the whole supply of food and water,
units.rightText: For, behold, the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, doth take away from Jerusalem and from Judah stay and staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water;
leftNotes: 3:1 Hebrew staff

units.leftText: the mighty man and the warrior, the judge and the prophet, the soothsayer and the elder,
units.rightText: the mighty man, and the man of war; the judge, and the prophet, and the diviner, and the elder;

units.leftText: the commander of fifty and the dignitary, the counselor, the cunning magician, and the clever enchanter.
units.rightText: the captain of fifty, and the honorable man, and the counsellor, and the expert artificer, and the skilful enchanter.

units.leftText: “I will make mere lads their leaders, and children will rule over them.”
units.rightText: And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them.

units.leftText: The people will oppress one another, man against man, neighbor against neighbor; the young will rise up against the old, and the base against the honorable.
units.rightText: And the people shall be oppressed, every one by another, and every one by his neighbor: the child shall behave himself proudly against the old man, and the base against the honorable.

units.leftText: A man will seize his brother within his father’s house: “You have a cloak— you be our leader! Take charge of this heap of rubble.”
units.rightText: When a man shall take hold of his brother in the house of his father, saying, Thou hast clothing, be thou our ruler, and let this ruin be under thy hand;

units.leftText: On that day he will cry aloud: “I am not a healer. I have no food or clothing in my house. Do not make me leader of the people!”
units.rightText: in that day shall he lift up his voice, saying, I will not be a healer; for in my house is neither bread nor clothing: ye shall not make me ruler of the people.
leftNotes: 3:7 Or binder of wounds

units.leftText: For Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen because they spoke and acted against the LORD, defying His glorious presence.
units.rightText: For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen; because their tongue and their doings are against Jehovah, to provoke the eyes of his glory.
leftNotes: 3:8 Hebrew defying the eyes of His glory

units.leftText: The expression on their faces testifies against them, and like Sodom they flaunt their sin; they do not conceal it. Woe to them, for they have brought disaster upon themselves.
units.rightText: The show of their countenance doth witness against them; and they declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not. Woe unto their soul! for they have done evil unto themselves.

units.leftText: Tell the righteous it will be well with them, for they will enjoy the fruit of their labor.
units.rightText: Say ye of the righteous, that it shall be well with him; for they shall eat the fruit of their doings.

units.leftText: Woe to the wicked; disaster is upon them! For they will be repaid with what their hands have done.
units.rightText: Woe unto the wicked! it shall be ill with him; for what his hands have done shall be done unto him.

units.leftText: Youths oppress My people, and women rule over them. O My people, your guides mislead you; they turn you from your paths.
units.rightText: As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, they that lead thee cause thee to err, and destroy the way of thy paths.

units.leftText: The LORD arises to contend; He stands to judge the people.
units.rightText: Jehovah standeth up to contend, and standeth to judge the peoples.

units.leftText: The LORD brings this charge against the elders and leaders of His people: “You have devoured the vineyard; the plunder of the poor is in your houses.
units.rightText: Jehovah will enter into judgment with the elders of his people, and the princes thereof: It is ye that have eaten up the vineyard; the spoil of the poor is in your houses:

units.leftText: Why do you crush My people and grind the faces of the poor?” declares the Lord GOD of Hosts. A Warning to the Daughters of Zion
units.rightText: what mean ye that ye crush my people, and grind the face of the poor? saith the Lord, Jehovah of hosts.

units.leftText: The LORD also says: “Because the daughters of Zion are haughty — walking with heads held high and wanton eyes, prancing and skipping as they go, jingling the bracelets on their ankles —
units.rightText: Moreover Jehovah said, Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with outstretched necks and wanton eyes, walking and mincing as they go, and making a tinkling with their feet;

units.leftText: the Lord will bring sores on the heads of the daughters of Zion, and the LORD will make their foreheads bare. ”
units.rightText: therefore the Lord will smite with a scab the crown of the head of the daughters of Zion, and Jehovah will lay bare their secret parts.
leftNotes: 3:17 Or will uncover their secret parts

units.leftText: In that day the Lord will take away their finery: their anklets and headbands and crescents;
units.rightText: In that day the Lord will take away the beauty of their anklets, and the cauls, and the crescents;

units.leftText: their pendants, bracelets, and veils;
units.rightText: the pendants, and the bracelets, and the mufflers;

units.leftText: their headdresses, ankle chains, and sashes; their perfume bottles and charms;
units.rightText: the headtires, and the ankle chains, and the sashes, and the perfume-boxes, and the amulets;

units.leftText: their signet rings and nose rings;
units.rightText: the rings, and the nose-jewels;

units.leftText: their festive robes, capes, cloaks, and purses;
units.rightText: the festival robes, and the mantles, and the shawls, and the satchels;

units.leftText: and their mirrors, linen garments, tiaras, and shawls.
units.rightText: the hand-mirrors, and the fine linen, and the turbans, and the veils.

units.leftText: Instead of fragrance there will be a stench; instead of a belt, a rope; instead of styled hair, baldness; instead of fine clothing, sackcloth; instead of beauty, shame.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, that instead of sweet spices there shall be rottenness; and instead of a girdle, a rope; and instead of well set hair, baldness; and instead of a robe, a girding of sackcloth; branding instead of beauty.
leftNotes: 3:24 DSS; MT branding

units.leftText: Your men will fall by the sword, and your warriors in battle.
units.rightText: Thy men shall fall by the sword, and thy mighty in the war.

units.leftText: And the gates of Zion will lament and mourn; destitute, she will sit on the ground.
units.rightText: And her gates shall lament and mourn; and she shall be desolate and sit upon the ground.

units.leftText: In that day seven women will take hold of one man and say, “We will eat our own bread and provide our own clothes. Just let us be called by your name. Take away our disgrace!”
units.rightText: And seven women shall take hold of one man in that day, saying, We will eat our own bread, and wear our own apparel: only let us be called by thy name; take thou away our reproach.

units.leftText: On that day the Branch of the LORD will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the pride and glory of Israel’s survivors.
units.rightText: In that day shall the branch of Jehovah be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land shall be excellent and comely for them that are escaped of Israel.

units.leftText: Whoever remains in Zion and whoever is left in Jerusalem will be called holy— all in Jerusalem who are recorded among the living—
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, that he that is left in Zion, and he that remaineth in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, even every one that is written among the living in Jerusalem;

units.leftText: when the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and cleansed the bloodstains from the heart of Jerusalem by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of fire.
units.rightText: when the Lord shall have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and shall have purged the blood of Jerusalem from the midst thereof, by the spirit of justice, and by the spirit of burning.

units.leftText: Then the LORD will create over all of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud of smoke by day and a glowing flame of fire by night. For over all the glory there will be a canopy,
units.rightText: And Jehovah will create over the whole habitation of mount Zion, and over her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night; for over all the glory shall be spread a covering.

units.leftText: a shelter to give shade from the heat by day, and a refuge and hiding place from the storm and the rain.
units.rightText: And there shall be a pavilion for a shade in the day-time from the heat, and for a refuge and for a covert from storm and from rain.

units.leftText: I will sing for my beloved a song of his vineyard: My beloved had a vineyard on a very fertile hill.
units.rightText: Let me sing for my wellbeloved a song of my beloved touching his vineyard. My wellbeloved had a vineyard in a very fruitful hill:

units.leftText: He dug it up and cleared the stones and planted the finest vines. He built a watchtower in the middle and dug out a winepress as well. He waited for the vineyard to yield good grapes, but the fruit it produced was sour!
units.rightText: and he digged it, and gathered out the stones thereof, and planted it with the choicest vine, and built a tower in the midst of it, and also hewed out a winepress therein: and he looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes.

units.leftText: “And now, O dwellers of Jerusalem and men of Judah, I exhort you to judge between Me and My vineyard.
units.rightText: And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah, judge, I pray you, betwixt me and my vineyard.

units.leftText: What more could have been done for My vineyard than I have done for it? Why, when I expected sweet grapes, did it bring forth sour fruit?
units.rightText: What could have been done more to my vineyard, that I have not done in it? wherefore, when I looked that it should bring forth grapes, brought it forth wild grapes?

units.leftText: Now I will tell you what I am about to do to My vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it will be consumed; I will tear down its wall, and it will be trampled.
units.rightText: And now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up; I will break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down:

units.leftText: I will make it a wasteland, neither pruned nor cultivated, and thorns and briers will grow up. I will command the clouds that rain shall not fall on it.”
units.rightText: and I will lay it waste; it shall not be pruned nor hoed; but there shall come up briers and thorns: I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it.

units.leftText: For the vineyard of the LORD of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are the plant of His delight. He looked for justice, but saw bloodshed; for righteousness, but heard a cry of distress. Woes to the Wicked
units.rightText: For the vineyard of Jehovah of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant: and he looked for justice, but, behold, oppression; for righteousness, but, behold, a cry.

units.leftText: Woe to you who add house to house and join field to field until no place is left and you live alone in the land.
units.rightText: Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no room, and ye be made to dwell alone in the midst of the land!

units.leftText: I heard the LORD of Hosts declare: “Surely many houses will become desolate, great mansions left unoccupied.
units.rightText: In mine ears saith Jehovah of hosts, Of a truth many houses shall be desolate, even great and fair, without inhabitant.

units.leftText: For ten acres of vineyard will yield but a bath of wine, and a homer of seed only an ephah of grain. ”
units.rightText: For ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath, and a homer of seed shall yield but an ephah.
leftNotes: 5:10 Literally ten yoke of vineyard will yield a bath; that is, the area ten yoke of oxen can plow in a day will yield approximately 5.8 gallons or 22 liters of wine.
5:10 Literally and a homer of seed will yield an ephah; that is, a homer of seed (approximately 6.24 bushels or 220 liters) will yield a tenth of its weight in grain.

units.leftText: Woe to those who rise early in the morning in pursuit of strong drink, who linger into the evening, to be inflamed by wine.
units.rightText: Woe unto them that rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink; that tarry late into the night, till wine inflame them!

units.leftText: At their feasts are the lyre and harp, tambourines and flutes and wine. They disregard the actions of the LORD and fail to see the work of His hands.
units.rightText: And the harp and the lute, the tabret and the pipe, and wine, are in their feasts; but they regard not the work of Jehovah, neither have they considered the operation of his hands.

units.leftText: Therefore My people will go into exile for their lack of understanding; their dignitaries are starving and their masses are parched with thirst.
units.rightText: Therefore my people are gone into captivity for lack of knowledge; and their honorable men are famished, and their multitude are parched with thirst.

units.leftText: Therefore Sheol enlarges its throat and opens wide its enormous jaws, and down go Zion’s nobles and masses, her revelers and carousers!
units.rightText: Therefore Sheol hath enlarged its desire, and opened its mouth without measure; and their glory, and their multitude, and their pomp, and he that rejoiceth among them, descend into it.

units.leftText: So mankind will be brought low, and each man humbled; the arrogant will lower their eyes.
units.rightText: And the mean man is bowed down, and the great man is humbled, and the eyes of the lofty are humbled:

units.leftText: But the LORD of Hosts will be exalted by His justice, and the holy God will show Himself holy in righteousness.
units.rightText: but Jehovah of hosts is exalted in justice, and God the Holy One is sanctified in righteousness.

units.leftText: Lambs will graze as in their own pastures, and strangers will feed in the ruins of the wealthy.
units.rightText: Then shall the lambs feed as in their pasture, and the waste places of the fat ones shall wanderers eat.
leftNotes: 5:17 LXX lambs

units.leftText: Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of deceit and pull sin along with cart ropes,
units.rightText: Woe unto them that draw iniquity with cords of falsehood, and sin as it were with a cart rope;

units.leftText: to those who say, “Let Him hurry and hasten His work so that we may see it! Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come so that we may know it!”
units.rightText: that say, Let him make speed, let him hasten his work, that we may see it; and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw nigh and come, that we may know it!

units.leftText: Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who turn darkness to light and light to darkness, who replace bitter with sweet and sweet with bitter.
units.rightText: Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!

units.leftText: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight.
units.rightText: Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!

units.leftText: Woe to those who are heroes in drinking wine and champions in mixing strong drink,
units.rightText: Woe unto them that are mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink;

units.leftText: who acquit the guilty for a bribe and deprive the innocent of justice.
units.rightText: that justify the wicked for a bribe, and take away the righteousness of the righteous from him!

units.leftText: Therefore, as a tongue of fire consumes the straw, and as dry grass shrivels in the flame, so their roots will decay and their blossoms will blow away like dust; for they have rejected the instruction of the LORD of Hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.
units.rightText: Therefore as the tongue of fire devoureth the stubble, and as the dry grass sinketh down in the flame, so their root shall be as rottenness, and their blossom shall go up as dust; because they have rejected the law of Jehovah of hosts, and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: Therefore the anger of the LORD burns against His people; His hand is raised against them to strike them down. The mountains quake, and the corpses lie like refuse in the streets. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.
units.rightText: Therefore is the anger of Jehovah kindled against his people, and he hath stretched forth his hand against them, and hath smitten them; and the mountains tremble, and their dead bodies are as refuse in the midst of the streets. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

units.leftText: He lifts a banner for the distant nations and whistles for those at the ends of the earth. Behold— how speedily and swiftly they come!
units.rightText: And he will lift up an ensign to the nations from far, and will hiss for them from the end of the earth; and, behold, they shall come with speed swiftly.

units.leftText: None of them grows weary or stumbles; no one slumbers or sleeps. No belt is loose and no sandal strap is broken.
units.rightText: None shall be weary nor stumble among them; none shall slumber nor sleep; neither shall the girdle of their loins be loosed, nor the latchet of their shoes be broken:

units.leftText: Their arrows are sharpened, and all their bows are strung. The hooves of their horses are like flint; their chariot wheels are like a whirlwind.
units.rightText: whose arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent; their horses’ hoofs shall be accounted as flint, and their wheels as a whirlwind:

units.leftText: Their roaring is like that of a lion; they roar like young lions. They growl and seize their prey; they carry it away, and no one can rescue it.
units.rightText: their roaring shall be like a lioness, they shall roar like young lions; yea, they shall roar, and lay hold of the prey, and carry it away safe, and there shall be none to deliver.

units.leftText: In that day they will roar over it, like the roaring of the sea. If one looks over the land, he will see darkness and distress; even the light will be obscured by clouds.
units.rightText: And they shall roar against them in that day like the roaring of the sea: and if one look unto the land, behold, darkness and distress; and the light is darkened in the clouds thereof.

units.leftText: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted; and the train of His robe filled the temple.
units.rightText: In the year that king Uzziah died I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple.
leftNotes: 6:1 Or the hem of His robe

units.leftText: Above Him stood seraphim, each having six wings: With two wings they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they were flying.
units.rightText: Above him stood the seraphim: each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly.

units.leftText: And they were calling out to one another: “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory.”
units.rightText: And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is Jehovah of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.

units.leftText: At the sound of their voices the doorposts and thresholds shook, and the temple was filled with smoke.
units.rightText: And the foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke.

units.leftText: Then I said: “Woe is me, for I am ruined, because I am a man of unclean lips dwelling among a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Hosts.”
units.rightText: Then said I, Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, Jehovah of hosts.

units.leftText: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, and in his hand was a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.
units.rightText: Then flew one of the seraphim unto me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar:

units.leftText: And with it he touched my mouth and said: “Now that this has touched your lips, your iniquity is removed and your sin is atoned for.”
units.rightText: and he touched my mouth with it, and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin forgiven.

units.leftText: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying: “Whom shall I send? Who will go for Us?” And I said: “Here am I. Send me!”
units.rightText: And I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then I said, Here am I; send me.

units.leftText: And He replied: “Go and tell this people, ‘Be ever hearing, but never understanding; be ever seeing, but never perceiving.’
units.rightText: And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.
leftNotes: 6:9 Hebrew; LXX ‘You shall be ever hearing, but never understanding; you shall be ever seeing, but never perceiving.’Cited in Matthew 13:14|MAT 13:14*, Mark 4:12, Luke 8:10, and Acts 28:26

units.leftText: Make the hearts of this people calloused; deafen their ears and close their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed. ”
units.rightText: Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn again, and be healed.
leftNotes: 6:10 Hebrew; LXX For this people’s heart has grown callous; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.Cited in Matthew 13:15|MAT 13:15*, Mark 4:12, John 12:40, and Acts 28:27

units.leftText: Then I asked: “How long, O Lord?” And He replied: “Until the cities lie ruined and without inhabitant, until the houses are left unoccupied and the land is desolate and ravaged,
units.rightText: Then said I, Lord, how long? And he answered, Until cities be waste without inhabitant, and houses without man, and the land become utterly waste,

units.leftText: until the LORD has driven men far away and the land is utterly forsaken.
units.rightText: and Jehovah have removed men far away, and the forsaken places be many in the midst of the land.

units.leftText: And though a tenth remains in the land, it will be burned again. As the terebinth and oak leave stumps when felled, so the holy seed will be a stump in the land.”
units.rightText: And if there be yet a tenth in it, it also shall in turn be eaten up: as a terebinth, and as an oak, whose stock remaineth, when they are felled; so the holy seed is the stock thereof.

units.leftText: Now in the days that Ahaz son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, was king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram marched up to wage war against Jerusalem. He was accompanied by Pekah son of Remaliah the king of Israel, but he could not overpower the city.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.
leftNotes: 7:1 That is, Syria

units.leftText: When it was reported to the house of David that Aram was in league with Ephraim, the hearts of Ahaz and his people trembled like trees in the forest shaken by the wind.
units.rightText: And it was told the house of David, saying, Syria is confederate with Ephraim. And his heart trembled, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the forest tremble with the wind.
leftNotes: 7:2 Or had set up camp in Ephraim, that is, the northern kingdom of Israel

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Isaiah, “Go out with your son Shear-jashub to meet Ahaz at the end of the aqueduct that feeds the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field,
units.rightText: Then said Jehovah unto Isaiah, Go forth now to meet Ahaz, thou, and Shear-jashub thy son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, in the highway of the fuller’s field;
leftNotes: 7:3 Shear-jashub means a remnant shall return.

units.leftText: and say to him: Calm down and be quiet. Do not be afraid or disheartened over these two smoldering stubs of firewood— over the fierce anger of Rezin and Aram and of the son of Remaliah.
units.rightText: and say unto him, Take heed, and be quiet; fear not, neither let thy heart be faint, because of these two tails of smoking firebrands, for the fierce anger of Rezin and Syria, and of the son of Remaliah.

units.leftText: For Aram, along with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, has plotted your ruin, saying:
units.rightText: Because Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah, have purposed evil against thee, saying,

units.leftText: ‘Let us invade Judah, terrorize it, and divide it among ourselves. Then we can install the son of Tabeal over it as king.’
units.rightText: Let us go up against Judah, and vex it, and let us make a breach therein for us, and set up a king in the midst of it, even the son of Tabeel;
leftNotes: 7:6 Hebrew split it open

units.leftText: But this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘It will not arise; it will not happen.
units.rightText: thus saith the Lord Jehovah, It shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass.

units.leftText: For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered as a people.
units.rightText: For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken in pieces, so that it shall not be a people:

units.leftText: The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not stand firm in your faith, then you will not stand at all.’” The Sign of Immanuel (Matthew 1:18–25|MAT 1:18-25*)
units.rightText: and the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If ye will not believe, surely ye shall not be established.

units.leftText: Again the LORD spoke to Ahaz, saying,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake again unto Ahaz, saying,

units.leftText: “Ask for a sign from the LORD your God, whether from the depths of Sheol or the heights of heaven.”
units.rightText: Ask thee a sign of Jehovah thy God; ask it either in the depth, or in the height above.

units.leftText: But Ahaz replied, “I will not ask; I will not test the LORD.”
units.rightText: But Ahaz said, I will not ask, neither will I tempt Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then Isaiah said, “Hear now, O house of David! Is it not enough to try the patience of men? Will you try the patience of my God as well?
units.rightText: And he said, Hear ye now, O house of David: Is it a small thing for you to weary men, that ye will weary my God also?

units.leftText: Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign: Behold, the virgin will be with child and give birth to a son, and will call Him Immanuel.
units.rightText: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
leftNotes: 7:14 Or young woman

7:14 Immanuel means God with us; literally and she will call His name Immanuel; DSS and His name will be called Immanuel or and He will call His name Immanuel; LXX and you will call His name Immanuel; cited in Matthew 1:23|MAT 1:23*.

units.leftText: By the time He knows enough to reject evil and choose good, He will be eating curds and honey.
units.rightText: Butter and honey shall he eat, when he knoweth to refuse the evil, and choose the good.

units.leftText: For before the boy knows enough to reject evil and choose good, the land of the two kings you dread will be laid waste. Judgment to Come (Micah 1:1–7|MIC 1:1-7*)
units.rightText: For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land whose two kings thou abhorrest shall be forsaken.

units.leftText: The LORD will bring on you and on your people and on the house of your father a time unlike any since the day Ephraim separated from Judah— He will bring the king of Assyria.”
units.rightText: Jehovah will bring upon thee, and upon thy people, and upon thy father’s house, days that have not come, from the day that Ephraim departed from Judah— even the king of Assyria.

units.leftText: On that day the LORD will whistle to the flies at the farthest streams of the Nile and to the bees in the land of Assyria.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that Jehovah will hiss for the fly that is in the uttermost part of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.

units.leftText: And they will all come and settle in the steep ravines and clefts of the rocks, in all the thornbushes and watering holes.
units.rightText: And they shall come, and shall rest all of them in the desolate valleys, and in the clefts of the rocks, and upon all thorn-hedges, and upon all pastures.

units.leftText: On that day the Lord will use a razor hired from beyond the Euphrates — the king of Assyria— to shave your head and the hair of your legs, and to remove your beard as well.
units.rightText: In that day will the Lord shave with a razor that is hired in the parts beyond the River, even with the king of Assyria, the head and the hair of the feet; and it shall also consume the beard.
leftNotes: 7:20 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: On that day a man will raise a young cow and two sheep,
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that a man shall keep alive a young cow, and two sheep;

units.leftText: and from the abundance of milk they give, he will eat curds; for all who remain in the land will eat curds and honey.
units.rightText: and it shall come to pass, that because of the abundance of milk which they shall give he shall eat butter: for butter and honey shall every one eat that is left in the midst of the land.

units.leftText: And on that day, in every place that had a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels of silver, only briers and thorns will be found.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that every place, where there were a thousand vines at a thousand silverlings, shall be for briers and thorns.
leftNotes: 7:23 Hebrew a thousand of silver; that is, approximately 25.1 pounds or 11.4 kilograms of silver

units.leftText: Men will go there with bow and arrow, for the land will be covered with briers and thorns.
units.rightText: With arrows and with bow shall one come thither, because all the land shall be briers and thorns.

units.leftText: For fear of the briers and thorns, you will no longer traverse the hills once tilled by the hoe; they will become places for oxen to graze and sheep to trample.
units.rightText: And all the hills that were digged with the mattock, thou shalt not come thither for fear of briers and thorns; but it shall be for the sending forth of oxen, and for the treading of sheep.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to me, “Take a large scroll and write on it with an ordinary stylus: Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto me, Take thee a great tablet, and write upon it with the pen of a man, For Maher-shalal-hash-baz;
leftNotes: 8:1 Hebrew with a man’s
8:1 Maher-shalal-hash-baz means The spoil speeds, the prey hastens or Swift to plunder, quick to carry away; also in verse 3.

units.leftText: And I will appoint for Myself trustworthy witnesses— Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberekiah.”
units.rightText: and I will take unto me faithful witnesses to record, Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah.

units.leftText: And I had relations with the prophetess, and she conceived and gave birth to a son. The LORD said to me, “Name him Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
units.rightText: And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son. Then said Jehovah unto me, Call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz.

units.leftText: For before the boy knows how to cry ‘Father’ or ‘Mother,’ the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried off by the king of Assyria.”
units.rightText: For before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and, My mother, the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be carried away before the king of Assyria.

units.leftText: And the LORD spoke to me further:
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto me yet again, saying,

units.leftText: “Because this people has rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah and rejoiced in Rezin and the son of Remaliah,
units.rightText: Forasmuch as this people have refused the waters of Shiloah that go softly, and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah’s son;

units.leftText: the Lord will surely bring against them the mighty floodwaters of the Euphrates — the king of Assyria and all his pomp. It will overflow its channels and overrun its banks.
units.rightText: now therefore, behold, the Lord bringeth up upon them the waters of the River, strong and many, even the king of Assyria and all his glory: and it shall come up over all its channels, and go over all its banks;
leftNotes: 8:7 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: It will pour into Judah, swirling and sweeping over it, reaching up to the neck; its spreading streams will cover your entire land, O Immanuel!
units.rightText: and it shall sweep onward into Judah; it shall overflow and pass through; it shall reach even to the neck; and the stretching out of its wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel.
leftNotes: 8:8 Immanuel means God with us.

units.leftText: Huddle together, O peoples, and be shattered; pay attention, all you distant lands; prepare for battle, and be shattered; prepare for battle, and be shattered!
units.rightText: Make an uproar, O ye peoples, and be broken in pieces; and give ear, all ye of far countries: gird yourselves, and be broken in pieces; gird yourselves, and be broken in pieces.
leftNotes: 8:9 Or Raise the war cry or Be evil or Be broken

units.leftText: Devise a plan, but it will be thwarted; state a proposal, but it will not happen. For God is with us. ” A Call to Fear God (Ecclesiastes 8:10–13|ECC 8:10-13*)
units.rightText: Take counsel together, and it shall be brought to nought; speak the word, and it shall not stand: for God is with us.
leftNotes: 8:10 Hebrew Immanuel; see Matthew 1:23|MAT 1:23*.

units.leftText: For this is what the LORD has spoken to me with a strong hand, instructing me not to walk in the way of this people:
units.rightText: For Jehovah spake thus to me with a strong hand, and instructed me not to walk in the way of this people, saying,

units.leftText: “Do not call conspiracy everything these people regard as conspiracy. Do not fear what they fear; do not live in dread.
units.rightText: Say ye not, A conspiracy, concerning all whereof this people shall say, A conspiracy; neither fear ye their fear, nor be in dread thereof.
leftNotes: 8:12 Or Do not fear their threats
8:12 LXX do not be shaken; cited in 1 Peter 3:14|1PE 3:14*

units.leftText: The LORD of Hosts is the One you shall regard as holy. Only He should be feared; only He should be dreaded.
units.rightText: Jehovah of hosts, him shall ye sanctify; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.

units.leftText: And He will be a sanctuary — but to both houses of Israel a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, to the dwellers of Jerusalem a trap and a snare.
units.rightText: And he shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
leftNotes: 8:14 Cited in Romans 9:33|ROM 9:33* and 1 Peter 2:8

units.leftText: Many will stumble over these; they will fall and be broken; they will be ensnared and captured.”
units.rightText: And many shall stumble thereon, and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken.

units.leftText: Bind up the testimony and seal the law among my disciples.
units.rightText: Bind thou up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.

units.leftText: I will wait for the LORD, who is hiding His face from the house of Jacob. I will put my trust in Him.
units.rightText: And I will wait for Jehovah, that hideth his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him.
leftNotes: 8:17 Or I will eagerly look for Him; cited in Hebrews 2:13|HEB 2:13*

units.leftText: Here am I, and the children the LORD has given me as signs and symbols in Israel from the LORD of Hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion. Darkness and Light
units.rightText: Behold, I and the children whom Jehovah hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from Jehovah of hosts, who dwelleth in mount Zion.
leftNotes: 8:18 Cited in Hebrews 2:13|HEB 2:13*

units.leftText: When men tell you to consult mediums and spiritists who whisper and mutter, shouldn’t a people consult their God instead? Why consult the dead on behalf of the living?
units.rightText: And when they shall say unto you, Seek unto them that have familiar spirits and unto the wizards, that chirp and that mutter: should not a people seek unto their God? on behalf of the living should they seek unto the dead?

units.leftText: To the law and to the testimony! If they do not speak according to this word, they have no light of dawn.
units.rightText: To the law and to the testimony! if they speak not according to this word, surely there is no morning for them.

units.leftText: They will roam the land, dejected and hungry. When they are famished, they will become enraged; and looking upward, they will curse their king and their God.
units.rightText: And they shall pass through it, sore distressed and hungry; and it shall come to pass that, when they shall be hungry, they shall fret themselves, and curse by their king and by their God, and turn their faces upward:

units.leftText: Then they will look to the earth and see only distress and darkness and the gloom of anguish. And they will be driven into utter darkness.
units.rightText: and they shall look unto the earth, and, behold, distress and darkness, the gloom of anguish; and into thick darkness they shall be driven away.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, there will be no more gloom for those in distress. In the past He humbled the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but in the future He will honor the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations:
units.rightText: But there shall be no gloom to her that was in anguish. In the former time he brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter time hath he made it glorious, by the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.

units.leftText: The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death, a light has dawned.
units.rightText: The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwelt in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.
leftNotes: 9:2 Cited in Matthew 4:15–16|MAT 4:15-16*

units.leftText: You have enlarged the nation and increased its joy. The people rejoice before You as they rejoice at harvest time, as men rejoice in dividing the plunder.
units.rightText: Thou hast multiplied the nation, thou hast increased their joy: they joy before thee according to the joy in harvest, as men rejoice when they divide the spoil.

units.leftText: For as in the day of Midian You have shattered the yoke of their burden, the bar across their shoulders, and the rod of their oppressor.
units.rightText: For the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, thou hast broken as in the day of Midian.

units.leftText: For every trampling boot of battle and every garment rolled in blood will be burned as fuel for the fire.
units.rightText: For all the armor of the armed man in the tumult, and the garments rolled in blood, shall be for burning, for fuel of fire.

units.leftText: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given, and the government will be upon His shoulders. And He will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
units.rightText: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given; and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

units.leftText: Of the increase of His government and peace there will be no end. He will reign on the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish and sustain it with justice and righteousness from that time and forevermore. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this. Judgment against Israel’s Pride
units.rightText: Of the increase of his government and of peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to establish it, and to uphold it with justice and with righteousness from henceforth even for ever. The zeal of Jehovah of hosts will perform this.

units.leftText: The Lord has sent a message against Jacob, and it has fallen upon Israel.
units.rightText: The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel.

units.leftText: All the people will know it — Ephraim and the dwellers of Samaria. With pride and arrogance of heart they will say:
units.rightText: And all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria, that say in pride and in stoutness of heart,
leftNotes: 9:9 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel

units.leftText: “The bricks have fallen, but we will rebuild with finished stone; the sycamores have been felled, but we will replace them with cedars.”
units.rightText: The bricks are fallen, but we will build with hewn stone; the sycomores are cut down, but we will put cedars in their place.

units.leftText: The LORD has raised up the foes of Rezin against him and joined his enemies together.
units.rightText: Therefore Jehovah will set up on high against him the adversaries of Rezin, and will stir up his enemies,

units.leftText: Aram from the east and Philistia from the west have devoured Israel with open mouths. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised. Judgment against Israel’s Hypocrisy
units.rightText: the Syrians before, and the Philistines behind; and they shall devour Israel with open mouth. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
leftNotes: 9:12 That is, Syria

units.leftText: But the people did not return to Him who struck them; they did not seek the LORD of Hosts.
units.rightText: Yet the people have not turned unto him that smote them, neither have they sought Jehovah of hosts.

units.leftText: So the LORD will cut off Israel’s head and tail, both palm branch and reed in a single day.
units.rightText: Therefore Jehovah will cut off from Israel head and tail, palm-branch and rush, in one day.

units.leftText: The head is the elder and honorable man, and the tail is the prophet who teaches lies.
units.rightText: The elder and the honorable man, he is the head; and the prophet that teacheth lies, he is the tail.

units.leftText: For those who guide this people mislead them, and those they mislead are swallowed up.
units.rightText: For they that lead this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed.

units.leftText: Therefore the Lord takes no pleasure in their young men; He has no compassion on their fatherless and widows. For every one of them is godless and wicked, and every mouth speaks folly. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised. Judgment against Israel’s Unrepentance
units.rightText: Therefore the Lord will not rejoice over their young men, neither will he have compassion on their fatherless and widows; for every one is profane and an evil-doer, and every mouth speaketh folly. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

units.leftText: For wickedness burns like a fire that consumes the thorns and briers and kindles the forest thickets, which roll upward in billows of smoke.
units.rightText: For wickedness burneth as the fire; it devoureth the briers and thorns; yea, it kindleth in the thickets of the forest, and they roll upward in a column of smoke.

units.leftText: By the wrath of the LORD of Hosts the land is scorched, and the people are fuel for the fire. No man even spares his brother.
units.rightText: Through the wrath of Jehovah of hosts is the land burnt up; and the people are as the fuel of fire: no man spareth his brother.

units.leftText: They carve out what is on the right, but they are still hungry; they eat what is on the left, but they are still not satisfied. Each one devours the flesh of his own offspring.
units.rightText: And one shall snatch on the right hand, and be hungry; and he shall eat on the left hand, and they shall not be satisfied: they shall eat every man the flesh of his own arm:
leftNotes: 9:20 Literally of his own arm

units.leftText: Manasseh devours Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh; together they turn against Judah. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.
units.rightText: Manasseh, Ephraim; and Ephraim, Manasseh; and they together shall be against Judah. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

units.leftText: Woe to those who enact unjust statutes and issue oppressive decrees,
units.rightText: Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees, and to the writers that write perverseness;

units.leftText: to deprive the poor of fair treatment and withhold justice from the oppressed of My people, to make widows their prey and orphans their plunder.
units.rightText: to turn aside the needy from justice, and to rob the poor of my people of their right, that widows may be their spoil, and that they may make the fatherless their prey!

units.leftText: What will you do on the day of reckoning when devastation comes from afar? To whom will you flee for help? Where will you leave your wealth?
units.rightText: And what will ye do in the day of visitation, and in the desolation which shall come from far? to whom will ye flee for help? and where will ye leave your glory?

units.leftText: Nothing will remain but to crouch among the captives or fall among the slain. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised. Judgment on Assyria
units.rightText: They shall only bow down under the prisoners, and shall fall under the slain. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

units.leftText: Woe to Assyria, the rod of My anger; the staff in their hands is My wrath.
units.rightText: Ho Assyrian, the rod of mine anger, the staff in whose hand is mine indignation!

units.leftText: I will send him against a godless nation; I will dispatch him against a people destined for My rage, to take spoils and seize plunder, and to trample them down like clay in the streets.
units.rightText: I will send him against a profane nation, and against the people of my wrath will I give him a charge, to take the spoil, and to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets.

units.leftText: But this is not his intention; this is not his plan. For it is in his heart to destroy and cut off many nations.
units.rightText: Howbeit he meaneth not so, neither doth his heart think so; but it is in his heart to destroy, and to cut off nations not a few.

units.leftText: “Are not all my commanders kings?” he says.
units.rightText: For he saith, Are not my princes all of them kings?

units.leftText: “Is not Calno like Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? Is not Samaria like Damascus?
units.rightText: Is not Calno as Carchemish? is not Hamath as Arpad? is not Samaria as Damascus?

units.leftText: As my hand seized the idolatrous kingdoms whose images surpassed those of Jerusalem and Samaria,
units.rightText: As my hand hath found the kingdoms of the idols, whose graven images did excel them of Jerusalem and of Samaria;

units.leftText: and as I have done to Samaria and its idols, will I not also do to Jerusalem and her idols?”
units.rightText: shall I not, as I have done unto Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and her idols?

units.leftText: So when the Lord has completed all His work against Mount Zion and Jerusalem, He will say, “I will punish the king of Assyria for the fruit of his arrogant heart and the proud look in his eyes.
units.rightText: Wherefore it shall come to pass, that, when the Lord hath performed his whole work upon mount Zion and on Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria, and the glory of his high looks.

units.leftText: For he says: ‘By the strength of my hand I have done this, and by my wisdom, for I am clever. I have removed the boundaries of nations and plundered their treasures; like a mighty one I subdued their rulers.
units.rightText: For he hath said, By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom; for I have understanding: and I have removed the bounds of the peoples, and have robbed their treasures, and like a valiant man I have brought down them that sit on thrones:

units.leftText: My hand reached as into a nest to seize the wealth of the nations. Like one gathering abandoned eggs, I gathered all the earth. No wing fluttered, no beak opened or chirped.’”
units.rightText: and my hand hath found as a nest the riches of the peoples; and as one gathereth eggs that are forsaken, have I gathered all the earth: and there was none that moved the wing, or that opened the mouth, or chirped.

units.leftText: Does an axe raise itself above the one who swings it? Does a saw boast over him who saws with it? It would be like a rod waving the one who lifts it, or a staff lifting him who is not wood!
units.rightText: Shall the axe boast itself against him that heweth therewith? shall the saw magnify itself against him that wieldeth it? as if a rod should wield them that lift it up, or as if a staff should lift up him that is not wood.

units.leftText: Therefore the Lord GOD of Hosts will send a wasting disease among Assyria’s stout warriors, and under his pomp will be kindled a fire like a burning flame.
units.rightText: Therefore will the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, send among his fat ones leanness; and under his glory there shall be kindled a burning like the burning of fire.

units.leftText: And the Light of Israel will become a fire, and its Holy One a flame. In a single day it will burn and devour Assyria’s thorns and thistles.
units.rightText: And the light of Israel will be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame; and it will burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day.

units.leftText: The splendor of its forests and orchards, both soul and body, it will completely destroy, as a sickness consumes a man.
units.rightText: And he will consume the glory of his forest, and of his fruitful field, both soul and body: and it shall be as when a standard-bearer fainteth.

units.leftText: The remaining trees of its forests will be so few that a child could count them. A Remnant Shall Return
units.rightText: And the remnant of the trees of his forest shall be few, so that a child may write them.

units.leftText: On that day the remnant of Israel and the survivors of the house of Jacob will no longer depend on him who struck them, but they will truly rely on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the remnant of Israel, and they that are escaped of the house of Jacob, shall no more again lean upon him that smote them, but shall lean upon Jehovah, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.

units.leftText: A remnant will return — a remnant of Jacob — to the Mighty God.
units.rightText: A remnant shall return, even the remnant of Jacob, unto the mighty God.
leftNotes: 10:21 Hebrew Shear-jashub; also in verse 22; see Isaiah 7:3|ISA 7:3*.

units.leftText: Though your people, O Israel, be like the sand of the sea, only a remnant will return. Destruction has been decreed, overflowing with righteousness.
units.rightText: For though thy people, Israel, be as the sand of the sea, only a remnant of them shall return: a destruction is determined, overflowing with righteousness.
leftNotes: 10:22 LXX Though the people of Israel be like the sand of the sea, only a remnant will be saved.Cited in Romans 9:27|ROM 9:27*

units.leftText: For the Lord GOD of Hosts will carry out the destruction decreed upon the whole land.
units.rightText: For a full end, and that determined, will the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, make in the midst of all the earth.
leftNotes: 10:23 LXX He will finish the work and cut it short in righteousness, because the Lord will make a short work in all the world.Cited in Romans 9:28|ROM 9:28*

units.leftText: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD of Hosts says: “O My people who dwell in Zion, do not fear Assyria, who strikes you with a rod and lifts his staff against you as the Egyptians did.
units.rightText: Therefore thus saith the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, O my people that dwellest in Zion, be not afraid of the Assyrian, though he smite thee with the rod, and lift up his staff against thee, after the manner of Egypt.

units.leftText: For in just a little while My fury against you will subside, and My anger will turn to their destruction.”
units.rightText: For yet a very little while, and the indignation against thee shall be accomplished, and mine anger shall be directed to his destruction.

units.leftText: And the LORD of Hosts will brandish a whip against them, as when He struck Midian at the rock of Oreb. He will raise His staff over the sea, as He did in Egypt.
units.rightText: And Jehovah of hosts will stir up against him a scourge, as in the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb: and his rod will be over the sea, and he will lift it up after the manner of Egypt.

units.leftText: On that day the burden will be lifted from your shoulders, and the yoke from your neck. The yoke will be broken because your neck will be too large.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that his burden shall depart from off thy shoulder, and his yoke from off thy neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed by reason of fatness.
leftNotes: 10:27 Literally broken because of fatness; LXX broken from your shoulders

units.leftText: Assyria has entered Aiath and passed through Migron, storing their supplies at Michmash.
units.rightText: He is come to Aiath, he is passed through Migron; at Michmash he layeth up his baggage;

units.leftText: They have crossed at the ford: “We will spend the night at Geba.” Ramah trembles; Gibeah of Saul flees.
units.rightText: they are gone over the pass; they have taken up their lodging at Geba; Ramah trembleth; Gibeah of Saul is fled.

units.leftText: Cry aloud, O Daughter of Gallim! Listen, O Laishah! O wretched Anathoth!
units.rightText: Cry aloud with thy voice, O daughter of Gallim! hearken, O Laishah! O thou poor Anathoth!

units.leftText: Madmenah flees; the people of Gebim take refuge.
units.rightText: Madmenah is a fugitive; the inhabitants of Gebim flee for safety.

units.leftText: Yet today they will halt at Nob, shaking a fist at the mount of Daughter Zion, at the hill of Jerusalem.
units.rightText: This very day shall he halt at Nob: he shaketh his hand at the mount of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Behold, the Lord GOD of Hosts will lop off the branches with terrifying power. The tall trees will be cut down, the lofty ones will be felled.
units.rightText: Behold, the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, will lop the boughs with terror: and the high of stature shall be hewn down, and the lofty shall be brought low.

units.leftText: He will clear the forest thickets with an axe, and Lebanon will fall before the Mighty One.
units.rightText: And he will cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon shall fall by a mighty one.

units.leftText: Then a shoot will spring up from the stump of Jesse, and a Branch from his roots will bear fruit.
units.rightText: And there shall come forth a shoot out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots shall bear fruit.

units.leftText: The Spirit of the LORD will rest on Him— the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and strength, the Spirit of knowledge and fear of the LORD.
units.rightText: And the Spirit of Jehovah shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Jehovah.

units.leftText: And He will delight in the fear of the LORD. He will not judge by what His eyes see, and He will not decide by what His ears hear,
units.rightText: And his delight shall be in the fear of Jehovah; and he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither decide after the hearing of his ears;

units.leftText: but with righteousness He will judge the poor, and with equity He will decide for the lowly of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of His mouth and slay the wicked with the breath of His lips.
units.rightText: but with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and decide with equity for the meek of the earth; and he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth; and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked.

units.leftText: Righteousness will be the belt around His hips, and faithfulness the sash around His waist.
units.rightText: And righteousness shall be the girdle of his waist, and faithfulness the girdle of his loins.

units.leftText: The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the goat; the calf and young lion and fatling will be together, and a little child will lead them.
units.rightText: And the wolf shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them.
leftNotes: 11:6 Hebrew; LXX the young calf and bull and lion will feed together

units.leftText: The cow will graze with the bear, their young will lie down together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox.
units.rightText: And the cow and the bear shall feed; their young ones shall lie down together; and the lion shall eat straw like the ox.

units.leftText: The infant will play by the cobra’s den, and the toddler will reach into the viper’s nest.
units.rightText: And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp, and the weaned child shall put his hand on the adder’s den.

units.leftText: They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain, for the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the sea is full of water.
units.rightText: They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain; for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of Jehovah, as the waters cover the sea.

units.leftText: On that day the Root of Jesse will stand as a banner for the peoples. The nations will seek Him, and His place of rest will be glorious.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the root of Jesse, that standeth for an ensign of the peoples, unto him shall the nations seek; and his resting-place shall be glorious.
leftNotes: 11:10 LXX On that day the Root of Jesse will appear, One who will arise to rule over the Gentiles; in Him the Gentiles will put their hope; cited in Romans 15:12|ROM 15:12*.

units.leftText: On that day the Lord will extend His hand a second time to recover the remnant of His people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord will set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, that shall remain, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.
leftNotes: 11:11 That is, the upper Nile region
11:11 That is, Babylonia
11:11 Or coastlands

units.leftText: He will raise a banner for the nations and gather the exiles of Israel; He will collect the scattered of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
units.rightText: And he will set up an ensign for the nations, and will assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.

units.leftText: Then the jealousy of Ephraim will depart, and the adversaries of Judah will be cut off. Ephraim will no longer envy Judah, nor will Judah harass Ephraim.
units.rightText: The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and they that vex Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.
leftNotes: 11:13 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel
11:13 Or hostility

units.leftText: They will swoop down on the slopes of the Philistines to the west; together they will plunder the sons of the east. They will lay their hands on Edom and Moab, and the Ammonites will be subject to them.
units.rightText: And they shall fly down upon the shoulder of the Philistines on the west; together shall they despoil the children of the east: they shall put forth their hand upon Edom and Moab; and the children of Ammon shall obey them.

units.leftText: The LORD will devote to destruction the gulf of the Sea of Egypt; with a scorching wind He will sweep His hand over the Euphrates. He will split it into seven streams for men to cross with dry sandals.
units.rightText: And Jehovah will utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea; and with his scorching wind will he wave his hand over the River, and will smite it into seven streams, and cause men to march over dryshod.
leftNotes: 11:15 Or will completely dry up
11:15 Hebrew the tongue
11:15 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: There will be a highway for the remnant of His people who remain from Assyria, as there was for Israel when they came up from the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And there shall be a highway for the remnant of his people, that shall remain, from Assyria; like as there was for Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: In that day you will say: “O LORD, I will praise You. Although You were angry with me, Your anger has turned away, and You have comforted me.
units.rightText: And in that day thou shalt say, I will give thanks unto thee, O Jehovah; for though thou wast angry with me, thine anger is turned away and thou comfortest me.

units.leftText: Surely God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid. For the LORD GOD is my strength and my song, and He also has become my salvation.”
units.rightText: Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and will not be afraid: for Jehovah, even Jehovah, is my strength and song; and he is become my salvation.

units.leftText: With joy you will draw water from the springs of salvation,
units.rightText: Therefore with joy shall ye draw water out of the wells of salvation.

units.leftText: and on that day you will say: “Give praise to the LORD; proclaim His name! Make His works known among the peoples; declare that His name is exalted.
