units.rightText: And in that day shall ye say, Give thanks unto Jehovah, call upon his name, declare his doings among the peoples, make mention that his name is exalted.

units.leftText: Sing to the LORD, for He has done glorious things. Let this be known in all the earth.
units.rightText: Sing unto Jehovah; for he hath done excellent things: let this be known in all the earth.

units.leftText: Cry out and sing, O citizen of Zion, for great among you is the Holy One of Israel.”
units.rightText: Cry aloud and shout, thou inhabitant of Zion; for great in the midst of thee is the Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: This is the burden against Babylon that Isaiah son of Amoz received:
units.rightText: The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz did see.

units.leftText: Raise a banner on a barren hilltop; call aloud to them. Wave your hand, that they may enter the gates of the nobles.
units.rightText: Set ye up an ensign upon the bare mountain, lift up the voice unto them, wave the hand, that they may go into the gates of the nobles.

units.leftText: I have commanded My sanctified ones; I have even summoned My warriors to execute My wrath and exult in My triumph.
units.rightText: I have commanded my consecrated ones, yea, I have called my mighty men for mine anger, even my proudly exulting ones.

units.leftText: Listen, a tumult on the mountains, like that of a great multitude! Listen, an uproar among the kingdoms, like nations gathered together! The LORD of Hosts is mobilizing an army for war.
units.rightText: The noise of a multitude in the mountains, as of a great people! the noise of a tumult of the kingdoms of the nations gathered together! Jehovah of hosts is mustering the host for the battle.

units.leftText: They are coming from faraway lands, from the ends of the heavens— the LORD and the weapons of His wrath— to destroy the whole country.
units.rightText: They come from a far country, from the uttermost part of heaven, even Jehovah, and the weapons of his indignation, to destroy the whole land.

units.leftText: Wail, for the Day of the LORD is near; it will come as destruction from the Almighty.
units.rightText: Wail ye; for the day of Jehovah is at hand; as destruction from the Almighty shall it come.
leftNotes: 13:6 Hebrew Shaddai

units.leftText: Therefore all hands will fall limp, and every man’s heart will melt.
units.rightText: Therefore shall all hands be feeble, and every heart of man shall melt:

units.leftText: Terror, pain, and anguish will seize them; they will writhe like a woman in labor. They will look at one another, their faces flushed with fear.
units.rightText: and they shall be dismayed; pangs and sorrows shall take hold of them; they shall be in pain as a woman in travail: they shall look in amazement one at another; their faces shall be faces of flame.

units.leftText: Behold, the Day of the LORD is coming— cruel, with fury and burning anger— to make the earth a desolation and to destroy the sinners within it.
units.rightText: Behold, the day of Jehovah cometh, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger; to make the land a desolation, and to destroy the sinners thereof out of it.

units.leftText: For the stars of heaven and their constellations will not give their light. The rising sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light.
units.rightText: For the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light; the sun shall be darkened in its going forth, and the moon shall not cause its light to shine.

units.leftText: I will punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their iniquity. I will end the haughtiness of the arrogant and lay low the pride of the ruthless.
units.rightText: And I will punish the world for their evil, and the wicked for their iniquity: and I will cause the arrogancy of the proud to cease, and will lay low the haughtiness of the terrible.

units.leftText: I will make man scarcer than pure gold, and mankind rarer than the gold of Ophir.
units.rightText: I will make a man more rare than fine gold, even a man than the pure gold of Ophir.

units.leftText: Therefore I will make the heavens tremble, and the earth will be shaken from its place at the wrath of the LORD of Hosts on the day of His burning anger.
units.rightText: Therefore I will make the heavens to tremble, and the earth shall be shaken out of its place, in the wrath of Jehovah of hosts, and in the day of his fierce anger.

units.leftText: Like a hunted gazelle, like a sheep without a shepherd, each will return to his own people, each will flee to his native land.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, that as the chased roe, and as sheep that no man gathereth, they shall turn every man to his own people, and shall flee every man to his own land.

units.leftText: Whoever is caught will be stabbed, and whoever is captured will die by the sword.
units.rightText: Every one that is found shall be thrust through; and every one that is taken shall fall by the sword.

units.leftText: Their infants will be dashed to pieces before their eyes, their houses will be looted, and their wives will be ravished.
units.rightText: Their infants also shall be dashed in pieces before their eyes; their houses shall be rifled, and their wives ravished.

units.leftText: Behold, I will stir up against them the Medes, who have no regard for silver and no desire for gold.
units.rightText: Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, who shall not regard silver, and as for gold, they shall not delight in it.

units.leftText: Their bows will dash young men to pieces; they will have no mercy on the fruit of the womb; they will not look with pity on the children.
units.rightText: And their bows shall dash the young men in pieces; and they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb; their eye shall not spare children.

units.leftText: And Babylon, the jewel of the kingdoms, the glory of the pride of the Chaldeans, will be overthrown by God like Sodom and Gomorrah.
units.rightText: And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldeans’ pride, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.

units.leftText: She will never be inhabited or settled from generation to generation; no nomad will pitch his tent there, no shepherd will rest his flock there.
units.rightText: It shall never be inhabited, neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation: neither shall the Arabian pitch tent there; neither shall shepherds make their flocks to lie down there.

units.leftText: But desert creatures will lie down there, and howling creatures will fill her houses. Ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will leap about.
units.rightText: But wild beasts of the desert shall lie there; and their houses shall be full of doleful creatures; and ostriches shall dwell there, and wild goats shall dance there.
leftNotes: 13:21 Literally Daughters of an ostrich or Daughters of an owl

units.leftText: Hyenas will howl in her fortresses and jackals in her luxurious palaces. Babylon’s time is at hand, and her days will not be prolonged.
units.rightText: And wolves shall cry in their castles, and jackals in the pleasant palaces: and her time is near to come, and her days shall not be prolonged.
leftNotes: 13:22 Or serpents or dragons

units.leftText: For the LORD will have compassion on Jacob; once again He will choose Israel and settle them in their own land. The foreigner will join them and unite with the house of Jacob.
units.rightText: For Jehovah will have compassion on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the sojourner shall join himself with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.

units.leftText: The nations will escort Israel and bring it to its homeland. Then the house of Israel will possess the nations as menservants and maidservants in the LORD’s land. They will make captives of their captors and rule over their oppressors. The Fall of the King of Babylon
units.rightText: And the peoples shall take them, and bring them to their place; and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of Jehovah for servants and for handmaids: and they shall take them captive whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.

units.leftText: On the day that the LORD gives you rest from your pain and torment, and from the hard labor into which you were forced,
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in the day that Jehovah shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy trouble, and from the hard service wherein thou wast made to serve,

units.leftText: you will sing this song of contempt against the king of Babylon: How the oppressor has ceased, and how his fury has ended!
units.rightText: that thou shalt take up this parable against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!
leftNotes: 14:4 DSS, LXX, and Syriac; MT the golden city

units.leftText: The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of the rulers.
units.rightText: Jehovah hath broken the staff of the wicked, the sceptre of the rulers;

units.leftText: It struck the peoples in anger with unceasing blows; it subdued the nations in rage with relentless persecution.
units.rightText: that smote the peoples in wrath with a continual stroke, that ruled the nations in anger, with a persecution that none restrained.

units.leftText: All the earth is at peace and at rest; they break out in song.
units.rightText: The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet: they break forth into singing.

units.leftText: Even the cypresses and cedars of Lebanon exult over you: “Since you have been laid low, no woodcutter comes against us.”
units.rightText: Yea, the fir-trees rejoice at thee, and the cedars of Lebanon, saying, Since thou art laid low, no hewer is come up against us.
leftNotes: 14:8 Or pines or junipers or firs

units.leftText: Sheol beneath is eager to meet you upon your arrival. It stirs the spirits of the dead to greet you— all the rulers of the earth. It makes all the kings of the nations rise from their thrones.
units.rightText: Sheol from beneath is moved for thee to meet thee at thy coming; it stirreth up the dead for thee, even all the chief ones of the earth; it hath raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.

units.leftText: They will all respond to you, saying, “You too have become weak, as we are; you have become like us!”
units.rightText: All they shall answer and say unto thee, Art thou also become weak as we? art thou become like unto us?

units.leftText: Your pomp has been brought down to Sheol, along with the music of your harps. Maggots are your bed and worms your blanket.
units.rightText: Thy pomp is brought down to Sheol, and the noise of thy viols: the worm is spread under thee, and worms cover thee.

units.leftText: How you have fallen from heaven, O day star, son of the dawn! You have been cut down to the ground, O destroyer of nations.
units.rightText: How art thou fallen from heaven, O day-star, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, that didst lay low the nations!
leftNotes: 14:12 Or morning star or shining one or Lucifer

units.leftText: You said in your heart: “I will ascend to the heavens; I will raise my throne above the stars of God. I will sit on the mount of assembly, in the far reaches of the north.
units.rightText: And thou saidst in thy heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God; and I will sit upon the mount of congregation, in the uttermost parts of the north;
leftNotes: 14:13 Or in the remote parts of Zaphon or on the heights of Zaphon

units.leftText: I will ascend above the tops of the clouds; I will make myself like the Most High.”
units.rightText: I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will make myself like the Most High.

units.leftText: But you will be brought down to Sheol, to the lowest depths of the Pit.
units.rightText: Yet thou shalt be brought down to Sheol, to the uttermost parts of the pit.

units.leftText: Those who see you will stare; they will ponder your fate: “Is this the man who shook the earth and made the kingdoms tremble,
units.rightText: They that see thee shall gaze at thee, they shall consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms;

units.leftText: who turned the world into a desert and destroyed its cities, who refused to let the captives return to their homes?”
units.rightText: that made the world as a wilderness, and overthrew the cities thereof; that let not loose his prisoners to their home?

units.leftText: All the kings of the nations lie in state, each in his own tomb.
units.rightText: All the kings of the nations, all of them, sleep in glory, every one in his own house.
leftNotes: 14:18 Hebrew house

units.leftText: But you are cast out of your grave like a rejected branch, covered by those slain with the sword, and dumped into a rocky pit like a carcass trampled underfoot.
units.rightText: But thou art cast forth away from thy sepulchre like an abominable branch, clothed with the slain, that are thrust through with the sword, that go down to the stones of the pit; as a dead body trodden under foot.

units.leftText: You will not join them in burial, since you have destroyed your land and slaughtered your own people. The offspring of the wicked will never again be mentioned.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not be joined with them in burial, because thou hast destroyed thy land, thou hast slain thy people; the seed of evil-doers shall not be named for ever.

units.leftText: Prepare a place to slaughter his sons for the iniquities of their forefathers. They will never rise up to possess a land or cover the earth with their cities.
units.rightText: Prepare ye slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers, that they rise not up, and possess the earth, and fill the face of the world with cities.

units.leftText: “I will rise up against them,” declares the LORD of Hosts. “I will cut off from Babylon her name and her remnant, her offspring and her posterity,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: And I will rise up against them, saith Jehovah of hosts, and cut off from Babylon name and remnant, and son and son’s son, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “I will make her a place for owls and for swamplands; I will sweep her away with the broom of destruction,” declares the LORD of Hosts. God’s Purpose against Assyria
units.rightText: I will also make it a possession for the porcupine, and pools of water: and I will sweep it with the besom of destruction, saith Jehovah of hosts.

units.leftText: The LORD of Hosts has sworn: “Surely, as I have planned, so will it be; as I have purposed, so will it stand.
units.rightText: Jehovah of hosts hath sworn, saying, Surely, as I have thought, so shall it come to pass; and as I have purposed, so shall it stand:

units.leftText: I will break Assyria in My land; I will trample him on My mountain. His yoke will be taken off My people, and his burden removed from their shoulders.”
units.rightText: that I will break the Assyrian in my land, and upon my mountains tread him under foot: then shall his yoke depart from off them, and his burden depart from off their shoulder.

units.leftText: This is the plan devised for the whole earth, and this is the hand stretched out over all the nations.
units.rightText: This is the purpose that is purposed upon the whole earth; and this is the hand that is stretched out upon all the nations.

units.leftText: The LORD of Hosts has purposed, and who can thwart Him? His hand is outstretched, so who can turn it back? Philistia Will Be Destroyed
units.rightText: For Jehovah of hosts hath purposed, and who shall annul it? and his hand is stretched out, and who shall turn it back?

units.leftText: In the year that King Ahaz died, this burden was received:
units.rightText: In the year that king Ahaz died was this burden.

units.leftText: Do not rejoice, all you Philistines, that the rod that struck you is broken. For a viper will spring from the root of the snake, and a flying serpent from its egg.
units.rightText: Rejoice not, O Philistia, all of thee, because the rod that smote thee is broken; for out of the serpent’s root shall come forth an adder, and his fruit shall be a fiery flying serpent.

units.leftText: Then the firstborn of the poor will find pasture, and the needy will lie down in safety, but I will kill your root by famine, and your remnant will be slain.
units.rightText: And the first-born of the poor shall feed, and the needy shall lie down in safety; and I will kill thy root with famine, and thy remnant shall be slain.

units.leftText: Wail, O gate! Cry out, O city! Melt away, all you Philistines! For a cloud of smoke comes from the north, and there are no stragglers in its ranks.
units.rightText: Howl, O gate; cry, O city; thou art melted away, O Philistia, all of thee; for there cometh a smoke out of the north, and there is no straggler in his ranks.

units.leftText: What answer will be given to the envoys of that nation? “The LORD has founded Zion, where His afflicted people will find refuge.”
units.rightText: What then shall one answer the messengers of the nation? That Jehovah hath founded Zion, and in her shall the afflicted of his people take refuge.

units.leftText: This is the burden against Moab: Ar in Moab is ruined, destroyed in a night! Kir in Moab is devastated, destroyed in a night!
units.rightText: The burden of Moab. For in a night Ar of Moab is laid waste, and brought to nought; for in a night Kir of Moab is laid waste, and brought to nought.

units.leftText: Dibon goes up to its temple to weep at its high places. Moab wails over Nebo, as well as over Medeba. Every head is shaved, every beard is cut off.
units.rightText: They are gone up to Bayith, and to Dibon, to the high places, to weep: Moab waileth over Nebo, and over Medeba; on all their heads is baldness, every beard is cut off.

units.leftText: In its streets they wear sackcloth; on the rooftops and in the public squares they all wail, falling down weeping.
units.rightText: In their streets they gird themselves with sackcloth; on their housetops, and in their broad places, every one waileth, weeping abundantly.

units.leftText: Heshbon and Elealeh cry out; their voices are heard as far as Jahaz. Therefore the soldiers of Moab cry out; their souls tremble within.
units.rightText: And Heshbon crieth out, and Elealeh; their voice is heard even unto Jahaz: therefore the armed men of Moab cry aloud; his soul trembleth within him.

units.leftText: My heart cries out over Moab; her fugitives flee as far as Zoar, as far as Eglath-shelishiyah. With weeping they ascend the slope of Luhith; they lament their destruction on the road to Horonaim.
units.rightText: My heart crieth out for Moab; her nobles flee unto Zoar, to Eglath-shelishi-yah: for by the ascent of Luhith with weeping they go up; for in the way of Horonaim they raise up a cry of destruction.
leftNotes: 15:5 Or Zoar, like a heifer three years of age.

units.leftText: The waters of Nimrim are dried up, and the grass is withered; the vegetation is gone, and the greenery is no more.
units.rightText: For the waters of Nimrim shall be desolate; for the grass is withered away, the tender grass faileth, there is no green thing.

units.leftText: So they carry their wealth and belongings over the Brook of the Willows.
units.rightText: Therefore the abundance they have gotten, and that which they have laid up, shall they carry away over the brook of the willows.
leftNotes: 15:7 Or Poplars

units.leftText: For their outcry echoes to the border of Moab. Their wailing reaches Eglaim; it is heard in Beer-elim.
units.rightText: For the cry is gone round about the borders of Moab; the wailing thereof unto Eglaim, and the wailing thereof unto Beer-elim.

units.leftText: The waters of Dimon are full of blood, but I will bring more upon Dimon — a lion upon the fugitives of Moab and upon the remnant of the land.
units.rightText: For the waters of Dimon are full of blood; for I will bring yet more upon Dimon, a lion upon them of Moab that escape, and upon the remnant of the land.
leftNotes: 15:9 MT, twice in this verse; DSS and Vulgate Dibon; Dimon, a wordplay on Dibon (see verse 2), sounds like the Hebrew for blood.

units.leftText: Send the tribute lambs to the ruler of the land, from Sela in the desert to the mount of Daughter Zion.
units.rightText: Send ye the lambs for the ruler of the land from Selah to the wilderness, unto the mount of the daughter of Zion.

units.leftText: Like fluttering birds pushed out of the nest, so are the daughters of Moab at the fords of the Arnon:
units.rightText: For it shall be that, as wandering birds, as a scattered nest, so shall the daughters of Moab be at the fords of the Arnon.

units.leftText: “Give us counsel; render a decision. Shelter us at noonday with shade as dark as night. Hide the refugees; do not betray the one who flees.
units.rightText: Give counsel, execute justice; make thy shade as the night in the midst of the noonday; hide the outcasts; betray not the fugitive.

units.leftText: Let my fugitives stay with you; be a refuge for Moab from the destroyer.” When the oppressor has gone, destruction has ceased, and the oppressors have vanished from the land,
units.rightText: Let mine outcasts dwell with thee; as for Moab, be thou a covert to him from the face of the destroyer. For the extortioner is brought to nought, destruction ceaseth, the oppressors are consumed out of the land.

units.leftText: in loving devotion a throne will be established in the tent of David. A judge seeking justice and hastening righteousness will sit on it in faithfulness.
units.rightText: And a throne shall be established in lovingkindness; and one shall sit thereon in truth, in the tent of David, judging, and seeking justice, and swift to do righteousness.
leftNotes: 16:5 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: We have heard of Moab’s pomposity, his exceeding pride and conceit, his overflowing arrogance. But his boasting is empty.
units.rightText: We have heard of the pride of Moab, that he is very proud; even of his arrogancy, and his pride, and his wrath; his boastings are nought.

units.leftText: Therefore let Moab wail; let them wail together for Moab. Moan for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, you who are utterly stricken.
units.rightText: Therefore shall Moab wail for Moab, every one shall wail: for the raisin-cakes of Kir-hareseth shall ye mourn, utterly stricken.

units.leftText: For the fields of Heshbon have withered, along with the grapevines of Sibmah. The rulers of the nations have trampled its choicest vines, which had reached as far as Jazer and spread toward the desert. Their shoots had spread out and passed over the sea.
units.rightText: For the fields of Heshbon languish, and the vine of Sibmah; the lords of the nations have broken down the choice branches thereof, which reached even unto Jazer, which wandered into the wilderness; its shoots were spread abroad, they passed over the sea.
leftNotes: 16:8 Or and had gone as far as the sea; that is, probably the Dead Sea

units.leftText: So I weep with Jazer for the vines of Sibmah; I drench Heshbon and Elealeh with my tears. Triumphant shouts have fallen silent over your summer fruit and your harvest.
units.rightText: Therefore I will weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah; I will water thee with my tears, O Heshbon, and Elealeh: for upon thy summer fruits and upon thy harvest the battle shout is fallen.

units.leftText: Joy and gladness are removed from the orchard; no one sings or shouts in the vineyards. No one tramples the grapes in the winepresses; I have put an end to the cheering.
units.rightText: And gladness is taken away, and joy out of the fruitful field; and in the vineyards there shall be no singing, neither joyful noise: no treader shall tread out wine in the presses; I have made the vintage shout to cease.

units.leftText: Therefore my heart laments for Moab like a harp, my inmost being for Kir-heres.
units.rightText: Wherefore my heart soundeth like a harp for Moab, and mine inward parts for Kir-heres.
leftNotes: 16:11 Kir-heres is a variant of Kir-hareseth; see verse 7.

units.leftText: When Moab appears on the high place, when he wearies himself and enters his sanctuary to pray, it will do him no good.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, when Moab presenteth himself, when he wearieth himself upon the high place, and shall come to his sanctuary to pray, that he shall not prevail.

units.leftText: This is the message that the LORD spoke earlier concerning Moab.
units.rightText: This is the word that Jehovah spake concerning Moab in time past.

units.leftText: And now the LORD says, “In three years, as a hired worker counts the years, Moab’s splendor will become an object of contempt, with all her many people. And those who are left will be few and feeble.”
units.rightText: But now Jehovah hath spoken, saying, Within three years, as the years of a hireling, the glory of Moab shall be brought into contempt, with all his great multitude; and the remnant shall be very small and of no account.

units.leftText: This is the burden against Damascus: “Behold, Damascus is no longer a city; it has become a heap of ruins.
units.rightText: The burden of Damascus. Behold, Damascus is taken away from being a city, and it shall be a ruinous heap.

units.leftText: The cities of Aroer are forsaken; they will be left to the flocks, which will lie down with no one to fear.
units.rightText: The cities of Aroer are forsaken; they shall be for flocks, which shall lie down, and none shall make them afraid.

units.leftText: The fortress will disappear from Ephraim, and the sovereignty from Damascus. The remnant of Aram will be like the splendor of the Israelites,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
units.rightText: And the fortress shall cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus, and the remnant of Syria; they shall be as the glory of the children of Israel, saith Jehovah of hosts.
leftNotes: 17:3 Or The fortified city will disappear from Ephraim, that is, from the northern kingdom of Israel

units.leftText: “In that day the splendor of Jacob will fade, and the fat of his body will waste away,
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the glory of Jacob shall be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh shall wax lean.

units.leftText: as the reaper gathers the standing grain and harvests the ears with his arm, as one gleans heads of grain in the Valley of Rephaim.
units.rightText: And it shall be as when the harvestman gathereth the standing grain, and his arm reapeth the ears; yea, it shall be as when one gleaneth ears in the valley of Rephaim.

units.leftText: Yet gleanings will remain, like an olive tree that has been beaten— two or three berries atop the tree, four or five on its fruitful branches,” declares the LORD, the God of Israel.
units.rightText: Yet there shall be left therein gleanings, as the shaking of an olive-tree, two or three berries in the top of the uppermost bough, four or five in the outmost branches of a fruitful tree, saith Jehovah, the God of Israel.

units.leftText: In that day men will look to their Maker and turn their eyes to the Holy One of Israel.
units.rightText: In that day shall men look unto their Maker, and their eyes shall have respect to the Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: They will not look to the altars they have fashioned with their hands or to the Asherahs and incense altars they have made with their fingers.
units.rightText: And they shall not look to the altars, the work of their hands; neither shall they have respect to that which their fingers have made, either the Asherim, or the sun-images.

units.leftText: In that day their strong cities will be like forsaken thickets and summits, abandoned to the Israelites and to utter desolation.
units.rightText: In that day shall their strong cities be as the forsaken places in the wood and on the mountain top, which were forsaken from before the children of Israel; and it shall be a desolation.

units.leftText: For you have forgotten the God of your salvation and failed to remember the Rock of your refuge. Therefore, though you cultivate delightful plots and set out cuttings from exotic vines —
units.rightText: For thou hast forgotten the God of thy salvation, and hast not been mindful of the rock of thy strength; therefore thou plantest pleasant plants, and settest it with strange slips.

units.leftText: though on the day you plant you make them grow, and on that morning you help your seed sprout — yet the harvest will vanish on the day of disease and incurable pain.
units.rightText: In the day of thy planting thou hedgest it in, and in the morning thou makest thy seed to blossom; but the harvest fleeth away in the day of grief and of desperate sorrow.

units.leftText: Alas, the tumult of many peoples; they rage like the roaring seas and clamoring nations; they rumble like the crashing of mighty waters.
units.rightText: Ah, the uproar of many peoples, that roar like the roaring of the seas; and the rushing of nations, that rush like the rushing of mighty waters!

units.leftText: The nations rage like the rush of many waters. He rebukes them, and they flee far away, driven before the wind like chaff on the hills, like tumbleweeds before a gale.
units.rightText: The nations shall rush like the rushing of many waters: but he shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far off, and shall be chased as the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like the whirling dust before the storm.

units.leftText: In the evening, there is sudden terror! Before morning, they are no more! This is the portion of those who loot us and the lot of those who plunder us.
units.rightText: At eventide, behold, terror; and before the morning they are not. This is the portion of them that despoil us, and the lot of them that rob us.

units.leftText: Woe to the land of whirring wings, along the rivers of Cush,
units.rightText: Ah, the land of the rustling of wings, which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia;
leftNotes: 18:1 Or of many locusts
18:1 That is, the upper Nile region

units.leftText: which sends couriers by sea, in papyrus vessels on the waters. Go, swift messengers, to a people tall and smooth-skinned, to a people widely feared, to a powerful nation of strange speech, whose land is divided by rivers.
units.rightText: that sendeth ambassadors by the sea, even in vessels of papyrus upon the waters, saying, Go, ye swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth, to a people terrible from their beginning onward, a nation that meteth out and treadeth down, whose land the rivers divide!

units.leftText: All you people of the world and dwellers of the earth, when a banner is raised on the mountains, you will see it; when a ram’s horn sounds, you will hear it.
units.rightText: All ye inhabitants of the world, and ye dwellers on the earth, when an ensign is lifted up on the mountains, see ye; and when the trumpet is blown, hear ye.

units.leftText: For this is what the LORD has told me: “I will quietly look on from My dwelling place, like shimmering heat in the sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.”
units.rightText: For thus hath Jehovah said unto me, I will be still, and I will behold in my dwelling-place, like clear heat in sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.

units.leftText: For before the harvest, when the blossom is gone and the flower becomes a ripening grape, He will cut off the shoots with a pruning knife and remove and discard the branches.
units.rightText: For before the harvest, when the blossom is over, and the flower becometh a ripening grape, he will cut off the sprigs with pruning-hooks, and the spreading branches will he take away and cut down.

units.leftText: They will all be left to the mountain birds of prey, and to the beasts of the land. The birds will feed on them in summer, and all the wild animals in winter.
units.rightText: They shall be left together unto the ravenous birds of the mountains, and to the beasts of the earth; and the ravenous birds shall summer upon them, and all the beasts of the earth shall winter upon them.

units.leftText: At that time gifts will be brought to the LORD of Hosts— from a people tall and smooth-skinned, from a people widely feared, from a powerful nation of strange speech, whose land is divided by rivers— to Mount Zion, the place of the Name of the LORD of Hosts.
units.rightText: In that time shall a present be brought unto Jehovah of hosts from a people tall and smooth, even from a people terrible from their beginning onward, a nation that meteth out and treadeth down, whose land the rivers divide, to the place of the name of Jehovah of hosts, the mount Zion.

units.leftText: This is the burden against Egypt: Behold, the LORD rides on a swift cloud; He is coming to Egypt. The idols of Egypt will tremble before Him, and the hearts of the Egyptians will melt within them.
units.rightText: The burden of Egypt. Behold, Jehovah rideth upon a swift cloud, and cometh unto Egypt: and the idols of Egypt shall tremble at his presence; and the heart of Egypt shall melt in the midst of it.

units.leftText: “So I will incite Egyptian against Egyptian; brother will fight against brother, neighbor against neighbor, city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.
units.rightText: And I will stir up the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbor; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.

units.leftText: Then the spirit of the Egyptians will be emptied out from among them, and I will frustrate their plans, so that they will resort to idols and spirits of the dead, to mediums and spiritists.
units.rightText: And the spirit of Egypt shall fail in the midst of it; and I will destroy the counsel thereof: and they shall seek unto the idols, and to the charmers, and to them that have familiar spirits, and to the wizards.

units.leftText: I will deliver the Egyptians into the hands of a harsh master, and a fierce king will rule over them,” declares the Lord GOD of Hosts.
units.rightText: And I will give over the Egyptians into the hand of a cruel lord; and a fierce king shall rule over them, saith the Lord, Jehovah of hosts.

units.leftText: The waters of the Nile will dry up, and the riverbed will be parched and empty.
units.rightText: And the waters shall fail from the sea, and the river shall be wasted and become dry.

units.leftText: The canals will stink; the streams of Egypt will trickle and dry up; the reeds and rushes will wither.
units.rightText: And the rivers shall become foul; the streams of Egypt shall be diminished and dried up; the reeds and flags shall wither away.

units.leftText: The bulrushes by the Nile, by the mouth of the river, and all the fields sown along the Nile, will wither, blow away, and be no more.
units.rightText: The meadows by the Nile, by the brink of the Nile, and all the sown fields of the Nile, shall become dry, be driven away, and be no more.

units.leftText: Then the fishermen will mourn, all who cast a hook into the Nile will lament, and those who spread nets on the waters will pine away.
units.rightText: And the fishers shall lament, and all they that cast angle into the Nile shall mourn, and they that spread nets upon the waters shall languish.

units.leftText: The workers in flax will be dismayed, and the weavers of fine linen will turn pale.
units.rightText: Moreover they that work in combed flax, and they that weave white cloth, shall be confounded.

units.leftText: The workers in cloth will be dejected, and all the hired workers will be sick at heart.
units.rightText: And the pillars of Egypt shall be broken in pieces; all they that work for hire shall be grieved in soul.
leftNotes: 19:10 Or Its pillars

units.leftText: The princes of Zoan are mere fools; Pharaoh’s wise counselors give senseless advice. How can you say to Pharaoh, “I am one of the wise, a son of eastern kings”?
units.rightText: The princes of Zoan are utterly foolish; the counsel of the wisest counsellors of Pharaoh is become brutish: how say ye unto Pharaoh, I am the son of the wise, the son of ancient kings?

units.leftText: Where are your wise men now? Let them tell you and reveal what the LORD of Hosts has planned against Egypt.
units.rightText: Where then are thy wise men? and let them tell thee now; and let them know what Jehovah of hosts hath purposed concerning Egypt.

units.leftText: The princes of Zoan have become fools; the princes of Memphis are deceived. The cornerstones of her tribes have led Egypt astray.
units.rightText: The princes of Zoan are become fools, the princes of Memphis are deceived; they have caused Egypt to go astray, that are the corner-stone of her tribes.
leftNotes: 19:13 LXX; Hebrew Noph

units.leftText: The LORD has poured into her a spirit of confusion. Egypt has been led astray in all she does, as a drunkard staggers through his own vomit.
units.rightText: Jehovah hath mingled a spirit of perverseness in the midst of her; and they have caused Egypt to go astray in every work thereof, as a drunken man staggereth in his vomit.

units.leftText: There is nothing Egypt can do — head or tail, palm or reed. A Blessing upon the Earth
units.rightText: Neither shall there be for Egypt any work, which head or tail, palm-branch or rush, may do.

units.leftText: In that day the Egyptians will be like women. They will tremble with fear beneath the uplifted hand of the LORD of Hosts, when He brandishes it against them.
units.rightText: In that day shall the Egyptians be like unto women; and they shall tremble and fear because of the shaking of the hand of Jehovah of hosts, which he shaketh over them.

units.leftText: The land of Judah will bring terror to Egypt; whenever Judah is mentioned, Egypt will tremble over what the LORD of Hosts has planned against it.
units.rightText: And the land of Judah shall become a terror unto Egypt; every one to whom mention is made thereof shall be afraid, because of the purpose of Jehovah of hosts, which he purposeth against it.

units.leftText: In that day five cities in the land of Egypt will speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the LORD of Hosts. One of them will be called the City of the Sun.
units.rightText: In that day there shall be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan, and swear to Jehovah of hosts; one shall be called The city of destruction.
leftNotes: 19:18 Some MT manuscripts, DSS, and Vulgate; most MT manuscripts City of Destruction

units.leftText: In that day there will be an altar to the LORD in the center of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to the LORD near her border.
units.rightText: In that day shall there be an altar to Jehovah in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof to Jehovah.

units.leftText: It will be a sign and a witness to the LORD of Hosts in the land of Egypt. When they cry out to the LORD because of their oppressors, He will send them a savior and defender to rescue them.
units.rightText: And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto Jehovah of hosts in the land of Egypt; for they shall cry unto Jehovah because of oppressors, and he will send them a saviour, and a defender, and he will deliver them.

units.leftText: The LORD will make Himself known to Egypt, and on that day Egypt will acknowledge the LORD. They will worship with sacrifices and offerings; they will make vows to the LORD and fulfill them.
units.rightText: And Jehovah shall be known to Egypt, and the Egyptians shall know Jehovah in that day; yea, they shall worship with sacrifice and oblation, and shall vow a vow unto Jehovah, and shall perform it.

units.leftText: And the LORD will strike Egypt with a plague; He will strike them but heal them. They will turn to the LORD, and He will hear their prayers and heal them.
units.rightText: And Jehovah will smite Egypt, smiting and healing; and they shall return unto Jehovah, and he will be entreated of them, and will heal them.

units.leftText: In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria. The Assyrians will go to Egypt, and the Egyptians to Assyria. The Egyptians and Assyrians will worship together.
units.rightText: In that day shall there be a highway out of Egypt to Assyria, and the Assyrian shall come into Egypt, and the Egyptian into Assyria; and the Egyptians shall worship with the Assyrians.

units.leftText: In that day Israel will join a three-party alliance with Egypt and Assyria— a blessing upon the earth.
units.rightText: In that day shall Israel be the third with Egypt and with Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the earth;

units.leftText: The LORD of Hosts will bless them, saying, “Blessed be Egypt My people, Assyria My handiwork, and Israel My inheritance.”
units.rightText: for that Jehovah of hosts hath blessed them, saying, Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel mine inheritance.

units.leftText: Before the year that the chief commander, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, came to Ashdod and attacked and captured it,
units.rightText: In the year that Tartan came unto Ashdod, when Sargon the king of Assyria sent him, and he fought against Ashdod and took it;

units.leftText: the LORD had already spoken through Isaiah son of Amoz, saying, “Go, remove the sackcloth from your waist and the sandals from your feet.” And Isaiah did so, walking around naked and barefoot.
units.rightText: at that time Jehovah spake by Isaiah the son of Amoz, saying, Go, and loose the sackcloth from off thy loins, and put thy shoe from off thy foot. And he did so, walking naked and barefoot.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said, “Just as My servant Isaiah has gone naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and omen against Egypt and Cush,
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, Like as my servant Isaiah hath walked naked and barefoot three years for a sign and a wonder concerning Egypt and concerning Ethiopia;
leftNotes: 20:3 That is, the upper Nile region; similarly in verses 4 and 5

units.leftText: so the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Cush, young and old alike, naked and barefoot, with bared buttocks— to Egypt’s shame.
units.rightText: so shall the king of Assyria lead away the captives of Egypt, and the exiles of Ethiopia, young and old, naked and barefoot, and with buttocks uncovered, to the shame of Egypt.

units.leftText: Those who made Cush their hope and Egypt their boast will be dismayed and ashamed.
units.rightText: And they shall be dismayed and confounded, because of Ethiopia their expectation, and of Egypt their glory.

units.leftText: And on that day the dwellers of this coastland will say, ‘See what has happened to our source of hope, those to whom we fled for help and deliverance from the king of Assyria! How then can we escape?’”
units.rightText: And the inhabitant of this coast-land shall say in that day, Behold, such is our expectation, whither we fled for help to be delivered from the king of Assyria: and we, how shall we escape?

units.leftText: This is the burden against the Desert by the Sea: Like whirlwinds sweeping through the Negev, an invader comes from the desert, from a land of terror.
units.rightText: The burden of the wilderness of the sea. As whirlwinds in the South sweep through, it cometh from the wilderness, from a terrible land.

units.leftText: A dire vision is declared to me: “The traitor still betrays, and the destroyer still destroys. Go up, O Elam! Lay siege, O Media! I will put an end to all her groaning.”
units.rightText: A grievous vision is declared unto me; the treacherous man dealeth treacherously, and the destroyer destroyeth. Go up, O Elam; besiege, O Media; all the sighing thereof have I made to cease.

units.leftText: Therefore my body is filled with anguish. Pain grips me, like the pains of a woman in labor. I am bewildered to hear, I am dismayed to see.
units.rightText: Therefore are my loins filled with anguish; pangs have taken hold upon me, as the pangs of a woman in travail: I am pained so that I cannot hear; I am dismayed so that I cannot see.

units.leftText: My heart falters; fear makes me tremble. The twilight I desired has turned to horror.
units.rightText: My heart fluttereth, horror hath affrighted me; the twilight that I desired hath been turned into trembling unto me.

units.leftText: They prepare a table, they lay out a carpet, they eat, they drink! Rise up, O princes, oil the shields!
units.rightText: They prepare the table, they set the watch, they eat, they drink: rise up, ye princes, anoint the shield.

units.leftText: For this is what the Lord says to me: “Go, post a lookout and have him report what he sees.
units.rightText: For thus hath the Lord said unto me, Go, set a watchman; let him declare what he seeth:

units.leftText: When he sees chariots with teams of horsemen, riders on donkeys, riders on camels, he must be alert, fully alert.”
units.rightText: and when he seeth a troop, horsemen in pairs, a troop of asses, a troop of camels, he shall hearken diligently with much heed.

units.leftText: Then the lookout shouted: “Day after day, my lord, I stand on the watchtower; night after night I stay at my post.
units.rightText: And he cried as a lion: O Lord, I stand continually upon the watch-tower in the day-time, and am set in my ward whole nights;
leftNotes: 21:8 DSS and Syriac; MT lion

units.leftText: Look, here come the riders, horsemen in pairs.” And one answered, saying: “Fallen, fallen is Babylon! All the images of her gods lie shattered on the ground!”
units.rightText: and, behold, here cometh a troop of men, horsemen in pairs. And he answered and said, Fallen, fallen is Babylon; and all the graven images of her gods are broken unto the ground.
leftNotes: 21:9 See Revelation 14:8|REV 14:8* and Revelation 18:2.

units.leftText: O my people, crushed on the threshing floor, I tell you what I have heard from the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel. The Burden against Edom (Isaiah 34:5–17|ISA 34:5-17*)
units.rightText: O thou my threshing, and the grain of my floor! that which I have heard from Jehovah of hosts, the God of Israel, have I declared unto you.

units.leftText: This is the burden against Dumah: One calls to me from Seir, “Watchman, what is left of the night? Watchman, what is left of the night?”
units.rightText: The burden of Dumah. One calleth unto me out of Seir, Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?
leftNotes: 21:11 Dumah is a wordplay on Edom, meaning silence.
21:11 Seir is another name for Edom.

units.leftText: The watchman replies, “Morning has come, but also the night. If you would inquire, then inquire. Come back yet again.” The Burden against Arabia
units.rightText: The watchman said, The morning cometh, and also the night: if ye will inquire, inquire ye: turn ye, come.

units.leftText: This is the burden against Arabia: In the thickets of Arabia you must lodge, O caravans of Dedanites.
units.rightText: The burden upon Arabia. In the forest in Arabia shall ye lodge, O ye caravans of Dedanites.

units.leftText: Bring water for the thirsty, O dwellers of Tema; meet the refugees with food.
units.rightText: Unto him that was thirsty they brought water; the inhabitants of the land of Tema did meet the fugitives with their bread.

units.leftText: For they flee from the sword— the sword that is drawn— from the bow that is bent, and from the stress of battle.
units.rightText: For they fled away from the swords, from the drawn sword, and from the bent bow, and from the grievousness of war.

units.leftText: For this is what the Lord says to me: “Within one year, as a hired worker would count it, all the glory of Kedar will be gone.
units.rightText: For thus hath the Lord said unto me, Within a year, according to the years of a hireling, all the glory of Kedar shall fail;

units.leftText: The remaining archers, the warriors of Kedar, will be few.” For the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.
units.rightText: and the residue of the number of the archers, the mighty men of the children of Kedar, shall be few; for Jehovah, the God of Israel, hath spoken it.

units.leftText: This is the burden against the Valley of Vision: What ails you now, that you have all gone up to the rooftops,
units.rightText: The burden of the valley of vision. What aileth thee now, that thou art wholly gone up to the housetops?

units.leftText: O city of commotion, O town of revelry? Your slain did not die by the sword, nor were they killed in battle.
units.rightText: O thou that art full of shoutings, a tumultuous city, a joyous town; thy slain are not slain with the sword, neither are they dead in battle.

units.leftText: All your rulers have fled together, captured without a bow. All your fugitives were captured together, having fled to a distant place.
units.rightText: All thy rulers fled away together, they were bound by the archers; all that were found of thee were bound together; they fled afar off.

units.leftText: Therefore I said, “Turn away from me, let me weep bitterly! Do not try to console me over the destruction of the daughter of my people.”
units.rightText: Therefore said I, Look away from me, I will weep bitterly; labor not to comfort me for the destruction of the daughter of my people.

units.leftText: For the Lord GOD of Hosts has set a day of tumult and trampling and confusion in the Valley of Vision— of breaking down the walls and crying to the mountains.
units.rightText: For it is a day of discomfiture, and of treading down, and of perplexity, from the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, in the valley of vision; a breaking down of the walls, and a crying to the mountains.

units.leftText: Elam takes up a quiver, with chariots and horsemen, and Kir uncovers the shield.
units.rightText: And Elam bare the quiver, with chariots of men and horsemen; and Kir uncovered the shield.

units.leftText: Your choicest valleys are full of chariots, and horsemen are posted at the gates.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that thy choicest valleys were full of chariots, and the horsemen set themselves in array at the gate.

units.leftText: He has uncovered the defenses of Judah.
units.rightText: And he took away the covering of Judah; and thou didst look in that day to the armor in the house of the forest.

units.leftText: You saw that there were many breaches in the walls of the City of David. You collected water from the lower pool.
units.rightText: And ye saw the breaches of the city of David, that they were many; and ye gathered together the waters of the lower pool;

units.leftText: You counted the houses of Jerusalem and tore them down to strengthen the wall.
units.rightText: and ye numbered the houses of Jerusalem, and ye brake down the houses to fortify the wall;

units.leftText: You built a reservoir between the walls for the waters of the ancient pool, but you did not look to the One who made it, or consider Him who planned it long ago.
units.rightText: ye made also a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool. But ye looked not unto him that had done this, neither had ye respect unto him that purposed it long ago.

units.leftText: On that day the Lord GOD of Hosts called for weeping and wailing, for shaven heads and the wearing of sackcloth.
units.rightText: And in that day did the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, call to weeping, and to mourning, and to baldness, and to girding with sackcloth:

units.leftText: But look, there is joy and gladness, butchering of cattle and slaughtering of sheep, eating of meat and drinking of wine: “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”
units.rightText: and, behold, joy and gladness, slaying oxen and killing sheep, eating flesh and drinking wine: Let us eat and drink, for to-morrow we shall die.
leftNotes: 22:13 Cited in 1 Corinthians 15:32|1CO 15:32*

units.leftText: The LORD of Hosts has revealed in my hearing: “Until your dying day, this sin of yours will never be atoned for,” says the Lord GOD of Hosts. A Message for Shebna
units.rightText: And Jehovah of hosts revealed himself in mine ears, Surely this iniquity shall not be forgiven you till ye die, saith the Lord, Jehovah of hosts.

units.leftText: This is what the Lord GOD of Hosts says: “Go, say to Shebna, the steward in charge of the palace:
units.rightText: Thus saith the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, Go, get thee unto this treasurer, even unto Shebna, who is over the house, and say,

units.leftText: What are you doing here, and who authorized you to carve out a tomb for yourself here — to chisel your tomb in the height and cut your resting place in the rock?
units.rightText: What doest thou here? and whom hast thou here, that thou hast hewed thee out here a sepulchre? hewing him out a sepulchre on high, graving a habitation for himself in the rock!

units.leftText: Look, O mighty man! The LORD is about to shake you violently. He will take hold of you,
units.rightText: Behold, Jehovah, like a strong man, will hurl thee away violently; yea, he will wrap thee up closely.

units.leftText: roll you into a ball, and sling you into a wide land. There you will die, and there your glorious chariots will remain— a disgrace to the house of your master.
units.rightText: He will surely wind thee round and round, and toss thee like a ball into a large country; there shalt thou die, and there shall be the chariots of thy glory, thou shame of thy lord’s house.

units.leftText: I will remove you from office, and you will be ousted from your position.
units.rightText: And I will thrust thee from thine office; and from thy station shalt thou be pulled down.

units.leftText: On that day I will summon My servant, Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah:

units.leftText: I will clothe him with your robe and tie your sash around him. I will put your authority in his hand, and he will be a father to the dwellers of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
units.rightText: and I will clothe him with thy robe, and strengthen him with thy girdle, and I will commit thy government into his hand; and he shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Judah.

units.leftText: I will place on his shoulder the key to the house of David. What he opens no one can shut, and what he shuts no one can open.
units.rightText: And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; and he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.
leftNotes: 22:22 See Revelation 3:7|REV 3:7*.

units.leftText: I will drive him like a peg into a firm place, and he will be a throne of glory for the house of his father.
units.rightText: And I will fasten him as a nail in a sure place; and he shall be for a throne of glory to his father’s house.

units.leftText: So they will hang on him all the glory of his father’s house: the descendants and the offshoots— all the lesser vessels, from bowls to every kind of jar.
units.rightText: And they shall hang upon him all the glory of his father’s house, the offspring and the issue, every small vessel, from the cups even to all the flagons.

units.leftText: In that day, declares the LORD of Hosts, the peg driven into a firm place will give way; it will be sheared off and fall, and the load upon it will be cut down.” Indeed, the LORD has spoken.
units.rightText: In that day, saith Jehovah of hosts, shall the nail that was fastened in a sure place give way; and it shall be hewn down, and fall; and the burden that was upon it shall be cut off; for Jehovah hath spoken it.

units.leftText: This is the burden against Tyre: Wail, O ships of Tarshish, for Tyre is laid waste, without house or harbor. Word has reached them from the land of Cyprus.
units.rightText: The burden of Tyre. Howl, ye ships of Tarshish; for it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in: from the land of Kittim it is revealed to them.
leftNotes: 23:1 Or Wail, O fleet of trading ships; also in verse 14
23:1 Hebrew Kittim; also in verse 12

units.leftText: Be silent, O dwellers of the coastland, you merchants of Sidon, whose traders have crossed the sea.
units.rightText: Be still, ye inhabitants of the coast, thou whom the merchants of Sidon, that pass over the sea, have replenished.
leftNotes: 23:2 DSS and LXX; MT whom the seafarers have enriched

units.leftText: On the great waters came the grain of Shihor; the harvest of the Nile was the revenue of Tyre; she was the merchant of the nations.
units.rightText: And on great waters the seed of the Shihor, the harvest of the Nile, was her revenue; and she was the mart of nations.

units.leftText: Be ashamed, O Sidon, the stronghold of the sea, for the sea has spoken: “I have not been in labor or given birth. I have not raised young men or brought up young women.”
units.rightText: Be thou ashamed, O Sidon; for the sea hath spoken, the stronghold of the sea, saying, I have not travailed, nor brought forth, neither have I nourished young men, nor brought up virgins.

units.leftText: When the report reaches Egypt, they will writhe in agony over the news of Tyre.
units.rightText: When the report cometh to Egypt, they shall be sorely pained at the report of Tyre.

units.leftText: Cross over to Tarshish; wail, O inhabitants of the coastland!
units.rightText: Pass ye over to Tarshish; wail, ye inhabitants of the coast.

units.leftText: Is this your jubilant city, whose origin is from antiquity, whose feet have taken her to settle far away?
units.rightText: Is this your joyous city, whose antiquity is of ancient days, whose feet carried her afar off to sojourn?

units.leftText: Who planned this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, whose traders are princes, whose merchants are renowned on the earth?
units.rightText: Who hath purposed this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, whose merchants are princes, whose traffickers are the honorable of the earth?

units.leftText: The LORD of Hosts planned it, to defile all its glorious beauty, to disgrace all the renowned of the earth.
units.rightText: Jehovah of hosts hath purposed it, to stain the pride of all glory, to bring into contempt all the honorable of the earth.

units.leftText: Cultivate your land like the Nile, O Daughter of Tarshish; there is no longer a harbor.
units.rightText: Pass through thy land as the Nile, O daughter of Tarshish; there is no restraint any more.
leftNotes: 23:10 DSS and some LXX manuscripts; MT Overflow

units.leftText: The LORD has stretched out His hand over the sea; He has made kingdoms tremble. He has given a command that the strongholds of Canaan be destroyed.
units.rightText: He hath stretched out his hand over the sea, he hath shaken the kingdoms: Jehovah hath given commandment concerning Canaan, to destroy the strongholds thereof.

units.leftText: He said, “You shall rejoice no more, O oppressed Virgin Daughter of Sidon. Get up and cross over to Cyprus— even there you will find no rest.”
units.rightText: And he said, Thou shalt no more rejoice, O thou oppressed virgin daughter of Sidon: arise, pass over to Kittim; even there shalt thou have no rest.

units.leftText: Look at the land of the Chaldeans — a people now of no account. The Assyrians destined it for the desert creatures; they set up their siege towers and stripped its palaces. They brought it to ruin.
units.rightText: Behold, the land of the Chaldeans: this people was not; the Assyrian founded it for them that dwell in the wilderness; they set up their towers; they overthrew the palaces thereof; they made it a ruin.
leftNotes: 23:13 That is, the Babylonians

units.leftText: Wail, O ships of Tarshish, for your harbor has been destroyed!
units.rightText: Howl, ye ships of Tarshish; for your stronghold is laid waste.

units.leftText: At that time Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years— the span of a king’s life. But at the end of seventy years, it will happen to Tyre as in the song of the harlot:
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that Tyre shall be forgotten seventy years, according to the days of one king: after the end of seventy years it shall be unto Tyre as in the song of the harlot.

units.leftText: “Take up your harp, stroll through the city, O forgotten harlot. Make sweet melody, sing many a song, so you will be remembered.”
units.rightText: Take a harp, go about the city, thou harlot that hast been forgotten; make sweet melody, sing many songs, that thou mayest be remembered.

units.leftText: And at the end of seventy years, the LORD will restore Tyre. Then she will return to hire as a prostitute and sell herself to all the kingdoms on the face of the earth.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass after the end of seventy years, that Jehovah will visit Tyre, and she shall return to her hire, and shall play the harlot with all the kingdoms of the world upon the face of the earth.

units.leftText: Yet her profits and wages will be set apart to the LORD; they will not be stored or saved, for her profit will go to those who live before the LORD, for abundant food and fine clothing.
units.rightText: And her merchandise and her hire shall be holiness to Jehovah: it shall not be treasured nor laid up; for her merchandise shall be for them that dwell before Jehovah, to eat sufficiently, and for durable clothing.

units.leftText: Behold, the LORD lays waste the earth and leaves it in ruins. He will twist its surface and scatter its inhabitants—
units.rightText: Behold, Jehovah maketh the earth empty, and maketh it waste, and turneth it upside down, and scattereth abroad the inhabitants thereof.

units.leftText: people and priest alike, servant and master, maid and mistress, buyer and seller, lender and borrower, creditor and debtor.
units.rightText: And it shall be, as with the people, so with the priest; as with the servant, so with his master; as with the maid, so with her mistress; as with the buyer, so with the seller; as with the creditor, so with the debtor; as with the taker of interest, so with the giver of interest to him.

units.leftText: The earth will be utterly laid waste and thoroughly plundered. For the LORD has spoken this word.
units.rightText: The earth shall be utterly emptied, and utterly laid waste; for Jehovah hath spoken this word.

units.leftText: The earth mourns and withers; the world languishes and fades; the exalted of the earth waste away.
units.rightText: The earth mourneth and fadeth away, the world languisheth and fadeth away, the lofty people of the earth do languish.

units.leftText: The earth is defiled by its people; they have transgressed the laws; they have overstepped the decrees and broken the everlasting covenant.
units.rightText: The earth also is polluted under the inhabitants thereof; because they have transgressed the laws, violated the statutes, broken the everlasting covenant.

units.leftText: Therefore a curse has consumed the earth, and its inhabitants must bear the guilt; the earth’s dwellers have been burned, and only a few survive.
units.rightText: Therefore hath the curse devoured the earth, and they that dwell therein are found guilty: therefore the inhabitants of the earth are burned, and few men left.

units.leftText: The new wine dries up, the vine withers. All the merrymakers now groan.
units.rightText: The new wine mourneth, the vine languisheth, all the merry-hearted do sigh.

units.leftText: The joyful tambourines have ceased; the noise of revelers has stopped; the joyful harp is silent.
units.rightText: The mirth of tabrets ceaseth, the noise of them that rejoice endeth, the joy of the harp ceaseth.

units.leftText: They no longer sing and drink wine; strong drink is bitter to those who consume it.
units.rightText: They shall not drink wine with a song; strong drink shall be bitter to them that drink it.

units.leftText: The city of chaos is shattered; every house is closed to entry.
units.rightText: The waste city is broken down; every house is shut up, that no man may come in.

units.leftText: In the streets they cry out for wine. All joy turns to gloom; rejoicing is exiled from the land.
units.rightText: There is a crying in the streets because of the wine; all joy is darkened, the mirth of the land is gone.

units.leftText: The city is left in ruins; its gate is reduced to rubble.
units.rightText: In the city is left desolation, and the gate is smitten with destruction.

units.leftText: So will it be on the earth and among the nations, like a harvested olive tree, like a gleaning after a grape harvest.
units.rightText: For thus shall it be in the midst of the earth among the peoples, as the shaking of an olive-tree, as the gleanings when the vintage is done.

units.leftText: They raise their voices, they shout for joy; from the west they proclaim the majesty of the LORD.
units.rightText: These shall lift up their voice, they shall shout; for the majesty of Jehovah they cry aloud from the sea.
leftNotes: 24:14 Or from the sea

units.leftText: Therefore glorify the LORD in the east. Extol the name of the LORD, the God of Israel in the islands of the sea.
units.rightText: Wherefore glorify ye Jehovah in the east, even the name of Jehovah, the God of Israel, in the isles of the sea.
leftNotes: 24:15 Or coastlands

units.leftText: From the ends of the earth we hear singing: “Glory to the Righteous One.” But I said, “I am wasting away! I am wasting away! Woe is me.” The treacherous betray; the treacherous deal in treachery.
units.rightText: From the uttermost part of the earth have we heard songs: Glory to the righteous. But I said, I pine away, I pine away, woe is me! the treacherous have dealt treacherously; yea, the treacherous have dealt very treacherously.

units.leftText: Terror and pit and snare await you, O dweller of the earth.
units.rightText: Fear, and the pit, and the snare, are upon thee, O inhabitant of the earth.

units.leftText: Whoever flees the sound of panic will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs from the pit will be caught in the snare. For the windows of heaven are open, and the foundations of the earth are shaken.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, that he who fleeth from the noise of the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that cometh up out of the midst of the pit shall be taken in the snare: for the windows on high are opened, and the foundations of the earth tremble.

units.leftText: The earth is utterly broken apart, the earth is split open, the earth is shaken violently.
units.rightText: The earth is utterly broken, the earth is rent asunder, the earth is shaken violently.

units.leftText: The earth staggers like a drunkard and sways like a shack. Earth’s rebellion weighs it down, and it falls, never to rise again.
units.rightText: The earth shall stagger like a drunken man, and shall sway to and fro like a hammock; and the transgression thereof shall be heavy upon it, and it shall fall, and not rise again.

units.leftText: In that day the LORD will punish the host of heaven above and the kings of the earth below.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that Jehovah will punish the host of the high ones on high, and the kings of the earth upon the earth.

units.leftText: They will be gathered together like prisoners in a pit. They will be confined to a dungeon and punished after many days.
units.rightText: And they shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit, and shall be shut up in the prison; and after many days shall they be visited.

units.leftText: The moon will be confounded and the sun will be ashamed; for the LORD of Hosts will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and before His elders with great glory.
units.rightText: Then the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed; for Jehovah of hosts will reign in mount Zion, and in Jerusalem; and before his elders shall be glory.

units.leftText: O LORD, You are my God! I will exalt You; I will praise Your name. For You have worked wonders — plans formed long ago — in perfect faithfulness.
units.rightText: O Jehovah, thou art my God; I will exalt thee, I will praise thy name; for thou hast done wonderful things, even counsels of old, in faithfulness and truth.

units.leftText: Indeed, You have made the city a heap of rubble, the fortified town a ruin. The fortress of strangers is a city no more; it will never be rebuilt.
units.rightText: For thou hast made of a city a heap, of a fortified city a ruin, a palace of strangers to be no city; it shall never be built.

units.leftText: Therefore, a strong people will honor You. The cities of ruthless nations will revere You.
units.rightText: Therefore shall a strong people glorify thee; a city of terrible nations shall fear thee.

units.leftText: For You have been a refuge for the poor, a stronghold for the needy in distress, a refuge from the storm, a shade from the heat. For the breath of the ruthless is like rain against a wall,
units.rightText: For thou hast been a stronghold to the poor, a stronghold to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shade from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall.

units.leftText: like heat in a dry land. You subdue the uproar of foreigners. As the shade of a cloud cools the heat, so the song of the ruthless is silenced.
units.rightText: As the heat in a dry place wilt thou bring down the noise of strangers; as the heat by the shade of a cloud, the song of the terrible ones shall be brought low.

units.leftText: On this mountain the LORD of Hosts will prepare a lavish banquet for all the peoples, a feast of aged wine, of choice meat, of finely aged wine.
units.rightText: And in this mountain will Jehovah of hosts make unto all peoples a feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees, of fat things full of marrow, of wines on the lees well refined.

units.leftText: On this mountain He will swallow up the shroud that enfolds all peoples, the sheet that covers all nations;
units.rightText: And he will destroy in this mountain the face of the covering that covereth all peoples, and the veil that is spread over all nations.

units.leftText: He will swallow up death forever. The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from every face and remove the disgrace of His people from the whole earth. For the LORD has spoken.
units.rightText: He hath swallowed up death for ever; and the Lord Jehovah will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the reproach of his people will he take away from off all the earth: for Jehovah hath spoken it.
leftNotes: 25:8 Or He will swallow up death in victory; cited in 1 Corinthians 15:54|1CO 15:54*
25:8 Cited in Revelation 7:17|REV 7:17* and Revelation 21:4

units.leftText: And in that day it will be said, “Surely this is our God; we have waited for Him, and He has saved us. This is the LORD for whom we have waited. Let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation.”
units.rightText: And it shall be said in that day, Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us: this is Jehovah; we have waited for him, we will be glad and rejoice in his salvation.

units.leftText: For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain. But Moab will be trampled in his place as straw is trodden into the dung pile.
units.rightText: For in this mountain will the hand of Jehovah rest; and Moab shall be trodden down in his place, even as straw is trodden down in the water of the dunghill.

units.leftText: He will spread out his hands within it, as a swimmer spreads his arms to swim. His pride will be brought low, despite the skill of his hands.
units.rightText: And he shall spread forth his hands in the midst thereof, as he that swimmeth spreadeth forth his hands to swim; but Jehovah will lay low his pride together with the craft of his hands.
leftNotes: 25:11 Or along with

units.leftText: The high-walled fortress will be brought down, cast to the ground, into the dust.
units.rightText: And the high fortress of thy walls hath he brought down, laid low, and brought to the ground, even to the dust.

units.leftText: In that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: We have a strong city; salvation is established as its walls and ramparts.
units.rightText: In that day shall this song be sung in the land of Judah: We have a strong city; salvation will he appoint for walls and bulwarks.

units.leftText: Open the gates so a righteous nation may enter— one that remains faithful.
units.rightText: Open ye the gates, that the righteous nation which keepeth faith may enter in.

units.leftText: You will keep in perfect peace the steadfast of mind, because he trusts in You.
units.rightText: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee; because he trusteth in thee.

units.leftText: Trust in the LORD forever, because GOD the LORD is the Rock eternal.
units.rightText: Trust ye in Jehovah for ever; for in Jehovah, even Jehovah, is an everlasting rock.

units.leftText: For He has humbled those who dwell on high; He lays the lofty city low. He brings it down to the ground; He casts it into the dust.
units.rightText: For he hath brought down them that dwell on high, the lofty city: he layeth it low, he layeth it low even to the ground; he bringeth it even to the dust.

units.leftText: Feet trample it down — the feet of the oppressed, the steps of the poor.
units.rightText: The foot shall tread it down; even the feet of the poor, and the steps of the needy.

units.leftText: The path of the righteous is level; You clear a straight path for the upright.
units.rightText: The way of the just is uprightness: thou that art upright dost direct the path of the just.

units.leftText: Yes, we wait for You, O LORD; we walk in the path of Your judgments. Your name and renown are the desire of our souls.
units.rightText: Yea, in the way of thy judgments, O Jehovah, have we waited for thee; to thy name, even to thy memorial name, is the desire of our soul.

units.leftText: My soul longs for You in the night; indeed, my spirit seeks You at dawn. For when Your judgments come upon the earth, the people of the world learn righteousness.
units.rightText: With my soul have I desired thee in the night; yea, with my spirit within me will I seek thee earnestly: for when thy judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
leftNotes: 26:9 Or my spirit within me seeks You.

units.leftText: Though grace is shown to the wicked man, he does not learn righteousness. In the land of righteousness he acts unjustly and fails to see the majesty of the LORD.
units.rightText: Let favor be showed to the wicked, yet will he not learn righteousness; in the land of uprightness will he deal wrongfully, and will not behold the majesty of Jehovah.

units.leftText: O LORD, Your hand is upraised, but they do not see it. They will see Your zeal for Your people and be put to shame. The fire set for Your enemies will consume them!
units.rightText: Jehovah, thy hand is lifted up, yet they see not: but they shall see thy zeal for the people, and be put to shame; yea, fire shall devour thine adversaries.

units.leftText: O LORD, You will establish peace for us. For all that we have accomplished, You have done for us.
units.rightText: Jehovah, thou wilt ordain peace for us; for thou hast also wrought all our works for us.

units.leftText: O LORD our God, other lords besides You have ruled over us, but Your name alone do we confess.
units.rightText: O Jehovah our God, other lords besides thee have had dominion over us; but by thee only will we make mention of thy name.

units.leftText: The dead will not live; the departed spirits will not rise. Therefore You have punished and destroyed them; You have wiped out all memory of them.
units.rightText: They are dead, they shall not live; they are deceased, they shall not rise: therefore hast thou visited and destroyed them, and made all remembrance of them to perish.

units.leftText: You have enlarged the nation, O LORD; You have enlarged the nation. You have gained glory for Yourself; You have extended all the borders of the land.
units.rightText: Thou hast increased the nation, O Jehovah, thou hast increased the nation; thou art glorified; thou hast enlarged all the borders of the land.

units.leftText: O LORD, they sought You in their distress; when You disciplined them, they poured out a quiet prayer.
units.rightText: Jehovah, in trouble have they visited thee; they poured out a prayer when thy chastening was upon them.

units.leftText: As a woman with child about to give birth writhes and cries out in pain, so were we in Your presence, O LORD.
units.rightText: Like as a woman with child, that draweth near the time of her delivery, is in pain and crieth out in her pangs; so we have been before thee, O Jehovah.

units.leftText: We were with child; we writhed in pain; but we gave birth to wind. We have given no salvation to the earth, nor brought any life into the world.
units.rightText: We have been with child, we have been in pain, we have as it were brought forth wind; we have not wrought any deliverance in the earth; neither have the inhabitants of the world fallen.

units.leftText: Your dead will live; their bodies will rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust! For your dew is like the dew of the morning, and the earth will bring forth her dead.
units.rightText: Thy dead shall live; my dead bodies shall arise. Awake and sing, ye that dwell in the dust; for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast forth the dead.

units.leftText: Go, my people, enter your rooms and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourselves a little while until the wrath has passed.
units.rightText: Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers, and shut thy doors about thee: hide thyself for a little moment, until the indignation be overpast.

units.leftText: For behold, the LORD is coming out of His dwelling to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity. The earth will reveal her bloodshed and will no longer conceal her slain.
units.rightText: For, behold, Jehovah cometh forth out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity: the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.

units.leftText: In that day the LORD will take His sharp, great, and mighty sword, and bring judgment on Leviathan the fleeing serpent — Leviathan the coiling serpent— and He will slay the dragon of the sea.
units.rightText: In that day Jehovah with his hard and great and strong sword will punish leviathan the swift serpent, and leviathan the crooked serpent; and he will slay the monster that is in the sea.
leftNotes: 27:1 Hebrew nachash; translated in most cases as snake; twice in this verse

units.leftText: In that day: “Sing about a fruitful vineyard.
units.rightText: In that day: A vineyard of wine, sing ye unto it.

units.leftText: I, the LORD, am its keeper; I water it continually. I guard it night and day so no one can disturb it;
units.rightText: I Jehovah am its keeper; I will water it every moment: lest any hurt it, I will keep it night and day.

units.leftText: I am not angry. If only thorns and briers confronted Me, I would march and trample them, I would burn them to the ground.
units.rightText: Wrath is not in me: would that the briers and thorns were against me in battle! I would march upon them, I would burn them together.
