units.leftText: Or let them lay claim to My protection; let them make peace with Me— yes, let them make peace with Me.”
units.rightText: Or else let him take hold of my strength, that he may make peace with me; yea, let him make peace with me.

units.leftText: In the days to come, Jacob will take root. Israel will bud and blossom and fill the whole world with fruit.
units.rightText: In days to come shall Jacob take root; Israel shall blossom and bud; and they shall fill the face of the world with fruit.

units.leftText: Has the LORD struck Israel as He struck her oppressors? Was she killed like those who slayed her?
units.rightText: Hath he smitten them as he smote those that smote them? or are they slain according to the slaughter of them that were slain by them?

units.leftText: By warfare and exile You contended with her and removed her with a fierce wind, as on the day the east wind blows.
units.rightText: In measure, when thou sendest them away, thou dost contend with them; he hath removed them with his rough blast in the day of the east wind.
leftNotes: 27:8 Or By driving her away into exile or Measure by measure, by exile

units.leftText: Therefore Jacob’s guilt will be atoned for, and the full fruit of the removal of his sin will be this: When he makes all the altar stones like crushed bits of chalk, no Asherah poles or incense altars will remain standing.
units.rightText: Therefore by this shall the iniquity of Jacob be forgiven, and this is all the fruit of taking away his sin: that he maketh all the stones of the altar as chalkstones that are beaten in sunder, so that the Asherim and the sun-images shall rise no more.
leftNotes: 27:9 LXX Therefore the guilt of Jacob will be taken away, and this is his blessing when I take away his sin; cited in Romans 11:27|ROM 11:27*

units.leftText: For the fortified city lies deserted — a homestead abandoned, a wilderness forsaken. There the calves graze, and there they lie down; they strip its branches bare.
units.rightText: For the fortified city is solitary, a habitation deserted and forsaken, like the wilderness: there shall the calf feed, and there shall he lie down, and consume the branches thereof.

units.leftText: When its limbs are dry, they are broken off. Women come and use them for kindling; for this is a people without understanding. Therefore their Maker has no compassion on them, and their Creator shows them no favor.
units.rightText: When the boughs thereof are withered, they shall be broken off; the women shall come, and set them on fire; for it is a people of no understanding: therefore he that made them will not have compassion upon them, and he that formed them will show them no favor.

units.leftText: In that day the LORD will thresh from the flowing Euphrates to the Wadi of Egypt, and you, O Israelites, will be gathered one by one.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that Jehovah will beat off his fruit from the flood of the River unto the brook of Egypt; and ye shall be gathered one by one, O ye children of Israel.
leftNotes: 27:12 Hebrew River

units.leftText: And in that day a great ram’s horn will sound, and those who were perishing in Assyria will come forth with those who were exiles in Egypt. And they will worship the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that a great trumpet shall be blown; and they shall come that were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and they that were outcasts in the land of Egypt; and they shall worship Jehovah in the holy mountain at Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Woe to the majestic crown of Ephraim’s drunkards, to the fading flower of his glorious splendor, set on the summit above the fertile valley, the pride of those overcome by wine.
units.rightText: Woe to the crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim, and to the fading flower of his glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fat valley of them that are overcome with wine!
leftNotes: 28:1 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verse 3

units.leftText: Behold, the Lord has one who is strong and mighty. Like a hailstorm or destructive tempest, like a driving rain or flooding downpour, he will smash that crown to the ground.
units.rightText: Behold, the Lord hath a mighty and strong one; as a tempest of hail, a destroying storm, as a tempest of mighty waters overflowing, will he cast down to the earth with the hand.

units.leftText: The majestic crown of Ephraim’s drunkards will be trampled underfoot.
units.rightText: The crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim shall be trodden under foot:

units.leftText: The fading flower of his beautiful splendor, set on the summit above the fertile valley, will be like a ripe fig before the summer harvest: Whoever sees it will take it in his hand and swallow it.
units.rightText: and the fading flower of his glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fat valley, shall be as the first-ripe fig before the summer; which when he that looketh upon it seeth, while it is yet in his hand he eateth it up.

units.leftText: On that day the LORD of Hosts will be a crown of glory, a diadem of splendor to the remnant of His people,
units.rightText: In that day will Jehovah of hosts become a crown of glory, and a diadem of beauty, unto the residue of his people;

units.leftText: a spirit of justice to him who sits in judgment, and a strength to those who repel the onslaught at the gate.
units.rightText: and a spirit of justice to him that sitteth in judgment, and strength to them that turn back the battle at the gate.

units.leftText: These also stagger from wine and stumble from strong drink: Priests and prophets reel from strong drink and are befuddled by wine. They stumble because of strong drink, muddled in their visions and stumbling in their judgments.
units.rightText: And even these reel with wine, and stagger with strong drink; the priest and the prophet reel with strong drink, they are swallowed up of wine, they stagger with strong drink; they err in vision, they stumble in judgment.

units.leftText: For all their tables are covered with vomit; there is not a place without filth.
units.rightText: For all tables are full of vomit and filthiness, so that there is no place clean.

units.leftText: Whom is He trying to teach? To whom is He explaining His message? To infants just weaned from milk? To babies removed from the breast?
units.rightText: Whom will he teach knowledge? and whom will he make to understand the message? them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts?

units.leftText: For they hear: “Order on order, order on order, line on line, line on line; a little here, a little there.”
units.rightText: For it is precept upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, there a little.
leftNotes: 28:10 Or For He says or For it is; literally For
28:10 Or Do this, do that, a rule for this, a rule for that; Hebrew sav lasav sav lasav kav lakav kav lakav (possibly meaningless sounds to demonstrate an inability to understand); also in verse 13

units.leftText: Indeed, with mocking lips and foreign tongues,
units.rightText: Nay, but by men of strange lips and with another tongue will he speak to this people;

units.leftText: to whom He has said: “This is the place of rest, let the weary rest; this is the place of repose.” But they would not listen.
units.rightText: to whom he said, This is the rest, give ye rest to him that is weary; and this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear.

units.leftText: Then the word of the LORD to them will become: “Order on order, order on order, line on line, line on line; a little here, a little there,” so that they will go stumbling backward and will be injured, ensnared, and captured. A Cornerstone in Zion (1 Corinthians 3:10–15|1CO 3:10-15*; Ephesians 2:19–22|EPH 2:19-22*; 1 Peter 2:1–8|1PE 2:1-8*)
units.rightText: Therefore shall the word of Jehovah be unto them precept upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, there a little; that they may go, and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken.

units.leftText: Therefore hear the word of the LORD, O scoffers who rule this people in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Wherefore hear the word of Jehovah, ye scoffers, that rule this people that is in Jerusalem:

units.leftText: For you said, “We have made a covenant with death; we have fashioned an agreement with Sheol. When the overwhelming scourge passes through it will not touch us, because we have made lies our refuge and falsehood our hiding place.”
units.rightText: Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with Sheol are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us; for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves:
leftNotes: 28:15 Or false gods

units.leftText: So this is what the Lord GOD says: “See, I lay a stone in Zion, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation; the one who believes will never be shaken.
units.rightText: therefore thus saith the Lord Jehovah, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner- stone of sure foundation: he that believeth shall not be in haste.
leftNotes: 28:16 LXX will never be put to shame; cited in Romans 9:33|ROM 9:33*, Romans 10:11, and 1 Peter 2:6

units.leftText: I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the level. Hail will sweep away your refuge of lies, and water will flood your hiding place.
units.rightText: And I will make justice the line, and righteousness the plummet; and the hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies, and the waters shall overflow the hiding-place.

units.leftText: Your covenant with death will be dissolved, and your agreement with Sheol will not stand. When the overwhelming scourge passes through, you will be trampled by it.
units.rightText: And your covenant with death shall be annulled, and your agreement with Sheol shall not stand; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, then ye shall be trodden down by it.

units.leftText: As often as it passes through, it will carry you away; it will sweep through morning after morning, by day and by night.” The understanding of this message will bring sheer terror.
units.rightText: As often as it passeth through, it shall take you; for morning by morning shall it pass through, by day and by night: and it shall be nought but terror to understand the message.

units.leftText: Indeed, the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket too small to wrap around you.
units.rightText: For the bed is shorter than that a man can stretch himself on it; and the covering narrower than that he can wrap himself in it.

units.leftText: For the LORD will rise up as at Mount Perazim. He will rouse Himself as in the Valley of Gibeon, to do His work, His strange work, and to perform His task, His disturbing task.
units.rightText: For Jehovah will rise up as in mount Perazim, he will be wroth as in the valley of Gibeon; that he may do his work, his strange work, and bring to pass his act, his strange act.

units.leftText: So now, do not mock, or your shackles will become heavier. Indeed, I have heard from the Lord GOD of Hosts a decree of destruction against the whole land. Listen and Hear
units.rightText: Now therefore be ye not scoffers, lest your bonds be made strong; for a decree of destruction have I heard from the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, upon the whole earth.

units.leftText: Listen and hear my voice. Pay attention and hear what I say.
units.rightText: Give ye ear, and hear my voice; hearken, and hear my speech.

units.leftText: Does the plowman plow for planting every day? Does he continuously loosen and harrow the soil?
units.rightText: Doth he that ploweth to sow plow continually? doth he continually open and harrow his ground?

units.leftText: When he has leveled its surface, does he not sow caraway and scatter cumin? He plants wheat in rows and barley in plots, and rye within its border.
units.rightText: When he hath levelled the face thereof, doth he not cast abroad the fitches, and scatter the cummin, and put in the wheat in rows, and the barley in the appointed place, and the spelt in the border thereof?

units.leftText: For his God instructs and teaches him properly.
units.rightText: For his God doth instruct him aright, and doth teach him.

units.leftText: Surely caraway is not threshed with a sledge, and the wheel of a cart is not rolled over the cumin. But caraway is beaten out with a stick, and cumin with a rod.
units.rightText: For the fitches are not threshed with a sharp threshing instrument, neither is a cart wheel turned about upon the cummin; but the fitches are beaten out with a staff, and the cummin with a rod.

units.leftText: Grain for bread must be ground, but it is not endlessly threshed. Though the wheels of the cart roll over it, the horses do not crush it.
units.rightText: Bread grain is ground; for he will not be always threshing it: and though the wheel of his cart and his horses scatter it, he doth not grind it.

units.leftText: This also comes from the LORD of Hosts, who is wonderful in counsel and excellent in wisdom.
units.rightText: This also cometh forth from Jehovah of hosts, who is wonderful in counsel, and excellent in wisdom.

units.leftText: Woe to you, O Ariel, the city of Ariel where David camped! Year upon year let your festivals recur.
units.rightText: Ho Ariel, Ariel, the city where David encamped! add ye year to year; let the feasts come round:
leftNotes: 29:1 Or Altar Hearth or Lion of God; probably a nickname for Jerusalem; twice in this verse, twice in verse 2, and once in verse 7

units.leftText: And I will constrain Ariel, and there will be mourning and lamentation; she will be like an altar hearth before Me.
units.rightText: then will I distress Ariel, and there shall be mourning and lamentation; and she shall be unto me as Ariel.
leftNotes: 29:2 Or like Ariel; see the footnote for verse 1.

units.leftText: I will camp in a circle around you; I will besiege you with towers and set up siege works against you.
units.rightText: And I will encamp against thee round about, and will lay siege against thee with posted troops, and I will raise siege works against thee.

units.leftText: You will be brought low, you will speak from the ground, and out of the dust your words will be muffled. Your voice will be like a spirit from the ground; your speech will whisper out of the dust.
units.rightText: And thou shalt be brought down, and shalt speak out of the ground, and thy speech shall be low out of the dust; and thy voice shall be as of one that hath a familiar spirit, out of the ground, and thy speech shall whisper out of the dust.

units.leftText: But your many foes will be like fine dust, the multitude of the ruthless like blowing chaff. Then suddenly, in an instant,
units.rightText: But the multitude of thy foes shall be like small dust, and the multitude of the terrible ones as chaff that passeth away: yea, it shall be in an instant suddenly.

units.leftText: you will be visited by the LORD of Hosts with thunder and earthquake and loud noise, with windstorm and tempest and consuming flame of fire.
units.rightText: She shall be visited of Jehovah of hosts with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with whirlwind and tempest, and the flame of a devouring fire.

units.leftText: All the many nations going out to battle against Ariel— even all who war against her, laying siege and attacking her— will be like a dream, like a vision in the night,
units.rightText: And the multitude of all the nations that fight against Ariel, even all that fight against her and her stronghold, and that distress her, shall be as a dream, a vision of the night.

units.leftText: as when a hungry man dreams he is eating, then awakens still hungry; as when a thirsty man dreams he is drinking, then awakens faint and parched. So will it be for all the many nations who go to battle against Mount Zion.
units.rightText: And it shall be as when a hungry man dreameth, and, behold, he eateth; but he awaketh, and his soul is empty: or as when a thirsty man dreameth, and, behold, he drinketh; but he awaketh, and, behold, he is faint, and his soul hath appetite: so shall the multitude of all the nations be, that fight against mount Zion.

units.leftText: Stop and be astonished; blind yourselves and be sightless; be drunk, but not with wine; stagger, but not from strong drink.
units.rightText: Tarry ye and wonder; take your pleasure and be blind: they are drunken, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.

units.leftText: For the LORD has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep. He has shut your eyes, O prophets; He has covered your heads, O seers.
units.rightText: For Jehovah hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep, and hath closed your eyes, the prophets; and your heads, the seers, hath he covered.

units.leftText: And the entire vision will be to you like the words sealed in a scroll. If it is handed to someone to read, he will say, “I cannot, because it is sealed.”
units.rightText: And all vision is become unto you as the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one that is learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee; and he saith, I cannot, for it is sealed:

units.leftText: Or if the scroll is handed to one unable to read, he will say, “I cannot read.”
units.rightText: and the book is delivered to him that is not learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee; and he saith, I am not learned.

units.leftText: Therefore the Lord said: “These people draw near to Me with their mouths and honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me. Their worship of Me is but rules taught by men.
units.rightText: And the Lord said, Forasmuch as this people draw nigh unto me, and with their mouth and with their lips do honor me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear of me is a commandment of men which hath been taught them;
leftNotes: 29:13 Hebrew; LXX They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.Cited in Matthew 15:8–9|MAT 15:8-9* and Mark 7:6–7

units.leftText: Therefore I will again confound these people with wonder upon wonder. The wisdom of the wise will vanish, and the intelligence of the intelligent will be hidden. ”
units.rightText: therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvellous work among this people, even a marvellous work and a wonder; and the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid.
leftNotes: 29:14 Hebrew; LXX I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will hide the intelligence of the intelligent.Cited in 1 Corinthians 1:19|1CO 1:19*

units.leftText: Woe to those who dig deep to hide their plans from the LORD. In darkness they do their works and say, “Who sees us, and who will know?”
units.rightText: Woe unto them that hide deep their counsel from Jehovah, and whose works are in the dark, and that say, Who seeth us? and who knoweth us?

units.leftText: You have turned things upside down, as if the potter were regarded as clay. Shall what is formed say to him who formed it, “He did not make me”? Can the pottery say of the potter, “He has no understanding”? Sanctification for the Godly
units.rightText: Ye turn things upside down! Shall the potter be esteemed as clay; that the thing made should say of him that made it, He made me not; or the thing formed say of him that formed it, He hath no understanding?
leftNotes: 29:16 Cited in Romans 9:20|ROM 9:20*

units.leftText: In a very short time, will not Lebanon become an orchard, and the orchard seem like a forest?
units.rightText: Is it not yet a very little while, and Lebanon shall be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field shall be esteemed as a forest?

units.leftText: On that day the deaf will hear the words of the scroll, and out of the deep darkness the eyes of the blind will see.
units.rightText: And in that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity and out of darkness.

units.leftText: The humble will increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor among men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
units.rightText: The meek also shall increase their joy in Jehovah, and the poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: For the ruthless will vanish, the mockers will disappear, and all who look for evil will be cut down—
units.rightText: For the terrible one is brought to nought, and the scoffer ceaseth, and all they that watch for iniquity are cut off;

units.leftText: those who indict a man with a word, who ensnare the mediator at the gate, and who with false charges deprive the innocent of justice.
units.rightText: that make a man an offender in his cause, and lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate, and turn aside the just with a thing of nought.

units.leftText: Therefore the LORD who redeemed Abraham says of the house of Jacob: “No longer will Jacob be ashamed and no more will his face grow pale.
units.rightText: Therefore thus saith Jehovah, who redeemed Abraham, concerning the house of Jacob: Jacob shall not now be ashamed, neither shall his face now wax pale.

units.leftText: For when he sees his children around him, the work of My hands, they will honor My name, they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and they will stand in awe of the God of Israel.
units.rightText: But when he seeth his children, the work of my hands, in the midst of him, they shall sanctify my name; yea, they shall sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall stand in awe of the God of Israel.

units.leftText: Then the wayward in spirit will come to understanding, and those who grumble will accept instruction.”
units.rightText: They also that err in spirit shall come to understanding, and they that murmur shall receive instruction.

units.leftText: “Woe to the rebellious children,” declares the LORD, “to those who carry out a plan that is not Mine, who form an alliance, but against My will, heaping up sin upon sin.
units.rightText: Woe to the rebellious children, saith Jehovah, that take counsel, but not of me; and that make a league, but not of my Spirit, that they may add sin to sin,

units.leftText: They set out to go down to Egypt without asking My advice, to seek shelter under Pharaoh’s protection and take refuge in Egypt’s shade.
units.rightText: that set out to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to take refuge in the shadow of Egypt!

units.leftText: But Pharaoh’s protection will become your shame, and the refuge of Egypt’s shade your disgrace.
units.rightText: Therefore shall the strength of Pharaoh be your shame, and the refuge in the shadow of Egypt your confusion.

units.leftText: For though their princes are at Zoan and their envoys have arrived in Hanes,
units.rightText: For their princes are at Zoan, and their ambassadors are come to Hanes.

units.leftText: everyone will be put to shame because of a people useless to them. They bring neither help nor benefit, but only shame and disgrace.”
units.rightText: They shall all be ashamed because of a people that cannot profit them, that are not a help nor profit, but a shame, and also a reproach.

units.leftText: This is the burden against the beasts of the Negev: Through a land of hardship and distress, of lioness and lion, of viper and flying serpent, they carry their wealth on the backs of donkeys and their treasures on the humps of camels, to a people of no profit to them.
units.rightText: The burden of the beasts of the South. Through the land of trouble and anguish, from whence come the lioness and the lion, the viper and fiery flying serpent, they carry their riches upon the shoulders of young asses, and their treasures upon the humps of camels, to a people that shall not profit them.

units.leftText: Egypt’s help is futile and empty; therefore I have called her Rahab Who Sits Still.
units.rightText: For Egypt helpeth in vain, and to no purpose: therefore have I called her Rahab that sitteth still.
leftNotes: 30:7 Hebrew Rahab-hem-shebeth

units.leftText: Go now, write it on a tablet in their presence and inscribe it on a scroll; it will be for the days to come, a witness forever and ever.
units.rightText: Now go, write it before them on a tablet, and inscribe it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever.

units.leftText: These are rebellious people, deceitful children, children unwilling to obey the LORD’s instruction.
units.rightText: For it is a rebellious people, lying children, children that will not hear the law of Jehovah;

units.leftText: They say to the seers, “Stop seeing visions!” and to the prophets, “Do not prophesy to us the truth! Speak to us pleasant words; prophesy illusions.
units.rightText: that say to the seers, See not; and to the prophets, Prophesy not unto us right things, speak unto us smooth things, prophesy deceits,

units.leftText: Get out of the way; turn off the road. Rid us of the Holy One of Israel!”
units.rightText: get you out of the way, turn aside out of the path, cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us.

units.leftText: Therefore this is what the Holy One of Israel says: “Because you have rejected this message, trusting in oppression and relying on deceit,
units.rightText: Wherefore thus saith the Holy One of Israel, Because ye despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and rely thereon;

units.leftText: this iniquity of yours is like a breach about to fail, a bulge in a high wall, whose collapse will come suddenly — in an instant!
units.rightText: therefore this iniquity shall be to you as a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking cometh suddenly in an instant.

units.leftText: It will break in pieces like a potter’s jar, shattered so that no fragment can be found. Not a shard will be found in the dust large enough to scoop the coals from a hearth or to skim the water from a cistern.”
units.rightText: And he shall break it as a potter’s vessel is broken, breaking it in pieces without sparing; so that there shall not be found among the pieces thereof a sherd wherewith to take fire from the hearth, or to dip up water out of the cistern.

units.leftText: For the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, has said: “By repentance and rest you would be saved; your strength would lie in quiet confidence — but you were not willing.”
units.rightText: For thus said the Lord Jehovah, the Holy One of Israel, In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength. And ye would not:

units.leftText: “No,” you say, “we will flee on horses.” Therefore you will flee! “We will ride swift horses,” but your pursuers will be faster.
units.rightText: but ye said, No, for we will flee upon horses; therefore shall ye flee: and, We will ride upon the swift; therefore shall they that pursue you be swift.

units.leftText: A thousand will flee at the threat of one; at the threat of five you will all flee, until you are left alone like a pole on a mountaintop, like a banner on a hill. God Will Be Gracious
units.rightText: One thousand shall flee at the threat of one; at the threat of five shall ye flee: till ye be left as a beacon upon the top of a mountain, and as an ensign on a hill.

units.leftText: Therefore the LORD longs to be gracious to you; therefore He rises to show you compassion, for the LORD is a just God. Blessed are all who wait for Him.
units.rightText: And therefore will Jehovah wait, that he may be gracious unto you; and therefore will he be exalted, that he may have mercy upon you: for Jehovah is a God of justice; blessed are all they that wait for him.

units.leftText: O people in Zion who dwell in Jerusalem, you will weep no more. He will surely be gracious when you cry for help; when He hears, He will answer you.
units.rightText: For the people shall dwell in Zion at Jerusalem; thou shalt weep no more; he will surely be gracious unto thee at the voice of thy cry; when he shall hear, he will answer thee.

units.leftText: The Lord will give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, but your Teacher will no longer hide Himself — with your own eyes you will see Him.
units.rightText: And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, yet shall not thy teachers be hidden anymore, but thine eyes shall see thy teachers;

units.leftText: And whether you turn to the right or to the left, your ears will hear this command behind you: “This is the way. Walk in it.”
units.rightText: and thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it; when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.

units.leftText: So you will desecrate your silver-plated idols and your gold-plated images. You will throw them away like menstrual cloths, saying to them, “Be gone!”
units.rightText: And ye shall defile the overlaying of thy graven images of silver, and the plating of thy molten images of gold: thou shalt cast them away as an unclean thing; thou shalt say unto it, Get thee hence.

units.leftText: Then He will send rain for the seed that you have sown in the ground, and the food that comes from your land will be rich and plentiful. On that day your cattle will graze in open pastures.
units.rightText: And he will give the rain for thy seed, wherewith thou shalt sow the ground; and bread of the increase of the ground, and it shall be fat and plenteous. In that day shall thy cattle feed in large pastures;

units.leftText: The oxen and donkeys that work the ground will eat salted fodder, winnowed with shovel and pitchfork.
units.rightText: the oxen likewise and the young asses that till the ground shall eat savory provender, which hath been winnowed with the shovel and with the fork.

units.leftText: And from every high mountain and every raised hill, streams of water will flow in the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall.
units.rightText: And there shall be upon every lofty mountain, and upon every high hill, brooks and streams of waters, in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.

units.leftText: The light of the moon will be as bright as the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter— like the light of seven days— on the day that the LORD binds up the brokenness of His people and heals the wounds He has inflicted.
units.rightText: Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that Jehovah bindeth up the hurt of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.

units.leftText: Behold, the Name of the LORD comes from afar, with burning anger and dense smoke. His lips are full of fury, and His tongue is like a consuming fire.
units.rightText: Behold, the name of Jehovah cometh from far, burning with his anger, and in thick rising smoke: his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue is as a devouring fire;

units.leftText: His breath is like a rushing torrent that rises to the neck. He comes to sift the nations in a sieve of destruction; He bridles the jaws of the peoples to lead them astray.
units.rightText: and his breath is as an overflowing stream, that reacheth even unto the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of destruction: and a bridle that causeth to err shall be in the jaws of the peoples.

units.leftText: You will sing as on the night of a holy festival, and your heart will rejoice like one who walks to the music of a flute, going up to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
units.rightText: Ye shall have a song as in the night when a holy feast is kept; and gladness of heart, as when one goeth with a pipe to come unto the mountain of Jehovah, to the Rock of Israel.

units.leftText: And the LORD will cause His majestic voice to be heard and His mighty arm to be revealed, striking in angry wrath with a flame of consuming fire, and with cloudburst, storm, and hailstones.
units.rightText: And Jehovah will cause his glorious voice to be heard, and will show the lighting down of his arm, with the indignation of his anger, and the flame of a devouring fire, with a blast, and tempest, and hailstones.

units.leftText: For Assyria will be shattered at the voice of the LORD; He will strike them with His scepter.
units.rightText: For through the voice of Jehovah shall the Assyrian be dismayed; with his rod will he smite him.

units.leftText: And with every stroke of the rod of punishment that the LORD brings down on them, the tambourines and lyres will sound as He battles with weapons brandished.
units.rightText: And every stroke of the appointed staff, which Jehovah shall lay upon him, shall be with the sound of tabrets and harps; and in battles with the brandishing of his arm will he fight with them.
leftNotes: 30:32 Some Hebrew manuscripts, Syriac; MT the rod of foundation; DSS the rod of His foundation

units.leftText: For Topheth has long been prepared; it has been made ready for the king. Its funeral pyre is deep and wide, with plenty of fire and wood. The breath of the LORD, like a torrent of burning sulfur, sets it ablaze.
units.rightText: For a Topheth is prepared of old; yea, for the king it is made ready; he hath made it deep and large; the pile thereof is fire and much wood; the breath of Jehovah, like a stream of brimstone, doth kindle it.

units.leftText: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, who rely on horses, who trust in their abundance of chariots and in their multitude of horsemen. They do not look to the Holy One of Israel; they do not seek the LORD.
units.rightText: Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help, and rely on horses, and trust in chariots because they are many, and in horsemen because they are very strong, but they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek Jehovah!

units.leftText: Yet He too is wise and brings disaster; He does not call back His words. He will rise up against the house of the wicked and against the allies of evildoers.
units.rightText: Yet he also is wise, and will bring evil, and will not call back his words, but will arise against the house of the evil-doers, and against the help of them that work iniquity.

units.leftText: But the Egyptians are men, not God; their horses are flesh, not spirit. When the LORD stretches out His hand, the helper will stumble, and the one he helps will fall; both will perish together.
units.rightText: Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit: and when Jehovah shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall stumble, and he that is helped shall fall, and they all shall be consumed together.

units.leftText: For this is what the LORD has said to me: “Like a lion roaring or a young lion over its prey — and though a band of shepherds is called out against it, it is not terrified by their shouting or subdued by their clamor — so the LORD of Hosts will come down to do battle on Mount Zion and its heights.
units.rightText: For thus saith Jehovah unto me, As the lion and the young lion growling over his prey, if a multitude of shepherds be called forth against him, will not be dismayed at their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them: so will Jehovah of hosts come down to fight upon mount Zion, and upon the hill thereof.

units.leftText: Like birds hovering overhead, so the LORD of Hosts will protect Jerusalem. He will shield it and deliver it; He will pass over it and preserve it.”
units.rightText: As birds hovering, so will Jehovah of hosts protect Jerusalem; he will protect and deliver it, he will pass over and preserve it.

units.leftText: Return to the One against whom you have so blatantly rebelled, O children of Israel.
units.rightText: Turn ye unto him from whom ye have deeply revolted, O children of Israel.

units.leftText: For on that day, every one of you will reject the idols of silver and gold that your own hands have sinfully made.
units.rightText: For in that day they shall cast away every man his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which your own hands have made unto you for a sin.

units.leftText: “Then Assyria will fall, but not by the sword of man; a sword will devour them, but not one made by mortals. They will flee before the sword, and their young men will be put to forced labor.
units.rightText: And the Assyrian shall fall by the sword, not of man; and the sword, not of men, shall devour him; and he shall flee from the sword, and his young men shall become subject to taskwork.

units.leftText: Their rock will pass away for fear, and their princes will panic at the sight of the battle standard,” declares the LORD, whose fire is in Zion, whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And his rock shall pass away by reason of terror, and his princes shall be dismayed at the ensign, saith Jehovah, whose fire is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Behold, a king will reign in righteousness, and princes will rule with justice.
units.rightText: Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in justice.

units.leftText: Each will be like a shelter from the wind, a refuge from the storm, like streams of water in a dry land, like the shadow of a great rock in an arid land.
units.rightText: And a man shall be as a hiding-place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest, as streams of water in a dry place, as the shade of a great rock in a weary land.

units.leftText: Then the eyes of those who see will no longer be closed, and the ears of those who hear will listen.
units.rightText: And the eyes of them that see shall not be dim, and the ears of them that hear shall hearken.

units.leftText: The mind of the rash will know and understand, and the stammering tongue will speak clearly and fluently.
units.rightText: And the heart of the rash shall understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers shall be ready to speak plainly.

units.leftText: No longer will a fool be called noble, nor a scoundrel be respected.
units.rightText: The fool shall be no more called noble, nor the churl said to be bountiful.

units.leftText: For a fool speaks foolishness; his mind plots iniquity. He practices ungodliness and speaks falsely about the LORD; he leaves the hungry empty and deprives the thirsty of drink.
units.rightText: For the fool will speak folly, and his heart will work iniquity, to practise profaneness, and to utter error against Jehovah, to make empty the soul of the hungry, and to cause the drink of the thirsty to fail.

units.leftText: The weapons of the scoundrel are destructive; he hatches plots to destroy the poor with lies, even when the plea of the needy is just.
units.rightText: And the instruments of the churl are evil: he deviseth wicked devices to destroy the meek with lying words, even when the needy speaketh right.

units.leftText: But a noble man makes honorable plans; he stands up for worthy causes. The Women of Jerusalem
units.rightText: But the noble deviseth noble things; and in noble things shall he continue.

units.leftText: Stand up, you complacent women; listen to me. Give ear to my word, you overconfident daughters.
units.rightText: Rise up, ye women that are at ease, and hear my voice; ye careless daughters, give ear unto my speech.

units.leftText: In a little more than a year you will tremble, O secure ones. For the grape harvest will fail and the fruit harvest will not arrive.
units.rightText: For days beyond a year shall ye be troubled, ye careless women; for the vintage shall fail, the ingathering shall not come.

units.leftText: Shudder, you ladies of leisure; tremble, you daughters of complacency. Strip yourselves bare and put sackcloth around your waists.
units.rightText: Tremble, ye women that are at ease; be troubled, ye careless ones; strip you, and make you bare, and gird sackcloth upon your loins.

units.leftText: Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vines,
units.rightText: They shall smite upon the breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine.

units.leftText: and for the land of my people, overgrown with thorns and briers — even for every house of merriment in this city of revelry.
units.rightText: Upon the land of my people shall come up thorns and briers; yea, upon all the houses of joy in the joyous city.

units.leftText: For the palace will be forsaken, the busy city abandoned. The hill and the watchtower will become caves forever — the delight of wild donkeys and a pasture for flocks —
units.rightText: For the palace shall be forsaken; the populous city shall be deserted; the hill and the watch-tower shall be for dens for ever, a joy of wild asses, a pasture of flocks;
leftNotes: 32:14 Hebrew The Ophel

units.leftText: until the Spirit is poured out upon us from on high. Then the desert will be an orchard, and the orchard will seem like a forest.
units.rightText: until the Spirit be poured upon us from on high, and the wilderness become a fruitful field, and the fruitful field be esteemed as a forest.

units.leftText: Then justice will inhabit the wilderness, and righteousness will dwell in the fertile field.
units.rightText: Then justice shall dwell in the wilderness; and righteousness shall abide in the fruitful field.

units.leftText: The work of righteousness will be peace; the service of righteousness will be quiet confidence forever.
units.rightText: And the work of righteousness shall be peace; and the effect of righteousness, quietness and confidence for ever.

units.leftText: Then my people will dwell in a peaceful place, in safe and secure places of rest.
units.rightText: And my people shall abide in a peaceable habitation, and in safe dwellings, and in quiet resting-places.

units.leftText: But hail will level the forest, and the city will sink to the depths.
units.rightText: But it shall hail in the downfall of the forest; and the city shall be utterly laid low.

units.leftText: Blessed are those who sow beside abundant waters, who let the ox and donkey range freely.
units.rightText: Blessed are ye that sow beside all waters, that send forth the feet of the ox and the ass.

units.leftText: Woe to you, O destroyer never destroyed, O traitor never betrayed! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed. When you have finished betraying, you will be betrayed.
units.rightText: Woe to thee that destroyest, and thou wast not destroyed; and dealest treacherously, and they dealt not treacherously with thee! When thou hast ceased to destroy, thou shalt be destroyed; and when thou hast made an end of dealing treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with thee.

units.leftText: O LORD, be gracious to us! We wait for You. Be our strength every morning and our salvation in time of trouble.
units.rightText: O Jehovah, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee: be thou our arm every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.

units.leftText: The peoples flee the thunder of Your voice; the nations scatter when You rise.
units.rightText: At the noise of the tumult the peoples are fled; at the lifting up of thyself the nations are scattered.

units.leftText: Your spoil, O nations, is gathered as by locusts; like a swarm of locusts men sweep over it.
units.rightText: And your spoil shall be gathered as the caterpillar gathereth: as locusts leap shall men leap upon it.
leftNotes: 33:4 O nations is added for clarity.

units.leftText: The LORD is exalted, for He dwells on high; He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
units.rightText: Jehovah is exalted; for he dwelleth on high: he hath filled Zion with justice and righteousness.

units.leftText: He will be the sure foundation for your times, a storehouse of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. The fear of the LORD is Zion’s treasure.
units.rightText: And there shall be stability in thy times, abundance of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge: the fear of Jehovah is thy treasure.

units.leftText: Behold, their valiant ones cry aloud in the streets; the envoys of peace weep bitterly.
units.rightText: Behold, their valiant ones cry without; the ambassadors of peace weep bitterly.

units.leftText: The highways are deserted; travel has ceased. The treaty has been broken, the witnesses are despised, and human life is disregarded.
units.rightText: The highways lie waste, the wayfaring man ceaseth: the enemy hath broken the covenant, he hath despised the cities, he regardeth not man.
leftNotes: 33:8 Forms of the Hebrew berit are translated in most passages as covenant.
33:8 DSS; MT the cities

units.leftText: The land mourns and languishes; Lebanon is ashamed and decayed. Sharon is like a desert; Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.
units.rightText: The land mourneth and languisheth; Lebanon is confounded and withereth away; Sharon is like a desert; and Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.

units.leftText: “Now I will arise,” says the LORD. “Now I will lift Myself up. Now I will be exalted.
units.rightText: Now will I arise, saith Jehovah; now will I lift up myself; now will I be exalted.

units.leftText: You conceive chaff; you give birth to stubble. Your breath is a fire that will consume you.
units.rightText: Ye shall conceive chaff, ye shall bring forth stubble: your breath is a fire that shall devour you.

units.leftText: The peoples will be burned to ashes, like thorns cut down and set ablaze.
units.rightText: And the peoples shall be as the burnings of lime, as thorns cut down, that are burned in the fire.

units.leftText: You who are far off, hear what I have done; you who are near, acknowledge My might.”
units.rightText: Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done; and, ye that are near, acknowledge my might.

units.leftText: The sinners in Zion are afraid; trembling grips the ungodly: “Who of us can dwell with a consuming fire? Who of us can dwell with everlasting flames?”
units.rightText: The sinners in Zion are afraid; trembling hath seized the godless ones: Who among us can dwell with the devouring fire? who among us can dwell with everlasting burnings?

units.leftText: He who walks righteously and speaks with sincerity, who refuses gain from extortion, whose hand never takes a bribe, who stops his ears against murderous plots and shuts his eyes tightly against evil—
units.rightText: He that walketh righteously, and speaketh uprightly; he that despiseth the gain of oppressions, that shaketh his hands from taking a bribe, that stoppeth his ears from hearing of blood, and shutteth his eyes from looking upon evil:

units.leftText: he will dwell on the heights; the mountain fortress will be his refuge; his food will be provided and his water assured.
units.rightText: He shall dwell on high; his place of defence shall be the munitions of rocks; his bread shall be given him; his waters shall be sure.

units.leftText: Your eyes will see the King in His beauty and behold a land that stretches afar.
units.rightText: Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold a land that reacheth afar.

units.leftText: Your mind will ponder the former terror: “Where is he who tallies? Where is he who weighs? Where is he who counts the towers?”
units.rightText: Thy heart shall muse on the terror: Where is he that counted, where is he that weighed the tribute? where is he that counted the towers?

units.leftText: You will no longer see the insolent, a people whose speech is unintelligible, who stammer in a language you cannot understand.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not see the fierce people, a people of a deep speech that thou canst not comprehend, of a strange tongue that thou canst not understand.

units.leftText: Look upon Zion, the city of our appointed feasts. Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a peaceful pasture, a tent that does not wander; its tent pegs will not be pulled up, nor will any of its cords be broken.
units.rightText: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities: thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, a tent that shall not be removed, the stakes whereof shall never be plucked up, neither shall any of the cords thereof be broken.

units.leftText: But there the Majestic One, our LORD, will be for us a place of rivers and wide canals, where no galley with oars will row, and no majestic vessel will pass.
units.rightText: But there Jehovah will be with us in majesty, a place of broad rivers and streams, wherein shall go no galley with oars, neither shall gallant ship pass thereby.

units.leftText: For the LORD is our Judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our King. It is He who will save us.
units.rightText: For Jehovah is our judge, Jehovah is our lawgiver, Jehovah is our king; he will save us.

units.leftText: Your ropes are slack; they cannot secure the mast or spread the sail. Then an abundance of spoils will be divided, and even the lame will carry off plunder.
units.rightText: Thy tacklings are loosed; they could not strengthen the foot of their mast, they could not spread the sail: then was the prey of a great spoil divided; the lame took the prey.

units.leftText: And no resident of Zion will say, “I am sick.” The people who dwell there will be forgiven of iniquity.
units.rightText: And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick: the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity.

units.leftText: Come near, O nations, to listen; pay attention, O peoples. Let the earth hear, and all that fills it, the world and all that springs from it.
units.rightText: Come near, ye nations, to hear; and hearken, ye peoples: let the earth hear, and the fulness thereof; the world, and all things that come forth from it.

units.leftText: The LORD is angry with all the nations and furious with all their armies. He will devote them to destruction; He will give them over to slaughter.
units.rightText: For Jehovah hath indignation against all the nations, and wrath against all their host: he hath utterly destroyed them, he hath delivered them to the slaughter.
leftNotes: 34:2 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering; also in verse 5.

units.leftText: Their slain will be left unburied, and the stench of their corpses will rise; the mountains will flow with their blood.
units.rightText: Their slain also shall be cast out, and the stench of their dead bodies shall come up; and the mountains shall be melted with their blood.

units.leftText: All the stars of heaven will be dissolved. The skies will be rolled up like a scroll, and all their stars will fall like withered leaves from the vine, like foliage from the fig tree. Judgment on Edom (Isaiah 21:11–12|ISA 21:11-12*)
units.rightText: And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll; and all their host shall fade away, as the leaf fadeth from off the vine, and as a fading leaf from the fig-tree.

units.leftText: When My sword has drunk its fill in the heavens, then it will come down upon Edom, upon the people I have devoted to destruction.
units.rightText: For my sword hath drunk its fill in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Edom, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.

units.leftText: The sword of the LORD is bathed in blood. It drips with fat — with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams. For the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah, a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
units.rightText: The sword of Jehovah is filled with blood, it is made fat with fatness, with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams; for Jehovah hath a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.

units.leftText: And the wild oxen will fall with them, the young bulls with the strong ones. Their land will be drenched with blood, and their soil will be soaked with fat.
units.rightText: And the wild-oxen shall come down with them, and the bullocks with the bulls: and their land shall be drunken with blood, and their dust made fat with fatness.

units.leftText: For the LORD has a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.
units.rightText: For Jehovah hath a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.
leftNotes: 34:8 Or of recompense for (Edom’s) hostility against Zion.

units.leftText: Edom’s streams will be turned to tar, and her soil to sulfur; her land will become a blazing pitch.
units.rightText: And the streams of Edom shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone, and the land thereof shall become burning pitch.

units.leftText: It will not be quenched— day or night. Its smoke will ascend forever. From generation to generation it will lie desolate; no one will ever again pass through it.
units.rightText: It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever; from generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it for ever and ever.

units.leftText: The desert owl and screech owl will possess it, and the great owl and raven will dwell in it. The LORD will stretch out over Edom a measuring line of chaos and a plumb line of destruction.
units.rightText: But the pelican and the porcupine shall possess it; and the owl and the raven shall dwell therein: and he will stretch over it the line of confusion, and the plummet of emptiness.
leftNotes: 34:11 The precise identification of these birds is uncertain.

units.leftText: No nobles will be left to proclaim a king, and all her princes will come to nothing.
units.rightText: They shall call the nobles thereof to the kingdom, but none shall be there; and all its princes shall be nothing.

units.leftText: Her towers will be overgrown with thorns, her fortresses with thistles and briers. She will become a haunt for jackals, an abode for ostriches.
units.rightText: And thorns shall come up in its palaces, nettles and thistles in the fortresses thereof; and it shall be a habitation of jackals, a court for ostriches.
leftNotes: 34:13 Or serpents or dragons
34:13 Literally for daughters of an ostrich or for daughters of an owl

units.leftText: The desert creatures will meet with hyenas, and one wild goat will call to another. There the night creature will settle and find her place of repose.
units.rightText: And the wild beasts of the desert shall meet with the wolves, and the wild goat shall cry to his fellow; yea, the night-monster shall settle there, and shall find her a place of rest.
leftNotes: 34:14 Hebrew Lilith

units.leftText: There the owl will make her nest; she will lay and hatch her eggs and gather her brood under her shadow. Even there the birds of prey will gather, each with its mate.
units.rightText: There shall the dart-snake make her nest, and lay, and hatch, and gather under her shade; yea, there shall the kites be gathered, every one with her mate.

units.leftText: Search and read the scroll of the LORD: Not one of these will go missing, not one will lack her mate, because He has ordered it by His mouth, and He will gather them by His Spirit.
units.rightText: Seek ye out of the book of Jehovah, and read: no one of these shall be missing, none shall want her mate; for my mouth, it hath commanded, and his Spirit, it hath gathered them.

units.leftText: He has allotted their portion; His hand has distributed it by measure. They will possess it forever; they will dwell in it from generation to generation.
units.rightText: And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line: they shall possess it for ever; from generation to generation shall they dwell therein.

units.leftText: The wilderness and the dry land will be glad; the desert will rejoice and blossom like a rose.
units.rightText: The wilderness and the dry land shall be glad; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose.

units.leftText: It will bloom profusely and rejoice with joy and singing. The glory of Lebanon will be given to it, the splendor of Carmel and Sharon. They will see the glory of the LORD, the splendor of our God.
units.rightText: It shall blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing; the glory of Lebanon shall be given unto it, the excellency of Carmel and Sharon: they shall see the glory of Jehovah, the excellency of our God.

units.leftText: Strengthen the limp hands and steady the feeble knees!
units.rightText: Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees.
leftNotes: 35:3 Cited in Hebrews 12:12|HEB 12:12*

units.leftText: Say to those with anxious hearts: “Be strong, do not fear! Behold, your God will come with vengeance. With divine retribution He will come to save you.”
units.rightText: Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come with vengeance, with the recompense of God; he will come and save you.

units.leftText: Then the eyes of the blind will be opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped.
units.rightText: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.

units.leftText: Then the lame will leap like a deer and the mute tongue will shout for joy. For waters will gush forth in the wilderness, and streams in the desert.
units.rightText: Then shall the lame man leap as a hart, and the tongue of the dumb shall sing; for in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert.

units.leftText: The parched ground will become a pool, the thirsty land springs of water. In the haunt where jackals once lay, there will be grass and reeds and papyrus.
units.rightText: And the glowing sand shall become a pool, and the thirsty ground springs of water: in the habitation of jackals, where they lay, shall be grass with reeds and rushes.
leftNotes: 35:7 Or serpents or dragons

units.leftText: And there will be a highway called the Way of Holiness. The unclean will not travel it — only those who walk in the Way — and fools will not stray onto it.
units.rightText: And a highway shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called The way of holiness; the unclean shall not pass over it; but it shall be for the redeemed: the wayfaring men, yea fools, shall not err therein.

units.leftText: No lion will be there, and no vicious beast will go up on it. Such will not be found there, but the redeemed will walk upon it.
units.rightText: No lion shall be there, nor shall any ravenous beast go up thereon; they shall not be found there; but the redeemed shall walk there:

units.leftText: So the redeemed of the LORD will return and enter Zion with singing, crowned with everlasting joy. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee.
units.rightText: and the ransomed of Jehovah shall return, and come with singing unto Zion; and everlasting joy shall be upon their heads: they shall obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.

units.leftText: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked and captured all the fortified cities of Judah.
units.rightText: Now it came to pass in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, that Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah, and took them.

units.leftText: And the king of Assyria sent the Rabshakeh, with a great army, from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem. And he stopped by the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field.
units.rightText: And the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem unto king Hezekiah with a great army. And he stood by the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller’s field.
leftNotes: 36:2 Hebrew Rabshakeh is the title of a high-ranking Assyrian military officer; here and throughout chapters 36 and 37, as well as 2 Kings 18 and 19

units.leftText: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder, went out to him.
units.rightText: Then came forth unto him Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph, the recorder.

units.leftText: The Rabshakeh said to them, “Tell Hezekiah that this is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is the basis of this confidence of yours?
units.rightText: And Rabshakeh said unto them, Say ye now to Hezekiah, Thus saith the great king, the king of Assyria, What confidence is this wherein thou trustest?

units.leftText: You claim to have a strategy and strength for war, but these are empty words. In whom are you now trusting, that you have rebelled against me?
units.rightText: I say, thy counsel and strength for the war are but vain words: now on whom dost thou trust, that thou hast rebelled against me?
leftNotes: 36:5 Literally You speak; see DSS and 2 Kings 18:20|2KI 18:20*; MT I speak.

units.leftText: Look now, you are trusting in Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff that will pierce the hand of anyone who leans on it. Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.
units.rightText: Behold, thou trustest upon the staff of this bruised reed, even upon Egypt, whereon if a man lean, it will go into his hand, and pierce it: so is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all that trust on him.

units.leftText: But if you say to me, ‘We trust in the LORD our God,’ is He not the One whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, ‘You must worship before this altar’?
units.rightText: But if thou say unto me, We trust in Jehovah our God: is not that he, whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah hath taken away, and hath said to Judah and to Jerusalem, Ye shall worship before this altar?

units.leftText: Now, therefore, make a bargain with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you two thousand horses — if you can put riders on them!
units.rightText: Now therefore, I pray thee, give pledges to my master the king of Assyria, and I will give thee two thousand horses, if thou be able on thy part to set riders upon them.

units.leftText: For how can you repel a single officer among the least of my master’s servants when you depend on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
units.rightText: How then canst thou turn away the face of one captain of the least of my master’s servants, and put thy trust on Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?

units.leftText: So now, was it apart from the LORD that I have come up against this land to destroy it? The LORD Himself said to me, ‘Go up against this land and destroy it.’”
units.rightText: And am I now come up without Jehovah against this land to destroy it? Jehovah said unto me, Go up against this land, and destroy it.

units.leftText: Then Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, since we understand it. Do not speak to us in Hebrew in the hearing of the people on the wall.”
units.rightText: Then said Eliakim and Shebna and Joah unto Rabshakeh, Speak, I pray thee, unto thy servants in the Syrian language; for we understand it: and speak not to us in the Jews’ language, in the ears of the people that are on the wall.
leftNotes: 36:11 Or in the dialect of Judah; also in verse 13

units.leftText: But the Rabshakeh replied, “Has my master sent me to speak these words only to you and your master, and not to the men sitting on the wall, who are destined with you to eat their own dung and drink their own urine?”
units.rightText: But Rabshakeh said, Hath my master sent me to thy master, and to thee, to speak these words? hath he not sent me to the men that sit upon the wall, to eat their own dung, and to drink their own water with you?

units.leftText: Then the Rabshakeh stood and called out loudly in Hebrew: “Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
units.rightText: Then Rabshakeh stood, and cried with a loud voice in the Jews’ language, and said, Hear ye the words of the great king, the king of Assyria.

units.leftText: This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he cannot deliver you.
units.rightText: Thus saith the king, Let not Hezekiah deceive you; for he will not be able to deliver you:

units.leftText: Do not let Hezekiah persuade you to trust in the LORD when he says, ‘The LORD will surely deliver us; this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.’
units.rightText: neither let Hezekiah make you trust in Jehovah, saying, Jehovah will surely deliver us; this city shall not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.

units.leftText: Do not listen to Hezekiah, for this is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me. Then every one of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and drink water from his own cistern,
units.rightText: Hearken not to Hezekiah: for thus saith the king of Assyria, Make your peace with me, and come out to me; and eat ye every one of his vine, and every one of his fig-tree, and drink ye every one the waters of his own cistern;
leftNotes: 36:16 Or Make a blessing with me

units.leftText: until I come and take you away to a land like your own— a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
units.rightText: until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.

units.leftText: Do not let Hezekiah mislead you when he says, ‘The LORD will deliver us.’ Has the god of any nation ever delivered his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
units.rightText: Beware lest Hezekiah persuade you, saying, Jehovah will deliver us. Hath any of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?

units.leftText: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Have they delivered Samaria from my hand?
units.rightText: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? where are the gods of Sepharvaim? and have they delivered Samaria out of my hand?

units.leftText: Who among all the gods of these lands has delivered his land from my hand? How then can the LORD deliver Jerusalem from my hand?”
units.rightText: Who are they among all the gods of these countries, that have delivered their country out of my hand, that Jehovah should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?

units.leftText: But the people remained silent and did not answer a word, for Hezekiah had commanded, “Do not answer him.”
units.rightText: But they held their peace, and answered him not a word; for the king’s commandment was, saying, Answer him not.

units.leftText: Then Hilkiah’s son Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and Asaph’s son Joah the recorder came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and they relayed to him the words of the Rabshakeh.
units.rightText: Then came Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, that was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph, the recorder, to Hezekiah with their clothes rent, and told him the words of Rabshakeh.

units.leftText: On hearing this report, King Hezekiah tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and entered the house of the LORD.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when king Hezekiah heard it, that he rent his clothes, and covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of Jehovah.

units.leftText: And he sent Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and the leading priests, all wearing sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz
units.rightText: And he sent Eliakim, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, unto Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz.

units.leftText: to tell him, “This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of distress, rebuke, and disgrace; for children have come to the point of birth, but there is no strength to deliver them.
units.rightText: And they said unto him, Thus saith Hezekiah, This day is a day of trouble, and of rebuke, and of contumely; for the children are come to the birth, and there is not strength to bring forth.

units.leftText: Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to defy the living God, and He will rebuke him for the words that the LORD your God has heard. Therefore lift up a prayer for the remnant that still survives.”
units.rightText: It may be Jehovah thy God will hear the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master hath sent to defy the living God, and will rebuke the words which Jehovah thy God hath heard: wherefore lift up thy prayer for the remnant that is left.

units.leftText: So the servants of King Hezekiah went to Isaiah,
units.rightText: So the servants of king Hezekiah came to Isaiah.

units.leftText: who replied, “Tell your master that this is what the LORD says: ‘Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed Me.
units.rightText: And Isaiah said unto them, Thus shall ye say to your master, Thus saith Jehovah, Be not afraid of the words that thou hast heard, wherewith the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.

units.leftText: Behold, I will put a spirit in him so that he will hear a rumor and return to his own land, where I will cause him to fall by the sword.’” Sennacherib’s Blasphemous Letter (2 Kings 19:8–13|2KI 19:8-13*)
units.rightText: Behold, I will put a spirit in him, and he shall hear tidings, and shall return unto his own land; and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.

units.leftText: When the Rabshakeh heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish, he withdrew and found the king fighting against Libnah.
units.rightText: So Rabshakeh returned, and found the king of Assyria warring against Libnah; for he had heard that he was departed from Lachish.

units.leftText: Now Sennacherib had been warned about Tirhakah king of Cush: “He has set out to fight against you.”
units.rightText: And he heard say concerning Tirhakah king of Ethiopia, He is come out to fight against thee. And when he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
leftNotes: 37:9 That is, the upper Nile region

units.leftText: “Give this message to Hezekiah king of Judah:
units.rightText: Thus shall ye speak to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying, Let not thy God in whom thou trustest deceive thee, saying, Jerusalem shall not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.

units.leftText: Surely you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the other countries, devoting them to destruction. Will you then be spared?
units.rightText: Behold, thou hast heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, by destroying them utterly: and shalt thou be delivered?
leftNotes: 37:11 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering.

units.leftText: Did the gods of the nations destroyed by my fathers rescue those nations— the gods of Gozan, Haran, and Rezeph, and of the people of Eden in Telassar?
units.rightText: Have the gods of the nations delivered them, which my fathers have destroyed, Gozan, and Haran, and Rezeph, and the children of Eden that were in Telassar?

units.leftText: Where are the kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?’” Hezekiah’s Prayer (2 Kings 19:14–19|2KI 19:14-19*)
units.rightText: Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivvah?

units.leftText: So Hezekiah received the letter from the messengers, read it, and went up to the house of the LORD and spread it out before the LORD.
units.rightText: And Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers, and read it; and Hezekiah went up unto the house of Jehovah, and spread it before Jehovah.

units.leftText: And Hezekiah prayed to the LORD:
units.rightText: And Hezekiah prayed unto Jehovah, saying,

units.leftText: “O LORD of Hosts, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.
units.rightText: O Jehovah of hosts, the God of Israel, that sittest above the cherubim, thou art the God, even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; thou hast made heaven and earth.

units.leftText: Incline Your ear, O LORD, and hear; open Your eyes, O LORD, and see. Listen to all the words that Sennacherib has sent to defy the living God.
units.rightText: Incline thine ear, O Jehovah, and hear; open thine eyes, O Jehovah, and see; and hear all the words of Sennacherib, who hath sent to defy the living God.

units.leftText: Truly, O LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all these countries and their lands.
units.rightText: Of a truth, Jehovah, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the countries, and their land,

units.leftText: They have cast their gods into the fire and destroyed them, for they were not gods, but only wood and stone — the work of human hands.
units.rightText: and have cast their gods into the fire: for they were no gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone; therefore they have destroyed them.

units.leftText: And now, O LORD our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone, O LORD, are God. ” Sennacherib’s Fall Prophesied (2 Kings 19:20–34|2KI 19:20-34*)
units.rightText: Now therefore, O Jehovah our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that thou art Jehovah, even thou only.
leftNotes: 37:20 DSS (see also 2 Kings 19:19|2KI 19:19*); MT You alone are the LORD

units.leftText: Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent a message to Hezekiah: “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Because you have prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria,
units.rightText: Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent unto Hezekiah, saying, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, Whereas thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria,

units.leftText: this is the word that the LORD has spoken against him: ‘The Virgin Daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you; the Daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head behind you.
units.rightText: this is the word which Jehovah hath spoken concerning him: The virgin daughter of Zion hath despised thee and laughed thee to scorn; the daughter of Jerusalem hath shaken her head at thee.

units.leftText: Whom have you taunted and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes in pride? Against the Holy One of Israel!
units.rightText: Whom hast thou defied and blasphemed? and against whom hast thou exalted thy voice and lifted up thine eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: Through your servants you have taunted the Lord, and you have said: “With my many chariots I have ascended to the heights of the mountains, to the remote peaks of Lebanon. I have cut down its tallest cedars, the finest of its cypresses. I have reached its farthest heights, the densest of its forests.
units.rightText: By thy servants hast thou defied the Lord, and hast said, With the multitude of my chariots am I come up to the height of the mountains, to the innermost parts of Lebanon; and I will cut down the tall cedars thereof, and the choice fir-trees thereof; and I will enter into its farthest height, the forest of its fruitful field;
leftNotes: 37:24 Or pines or junipers or firs

units.leftText: I have dug wells and drunk foreign waters. With the soles of my feet I have dried up all the streams of Egypt.”
units.rightText: I have digged and drunk water, and with the sole of my feet will I dry up all the rivers of Egypt.
leftNotes: 37:25 DSS (see also 2 Kings 19:24|2KI 19:24*); MT does not include foreign.

units.leftText: Have you not heard? Long ago I ordained it; in days of old I planned it. Now I have brought it to pass, that you should crush fortified cities into piles of rubble.
units.rightText: Hast thou not heard how I have done it long ago, and formed it of ancient times? now have I brought it to pass, that it should be thine to lay waste fortified cities into ruinous heaps.

units.leftText: Therefore their inhabitants, devoid of power, are dismayed and ashamed. They are like plants in the field, tender green shoots, grass on the rooftops, scorched before it is grown.
units.rightText: Therefore their inhabitants were of small power, they were dismayed and confounded; they were as the grass of the field, and as the green herb, as the grass on the housetops, and as a field of grain before it is grown up.
leftNotes: 37:27 DSS, some MT manuscripts, and some LXX manuscripts (see also 2 Kings 19:26|2KI 19:26*); most MT manuscripts on the rooftops and terraced fields

units.leftText: But I know your sitting down, your going out and coming in, and your raging against Me.
units.rightText: But I know thy sitting down, and thy going out, and thy coming in, and thy raging against me.

units.leftText: Because your rage and arrogance against Me have reached My ears, I will put My hook in your nose and My bit in your mouth; I will send you back the way you came.’
units.rightText: Because of thy raging against me, and because thine arrogancy is come up into mine ears, therefore will I put my hook in thy nose, and my bridle in thy lips, and I will turn thee back by the way by which thou camest.

units.leftText: And this will be a sign to you, O Hezekiah: This year you will eat what grows on its own, and in the second year what springs from the same. But in the third year you will sow and reap; you will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
units.rightText: And this shall be the sign unto thee: ye shall eat this year that which groweth of itself, and in the second year that which springeth of the same; and in the third year sow ye, and reap, and plant vineyards, and eat the fruit thereof.

units.leftText: And the surviving remnant of the house of Judah will again take root below and bear fruit above.
units.rightText: And the remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah shall again take root downward, and bear fruit upward.

units.leftText: For a remnant will go forth from Jerusalem, and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this.
units.rightText: For out of Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant, and out of mount Zion they that shall escape. The zeal of Jehovah of hosts will perform this.

units.leftText: So this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: ‘He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow into it. He will not come before it with a shield or build up a siege ramp against it.
units.rightText: Therefore thus saith Jehovah concerning the king of Assyria, He shall not come unto this city, nor shoot an arrow there, neither shall he come before it with shield, nor cast up a mound against it.

units.leftText: He will go back the way he came, and he will not enter this city,’ declares the LORD.
units.rightText: By the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and he shall not come unto this city, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: ‘I will defend this city and save it for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David.’” Jerusalem Delivered from the Assyrians (2 Kings 19:35–37|2KI 19:35-37*; 2 Chronicles 32:20–23|2CH 32:20-23*)
units.rightText: For I will defend this city to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.

units.leftText: Then the angel of the LORD went out and struck down 185,000 men in the camp of the Assyrians. When the people got up the next morning, there were all the dead bodies!
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand; and when men arose early in the morning, behold, these were all dead bodies.
leftNotes: 37:36 Hebrew When they got up
