units.leftText: So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and withdrew. He returned to Nineveh and stayed there.
units.rightText: So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh.

units.leftText: One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer put him to the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. And his son Esar-haddon reigned in his place.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Ararat. And Esar-haddon his son reigned in his stead.

units.leftText: In those days Hezekiah became mortally ill. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Put your house in order, for you are about to die; you will not recover.’”
units.rightText: In those days was Hezekiah sick unto death. And Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz came to him, and said unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, Set thy house in order; for thou shalt die, and not live.

units.leftText: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD,
units.rightText: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall, and prayed unto Jehovah,

units.leftText: saying, “Please, O LORD, remember how I have walked before You faithfully and with wholehearted devotion; I have done what is good in Your sight.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
units.rightText: and said, Remember now, O Jehovah, I beseech thee, how I have walked before thee in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in thy sight. And Hezekiah wept sore.

units.leftText: And the word of the LORD came to Isaiah, saying,
units.rightText: Then came the word of Jehovah to Isaiah, saying,

units.leftText: “Go and tell Hezekiah that this is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: ‘I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Behold, I will add fifteen years to your life.
units.rightText: Go, and say to Hezekiah, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of David thy father, I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tears: behold, I will add unto thy days fifteen years.

units.leftText: And I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria. I will defend this city.
units.rightText: And I will deliver thee and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria; and I will defend this city.
leftNotes: 38:6 MT and LXX; DSS includes for My sake and for the sake of My servant David; see 2 Kings 20:6|2KI 20:6*.

units.leftText: This will be a sign to you from the LORD that He will do what He has promised:
units.rightText: And this shall be the sign unto thee from Jehovah, that Jehovah will do this thing that he hath spoken:

units.leftText: I will make the sun’s shadow that falls on the stairway of Ahaz go back ten steps.’” So the sunlight went back the ten steps it had descended. Hezekiah’s Song of Thanksgiving
units.rightText: behold, I will cause the shadow on the steps, which is gone down on the dial of Ahaz with the sun, to return backward ten steps. So the sun returned ten steps on the dial whereon it was gone down.

units.leftText: This is a writing by Hezekiah king of Judah after his illness and recovery:
units.rightText: The writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he had been sick, and was recovered of his sickness.

units.leftText: I said, “In the prime of my life I must go through the gates of Sheol and be deprived of the remainder of my years.”
units.rightText: I said, In the noontide of my days I shall go into the gates of Sheol: I am deprived of the residue of my years.
leftNotes: 38:10 Or In the quiet or In the middle

units.leftText: I said, “I will never again see the LORD, even the LORD, in the land of the living; I will no longer look on mankind with those who dwell in this world.
units.rightText: I said, I shall not see Jehovah, even Jehovah in the land of the living: I shall behold man no more with the inhabitants of the world.

units.leftText: My dwelling has been picked up and removed from me like a shepherd’s tent. I have rolled up my life like a weaver; He cuts me off from the loom; from day until night You make an end of me.
units.rightText: My dwelling is removed, and is carried away from me as a shepherd’s tent: I have rolled up, like a weaver, my life; he will cut me off from the loom: From day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.

units.leftText: I composed myself until the morning. Like a lion He breaks all my bones; from day until night You make an end of me.
units.rightText: I quieted myself until morning; as a lion, so he breaketh all my bones: From day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.
leftNotes: 38:13 Or I cried out; see Targum Yonaton.

units.leftText: I chirp like a swallow or crane; I moan like a dove. My eyes grow weak as I look upward. O Lord, I am oppressed; be my security.”
units.rightText: Like a swallow or a crane, so did I chatter; I did moan as a dove; mine eyes fail with looking upward: O Lord, I am oppressed, be thou my surety.

units.leftText: What can I say? He has spoken to me, and He Himself has done this. I will walk slowly all my years because of the anguish of my soul.
units.rightText: What shall I say? he hath both spoken unto me, and himself hath done it: I shall go softly all my years because of the bitterness of my soul.

units.leftText: O Lord, by such things men live, and in all of them my spirit finds life. You have restored me to health and have let me live.
units.rightText: O Lord, by these things men live; And wholly therein is the life of my spirit: Wherefore recover thou me, and make me to live.

units.leftText: Surely for my own welfare I had such great anguish; but Your love has delivered me from the pit of oblivion, for You have cast all my sins behind Your back.
units.rightText: Behold, it was for my peace that I had great bitterness: But thou hast in love to my soul delivered it from the pit of corruption; For thou hast cast all my sins behind thy back.

units.leftText: For Sheol cannot thank You; Death cannot praise You. Those who descend to the Pit cannot hope for Your faithfulness.
units.rightText: For Sheol cannot praise thee, death cannot celebrate thee: They that go down into the pit cannot hope for thy truth.

units.leftText: The living, only the living, can thank You, as I do today; fathers will tell their children about Your faithfulness.
units.rightText: The living, the living, he shall praise thee, as I do this day: The father to the children shall make known thy truth.

units.leftText: The LORD will save me; we will play songs on stringed instruments all the days of our lives in the house of the LORD.
units.rightText: Jehovah is ready to save me: Therefore we will sing my songs with stringed instruments All the days of our life in the house of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Now Isaiah had said, “Prepare a lump of pressed figs and apply it to the boil, and he will recover.”
units.rightText: Now Isaiah had said, Let them take a cake of figs, and lay it for a plaster upon the boil, and he shall recover.

units.leftText: And Hezekiah had asked, “What will be the sign that I will go up to the house of the LORD?”
units.rightText: Hezekiah also had said, What is the sign that I shall go up to the house of Jehovah?

units.leftText: At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan king of Babylon sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard about Hezekiah’s illness and recovery.
units.rightText: At that time Merodach-baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah; for he heard that he had been sick, and was recovered.

units.leftText: And Hezekiah welcomed the envoys gladly and showed them what was in his treasure house — the silver, the gold, the spices, and the precious oil, as well as his entire armory — all that was found in his storehouses. There was nothing in his palace or in all his dominion that Hezekiah did not show them.
units.rightText: And Hezekiah was glad of them, and showed them the house of his precious things, the silver, and the gold, and the spices, and the precious oil, and all the house of his armor, and all that was found in his treasures: there was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah showed them not.

units.leftText: Then the prophet Isaiah went to King Hezekiah and asked, “Where did those men come from, and what did they say to you?” “They came to me from a distant land,” Hezekiah replied, “from Babylon.”
units.rightText: Then came Isaiah the prophet unto king Hezekiah, and said unto him, What said these men? and from whence came they unto thee? And Hezekiah said, They are come from a far country unto me, even from Babylon.

units.leftText: “What have they seen in your palace?” Isaiah asked. “They have seen everything in my palace,” answered Hezekiah. “There is nothing among my treasures that I did not show them.”
units.rightText: Then said he, What have they seen in thy house? And Hezekiah answered, All that is in my house have they seen: there is nothing among my treasures that I have not showed them.

units.leftText: Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the LORD of Hosts:
units.rightText: Then said Isaiah to Hezekiah, Hear the word of Jehovah of hosts:

units.leftText: The time will surely come when everything in your palace and all that your fathers have stored up until this day will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left, says the LORD.
units.rightText: Behold, the days are coming, when all that is in thy house, and that which thy fathers have laid up in store until this day, shall be carried to Babylon: nothing shall be left, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: And some of your descendants, your own flesh and blood, will be taken away to be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.”
units.rightText: And of thy sons that shall issue from thee, whom thou shalt beget, shall they take away; and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.

units.leftText: But Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good.” For he thought, “At least there will be peace and security in my lifetime.”
units.rightText: Then said Hezekiah unto Isaiah, Good is the word of Jehovah which thou hast spoken. He said moreover, For there shall be peace and truth in my days.

units.leftText: “Comfort, comfort My people,” says your God.
units.rightText: Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God.

units.leftText: “Speak tenderly to Jerusalem, and proclaim to her that her forced labor has been completed; her iniquity has been pardoned. For she has received from the hand of the LORD double for all her sins.”
units.rightText: Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem; and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she hath received of Jehovah’s hand double for all her sins.

units.leftText: A voice of one calling: “Prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness; make a straight highway for our God in the desert.
units.rightText: The voice of one that crieth, Prepare ye in the wilderness the way of Jehovah; make level in the desert a highway for our God.
leftNotes: 40:3 Or A voice of one calling in the wilderness: “Prepare the way for the LORD
40:3 LXX make straight the paths of our God; cited in Matthew 3:3|MAT 3:3*, Mark 1:3, Luke 3:4, and John 1:23

units.leftText: Every valley shall be lifted up, and every mountain and hill made low; the uneven ground will become smooth, and the rugged land a plain.
units.rightText: Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low; and the uneven shall be made level, and the rough places a plain:
leftNotes: 40:4 LXX Every valley shall be filled in, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low. All the crooked ways shall become straight, and the rough places plains.Cited in Luke 3:5|LUK 3:5*

units.leftText: And the glory of the LORD will be revealed, and all humanity together will see it.” For the mouth of the LORD has spoken. The Enduring Word (1 Peter 1:22–25|1PE 1:22-25*)
units.rightText: and the glory of Jehovah shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together; for the mouth of Jehovah hath spoken it.
leftNotes: 40:5 Literally and all flesh together will see it.Cited in Luke 3:6|LUK 3:6*

units.leftText: A voice says, “Cry out!” And I asked, “What should I cry out?” “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field.
units.rightText: The voice of one saying, Cry. And one said, What shall I cry? All flesh is grass, and all the goodliness thereof is as the flower of the field.

units.leftText: The grass withers and the flowers fall when the breath of the LORD blows on them; indeed, the people are grass.
units.rightText: The grass withereth, the flower fadeth, because the breath of Jehovah bloweth upon it; surely the people is grass.

units.leftText: The grass withers and the flowers fall, but the word of our God stands forever.” Here Is Your God! (Romans 11:33–36|ROM 11:33-36*)
units.rightText: The grass withereth, the flower fadeth; but the word of our God shall stand forever.

units.leftText: Go up on a high mountain, O Zion, herald of good news. Raise your voice loudly, O Jerusalem, herald of good news. Lift it up, do not be afraid! Say to the cities of Judah, “Here is your God!”
units.rightText: O thou that tellest good tidings to Zion, get thee up on a high mountain; O thou that tellest good tidings to Jerusalem, lift up thy voice with strength; lift it up, be not afraid; say unto the cities of Judah, Behold, your God!
leftNotes: 40:9 Or O herald of good news to Zion, go up on a high mountain. O herald of good news to Jerusalem, lift it up,

units.leftText: Behold, the Lord GOD comes with might, and His arm establishes His rule. His reward is with Him, and His recompense accompanies Him.
units.rightText: Behold, the Lord Jehovah will come as a mighty one, and his arm will rule for him: Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.

units.leftText: He tends His flock like a shepherd; He gathers the lambs in His arms and carries them close to His heart. He gently leads the nursing ewes.
units.rightText: He will feed his flock like a shepherd, he will gather the lambs in his arm, and carry them in his bosom, and will gently lead those that have their young.

units.leftText: Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, or marked off the heavens with the span of his hand? Who has held the dust of the earth in a basket, or weighed the mountains on a scale and the hills with a balance?
units.rightText: Who hath measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and meted out heaven with the span, and comprehended the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance?

units.leftText: Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD, or informed Him as His counselor?
units.rightText: Who hath directed the Spirit of Jehovah, or being his counsellor hath taught him?
leftNotes: 40:13 Or mind of the LORD; see also LXX.
40:13 Cited in Romans 11:34|ROM 11:34* and 1 Corinthians 2:16

units.leftText: Whom did He consult to enlighten Him, and who taught Him the paths of justice? Who imparted knowledge to Him and showed Him the way of understanding?
units.rightText: With whom took he counsel, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of justice, and taught him knowledge, and showed to him the way of understanding?

units.leftText: Surely the nations are like a drop in a bucket; they are considered a speck of dust on the scales; He lifts up the islands like fine dust.
units.rightText: Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket, and are accounted as the small dust of the balance: behold, he taketh up the isles as a very little thing.
leftNotes: 40:15 Or coastlands

units.leftText: Lebanon is not sufficient for fuel, nor its animals enough for a burnt offering.
units.rightText: And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt-offering.

units.leftText: All the nations are as nothing before Him; He regards them as nothingness and emptiness.
units.rightText: All the nations are as nothing before him; they are accounted by him as less than nothing, and vanity.

units.leftText: To whom will you liken God? To what image will you compare Him?
units.rightText: To whom then will ye liken God? or what likeness will ye compare unto him?

units.leftText: To an idol that a craftsman casts and a metalworker overlays with gold and fits with silver chains?
units.rightText: The image, a workman hath cast it, and the goldsmith overlayeth it with gold, and casteth for it silver chains.

units.leftText: One lacking such an offering chooses wood that will not rot. He seeks a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not topple.
units.rightText: He that is too impoverished for such an oblation chooseth a tree that will not rot; he seeketh unto him a skilful workman to set up a graven image, that shall not be moved.

units.leftText: Do you not know? Have you not heard? Has it not been declared to you from the beginning? Have you not understood since the foundation of the earth?
units.rightText: Have ye not known? have ye not heard? hath it not been told you from the beginning? have ye not understood from the foundations of the earth?

units.leftText: He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth; its dwellers are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in.
units.rightText: It is he that sitteth above the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants thereof are as grasshoppers; that stretcheth out the heavens as a curtain, and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in;

units.leftText: He brings the princes to nothing and makes the rulers of the earth meaningless.
units.rightText: that bringeth princes to nothing; that maketh the judges of the earth as vanity.
leftNotes: 40:23 Or judges

units.leftText: No sooner are they planted, no sooner are they sown, no sooner have their stems taken root in the ground, than He blows on them and they wither, and a whirlwind sweeps them away like stubble.
units.rightText: Yea, they have not been planted; yea, they have not been sown; yea, their stock hath not taken root in the earth: moreover he bloweth upon them, and they wither, and the whirlwind taketh them away as stubble.

units.leftText: “To whom will you liken Me, or who is My equal?” asks the Holy One.
units.rightText: To whom then will ye liken me, that I should be equal to him? saith the Holy One.

units.leftText: Lift up your eyes on high: Who created all these? He leads forth the starry host by number; He calls each one by name. Because of His great power and mighty strength, not one of them is missing.
units.rightText: Lift up your eyes on high, and see who hath created these, that bringeth out their host by number; he calleth them all by name; by the greatness of his might, and for that he is strong in power, not one is lacking.

units.leftText: Why do you say, O Jacob, and why do you assert, O Israel, “My way is hidden from the LORD, and my claim is ignored by my God”?
units.rightText: Why sayest thou, O Jacob, and speakest, O Israel, My way is hid from Jehovah, and the justice due to me is passed away from my God?

units.leftText: Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He will not grow tired or weary; His understanding is beyond searching out.
units.rightText: Hast thou not known? hast thou not heard? The everlasting God, Jehovah, the Creator of the ends of the earth, fainteth not, neither is weary; there is no searching of his understanding.

units.leftText: He gives power to the faint and increases the strength of the weak.
units.rightText: He giveth power to the faint; and to him that hath no might he increaseth strength.

units.leftText: Even youths grow tired and weary, and young men stumble and fall.
units.rightText: Even the youths shall faint and be weary, and the young men shall utterly fall:

units.leftText: But those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength; they will mount up with wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not faint.
units.rightText: but they that wait for Jehovah shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; they shall walk, and not faint.

units.leftText: “Be silent before Me, O islands, and let the peoples renew their strength. Let them come forward and testify; let us together draw near for judgment.
units.rightText: Keep silence before me, O islands; and let the peoples renew their strength: let them come near; then let them speak; let us come near together to judgment.
leftNotes: 41:1 Or coastlands; also in verse 5

units.leftText: Who has aroused one from the east and called him to his feet in righteousness ? He hands nations over to him and subdues kings before him. He turns them to dust with his sword, to windblown chaff with his bow.
units.rightText: Who hath raised up one from the east, whom he calleth in righteousness to his foot? he giveth nations before him, and maketh him rule over kings; he giveth them as the dust to his sword, as the driven stubble to his bow.
leftNotes: 41:2 Or from the east, whom victory meets at every step

units.leftText: He pursues them, going on safely, hardly touching the path with his feet.
units.rightText: He pursueth them, and passeth on safely, even by a way that he had not gone with his feet.

units.leftText: Who has performed this and carried it out, calling forth the generations from the beginning? I, the LORD — the first and the last— I am He.”
units.rightText: Who hath wrought and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, Jehovah, the first, and with the last, I am he.

units.leftText: The islands see and fear; the ends of the earth tremble. They approach and come forward.
units.rightText: The isles have seen, and fear; the ends of the earth tremble; they draw near, and come.

units.leftText: Each one helps the other and says to his brother, “Be strong!”
units.rightText: They help every one his neighbor; and every one saith to his brother, Be of good courage.

units.leftText: The craftsman encourages the goldsmith, and he who wields the hammer cheers him who strikes the anvil, saying of the welding, “It is good.” He nails it down so it will not be toppled.
units.rightText: So the carpenter encourageth the goldsmith, and he that smootheth with the hammer him that smiteth the anvil, saying of the soldering, It is good; and he fasteneth it with nails, that it should not be moved.

units.leftText: “But you, O Israel, My servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, descendant of Abraham My friend—
units.rightText: But thou, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend,

units.leftText: I brought you from the ends of the earth and called you from its farthest corners. I said, ‘You are My servant.’ I have chosen and not rejected you.
units.rightText: thou whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth, and called from the corners thereof, and said unto thee, Thou art my servant, I have chosen thee and not cast thee away;

units.leftText: Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be afraid, for I am your God. I will strengthen you; I will surely help you; I will uphold you with My righteous right hand.
units.rightText: fear thou not, for I am with thee; be not dismayed, for I am thy God; I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.

units.leftText: Behold, all who rage against you will be ashamed and disgraced; those who contend with you will be reduced to nothing and will perish.
units.rightText: Behold, all they that are incensed against thee shall be put to shame and confounded: they that strive with thee shall be as nothing, and shall perish.

units.leftText: You will seek them but will not find them. Those who wage war against you will come to nothing.
units.rightText: Thou shalt seek them, and shalt not find them, even them that contend with thee: they that war against thee shall be as nothing, and as a thing of nought.

units.leftText: For I am the LORD your God, who takes hold of your right hand and tells you: Do not fear, I will help you.
units.rightText: For I, Jehovah thy God, will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee.

units.leftText: Do not fear, O Jacob, you worm, O few men of Israel. I will help you,” declares the LORD. “Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
units.rightText: Fear not, thou worm Jacob, and ye men of Israel; I will help thee, saith Jehovah, and thy Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: Behold, I will make you into a threshing sledge, new and sharp, with many teeth. You will thresh the mountains and crush them, and reduce the hills to chaff.
units.rightText: Behold, I have made thee to be a new sharp threshing instrument having teeth; thou shalt thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and shalt make the hills as chaff.

units.leftText: You will winnow them, and a wind will carry them away; a gale will scatter them. But you will rejoice in the LORD; you will glory in the Holy One of Israel.
units.rightText: Thou shalt winnow them, and the wind shall carry them away, and the whirlwind shall scatter them; and thou shalt rejoice in Jehovah, thou shalt glory in the Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: The poor and needy seek water, but there is none; their tongues are parched with thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.
units.rightText: The poor and needy seek water, and there is none, and their tongue faileth for thirst; I, Jehovah, will answer them, I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.

units.leftText: I will open rivers on the barren heights, and fountains in the middle of the valleys. I will turn the desert into a pool of water, and the dry land into flowing springs.
units.rightText: I will open rivers on the bare heights, and fountains in the midst of the valleys; I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water.

units.leftText: I will plant cedars in the wilderness, acacias, myrtles, and olive trees. I will set cypresses in the desert, elms and boxwood together,
units.rightText: I will put in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia, and the myrtle, and the oil-tree; I will set in the desert the fir-tree, the pine, and the box-tree together:
leftNotes: 41:19 Or pines or junipers or firs

units.leftText: so that all may see and know, may consider and understand, that the hand of the LORD has done this and the Holy One of Israel has created it.” Meaningless Idols
units.rightText: that they may see, and know, and consider, and understand together, that the hand of Jehovah hath done this, and the Holy One of Israel hath created it.

units.leftText: “Present your case,” says the LORD. “Submit your arguments,” says the King of Jacob.
units.rightText: Produce your cause, saith Jehovah; bring forth your strong reasons, saith the King of Jacob.

units.leftText: “Let them come and tell us what will happen. Tell the former things, so that we may reflect on them and know the outcome. Or announce to us what is coming.
units.rightText: Let them bring forth, and declare unto us what shall happen: declare ye the former things, what they are, that we may consider them, and know the latter end of them; or show us things to come.

units.leftText: Tell us the things that are to come, so that we may know that you are gods. Yes, do something good or evil, that we may look on together in dismay.
units.rightText: Declare the things that are to come hereafter, that we may know that ye are gods: yea, do good, or do evil, that we may be dismayed, and behold it together.

units.leftText: Behold, you are nothing and your work is of no value. Anyone who chooses you is detestable.
units.rightText: Behold, ye are of nothing, and your work is of nought; an abomination is he that chooseth you.

units.leftText: I have raised up one from the north, and he has come — one from the east who calls on My name. He will march over rulers as if they were mortar, like a potter who treads the clay.
units.rightText: I have raised up one from the north, and he is come; from the rising of the sun one that calleth upon my name: and he shall come upon rulers as upon mortar, and as the potter treadeth clay.

units.leftText: Who has declared this from the beginning, so that we may know, and from times past, so that we may say: ‘He was right’? No one announced it, no one foretold it, no one heard your words.
units.rightText: Who hath declared it from the beginning, that we may know? and beforetime, that we may say, He is right? yea, there is none that declareth, yea, there is none that showeth, yea, there is none that heareth your words.

units.leftText: I was the first to tell Zion: ‘Look, here they are!’ And I gave to Jerusalem a herald of good news.
units.rightText: I am the first that saith unto Zion, Behold, behold them; and I will give to Jerusalem one that bringeth good tidings.
leftNotes: 41:27 Or Formerly I said to Zion:

units.leftText: When I look, there is no one; there is no counselor among them; when I ask them, they have nothing to say.
units.rightText: And when I look, there is no man: even among them there is no counsellor, that, when I ask of them, can answer a word.

units.leftText: See, they are all a delusion; their works amount to nothing; their images are as empty as the wind.[’’]
units.rightText: Behold, all of them, their works are vanity and nought; their molten images are wind and confusion.

units.leftText: “Here is My Servant, whom I uphold, My Chosen One, in whom My soul delights. I will put My Spirit on Him, and He will bring justice to the nations.
units.rightText: Behold, my servant, whom I uphold; my chosen, in whom my soul delighteth: I have put my Spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the Gentiles.

units.leftText: He will not cry out or raise His voice, nor make His voice heard in the streets.
units.rightText: He will not cry, nor lift up his voice, nor cause it to be heard in the street.

units.leftText: A bruised reed He will not break and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish; He will faithfully bring forth justice.
units.rightText: A bruised reed will he not break, and a dimly burning wick will he not quench: he will bring forth justice in truth.

units.leftText: He will not grow weak or discouraged before He has established justice on the earth. In His law the islands will put their hope.”
units.rightText: He will not fail nor be discouraged, till he have set justice in the earth; and the isles shall wait for his law.
leftNotes: 42:4 Or bruised
42:4 Or In His teaching the coastlands will put their hope; LXX In His name the nations will put their hope; cited in Matthew 12:18–21|MAT 12:18-21*

units.leftText: This is what God the LORD says— He who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and its offspring, who gives breath to the people on it and life to those who walk in it:
units.rightText: Thus saith God Jehovah, he that created the heavens, and stretched them forth; he that spread abroad the earth and that which cometh out of it; he that giveth breath unto the people upon it, and spirit to them that walk therein:

units.leftText: “I, the LORD, have called you for a righteous purpose, and I will take hold of your hand. I will keep you and appoint you to be a covenant for the people and a light to the nations,
units.rightText: I, Jehovah, have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thy hand, and will keep thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles;

units.leftText: to open the eyes of the blind, to bring prisoners out of the dungeon and those sitting in darkness out from the prison house.
units.rightText: to open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the dungeon, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison-house.

units.leftText: I am the LORD; that is My name! I will not yield My glory to another or My praise to idols.
units.rightText: I am Jehovah, that is my name; and my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise unto graven images.

units.leftText: Behold, the former things have happened, and now I declare new things. Before they spring forth I proclaim them to you.” A New Song of Praise (Psalm 98:1–9|PSA 98:1-9*; Psalm 149:1–9|PSA 149:1-9*)
units.rightText: Behold, the former things are come to pass, and new things do I declare; before they spring forth I tell you of them.

units.leftText: Sing to the LORD a new song— His praise from the ends of the earth— you who go down to the sea, and all that is in it, you islands, and all who dwell in them.
units.rightText: Sing unto Jehovah a new song, and his praise from the end of the earth; ye that go down to the sea, and all that is therein, the isles, and the inhabitants thereof.
leftNotes: 42:10 Or coastlands; also in verse 12

units.leftText: Let the desert and its cities raise their voices; let the villages of Kedar cry aloud. Let the people of Sela sing for joy; let them cry out from the mountaintops.
units.rightText: Let the wilderness and the cities thereof lift up their voice, the villages that Kedar doth inhabit; let the inhabitants of Sela sing, let them shout from the top of the mountains.

units.leftText: Let them give glory to the LORD and declare His praise in the islands.
units.rightText: Let them give glory unto Jehovah, and declare his praise in the islands.

units.leftText: The LORD goes forth like a mighty one; He stirs up His zeal like a warrior. He shouts; yes, He roars in triumph over His enemies:
units.rightText: Jehovah will go forth as a mighty man; he will stir up his zeal like a man of war: he will cry, yea, he will shout aloud; he will do mightily against his enemies.

units.leftText: “I have kept silent from ages past; I have remained quiet and restrained. But now I will groan like a woman in labor; I will at once gasp and pant.
units.rightText: I have long time holden my peace; I have been still, and refrained myself: now will I cry out like a travailing woman; I will gasp and pant together.

units.leftText: I will lay waste the mountains and hills and dry up all their vegetation. I will turn the rivers into dry land and drain the marshes.
units.rightText: I will lay waste mountains and hills, and dry up all their herbs; and I will make the rivers islands, and will dry up the pools.
leftNotes: 42:15 Or coastlands or islands

units.leftText: I will lead the blind by a way they did not know; I will guide them on unfamiliar paths. I will turn darkness into light before them and rough places into level ground. These things I will do for them, and I will not forsake them.
units.rightText: And I will bring the blind by a way that they know not; in paths that they know not will I lead them; I will make darkness light before them, and crooked places straight. These things will I do, and I will not forsake them.

units.leftText: But those who trust in idols and say to molten images, ‘You are our gods!’ will be turned back in utter shame. Israel Is Deaf and Blind
units.rightText: They shall be turned back, they shall be utterly put to shame, that trust in graven images, that say unto molten images, Ye are our gods.

units.leftText: Listen, you deaf ones; look, you blind ones, that you may see!
units.rightText: Hear, ye deaf; and look, ye blind, that ye may see.

units.leftText: Who is blind but My servant, or deaf like the messenger I am sending? Who is blind like My covenant partner, or blind like the servant of the LORD?
units.rightText: Who is blind, but my servant? or deaf, as my messenger that I send? who is blind as he that is at peace with me, and blind as Jehovah’s servant?

units.leftText: Though seeing many things, you do not keep watch. Though your ears are open, you do not hear.”
units.rightText: Thou seest many things, but thou observest not; his ears are open, but he heareth not.

units.leftText: The LORD was pleased, for the sake of His righteousness, to magnify His law and make it glorious.
units.rightText: It pleased Jehovah, for his righteousness’ sake, to magnify the law, and make it honorable.

units.leftText: But this is a people plundered and looted, all trapped in caves or imprisoned in dungeons. They have become plunder with no one to rescue them, and loot with no one to say, “Send them back!”
units.rightText: But this is a people robbed and plundered; they are all of them snared in holes, and they are hid in prison-houses: they are for a prey, and none delivereth; for a spoil, and none saith, Restore.

units.leftText: Who among you will pay attention to this? Who will listen and obey hereafter?
units.rightText: Who is there among you that will give ear to this? that will hearken and hear for the time to come?

units.leftText: Who gave Jacob up for spoil, and Israel to the plunderers? Was it not the LORD, against whom we have sinned? They were unwilling to walk in His ways, and they would not obey His law.
units.rightText: Who gave Jacob for a spoil, and Israel to the robbers? did not Jehovah? he against whom we have sinned, and in whose ways they would not walk, neither were they obedient unto his law.

units.leftText: So He poured out on them His furious anger and the fierceness of battle. It enveloped them in flames, but they did not understand; it consumed them, but they did not take it to heart.
units.rightText: Therefore he poured upon him the fierceness of his anger, and the strength of battle; and it set him on fire round about, yet he knew not; and it burned him, yet he laid it not to heart.

units.leftText: But now, this is what the LORD says— He who created you, O Jacob, and He who formed you, O Israel: “Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by your name; you are Mine!
units.rightText: But now thus saith Jehovah that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel: Fear not, for I have redeemed thee; I have called thee by thy name, thou art mine.

units.leftText: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and when you go through the rivers, they will not overwhelm you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be scorched; the flames will not set you ablaze.
units.rightText: When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned, neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.

units.leftText: For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior; I give Egypt for your ransom, Cush and Seba in your place.
units.rightText: For I am Jehovah thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour; I have given Egypt as thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba in thy stead.
leftNotes: 43:3 That is, the upper Nile region

units.leftText: Because you are precious and honored in My sight, and because I love you, I will give men in exchange for you and nations in place of your life.
units.rightText: Since thou hast been precious in my sight, and honorable, and I have loved thee; therefore will I give men in thy stead, and peoples instead of thy life.

units.leftText: Do not be afraid, for I am with you; I will bring your offspring from the east and gather you from the west.
units.rightText: Fear not; for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west;

units.leftText: I will say to the north, ‘Give them up!’ and to the south, ‘Do not hold them back!’ Bring My sons from afar, and My daughters from the ends of the earth—
units.rightText: I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back; bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the end of the earth;

units.leftText: everyone called by My name and created for My glory, whom I have indeed formed and made.”
units.rightText: every one that is called by my name, and whom I have created for my glory, whom I have formed, yea, whom I have made.

units.leftText: Bring out a people who have eyes but are blind, and who have ears but are deaf.
units.rightText: Bring forth the blind people that have eyes, and the deaf that have ears.

units.leftText: All the nations gather together and the peoples assemble. Who among them can declare this, and proclaim to us the former things? Let them present their witnesses to vindicate them, so that others may hear and say, “It is true.”
units.rightText: Let all the nations be gathered together, and let the peoples be assembled: who among them can declare this, and show us former things? let them bring their witnesses, that they may be justified; or let them hear, and say, It is truth.

units.leftText: “You are My witnesses,” declares the LORD, “and My servant whom I have chosen, so that you may consider and believe Me and understand that I am He. Before Me no god was formed, and after Me none will come.
units.rightText: Ye are my witnesses, saith Jehovah, and my servant whom I have chosen; that ye may know and believe me, and understand that I am he: before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me.

units.leftText: I, yes I, am the LORD, and there is no Savior but Me.
units.rightText: I, even I, am Jehovah; and besides me there is no saviour.

units.leftText: I alone decreed and saved and proclaimed— I, and not some foreign god among you. So you are My witnesses,” declares the LORD, “that I am God.
units.rightText: I have declared, and I have saved, and I have showed; and there was no strange god among you: therefore ye are my witnesses, saith Jehovah, and I am God.

units.leftText: Even from eternity I am He, and none can deliver out of My hand. When I act, who can reverse it?” A Way in the Wilderness
units.rightText: Yea, since the day was I am he; and there is none that can deliver out of my hand: I will work, and who can hinder it?

units.leftText: Thus says the LORD your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: “For your sake, I will send to Babylon and bring them all as fugitives, even the Chaldeans, in the ships in which they rejoice.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: For your sake I have sent to Babylon, and I will bring down all of them as fugitives, even the Chaldeans, in the ships of their rejoicing.
leftNotes: 43:14 That is, the Babylonians

units.leftText: I am the LORD, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, and your King.”
units.rightText: I am Jehovah, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, your King.

units.leftText: Thus says the LORD, who makes a way in the sea and a path through the surging waters,
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah, who maketh a way in the sea, and a path in the mighty waters;

units.leftText: who brings out the chariots and horses, the armies and warriors together, to lie down, never to rise again; to be extinguished, snuffed out like a wick:
units.rightText: who bringeth forth the chariot and horse, the army and the mighty man (they lie down together, they shall not rise; they are extinct, they are quenched as a wick):

units.leftText: “Do not call to mind the former things; pay no attention to the things of old.
units.rightText: Remember ye not the former things, neither consider the things of old.

units.leftText: Behold, I am about to do something new; even now it is coming. Do you not see it? Indeed, I will make a way in the wilderness and streams in the desert.
units.rightText: Behold, I will do a new thing; now shall it spring forth; shall ye not know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.

units.leftText: The beasts of the field will honor Me, the jackals and the ostriches, because I provide water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert, to give drink to My chosen people.
units.rightText: The beasts of the field shall honor me, the jackals and the ostriches; because I give waters in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen,
leftNotes: 43:20 Or serpents or dragons
43:20 Literally and daughters of an ostrich or and daughters of an owl

units.leftText: The people I formed for Myself will declare My praise. Israel’s Unfaithfulness (Judges 2:10–15|JDG 2:10-15*; Jeremiah 2:23–37|JER 2:23-37*)
units.rightText: the people which I formed for myself, that they might set forth my praise.

units.leftText: But you have not called on Me, O Jacob, because you have grown weary of Me, O Israel.
units.rightText: Yet thou hast not called upon me, O Jacob; but thou hast been weary of me, O Israel.

units.leftText: You have not brought Me sheep for burnt offerings, nor honored Me with your sacrifices. I have not burdened you with offerings, nor wearied you with frankincense.
units.rightText: Thou hast not brought me of thy sheep for burnt-offerings; neither hast thou honored me with thy sacrifices. I have not burdened thee with offerings, nor wearied thee with frankincense.

units.leftText: You have not bought Me sweet cane with your silver, nor satisfied Me with the fat of your sacrifices. But you have burdened Me with your sins; you have wearied Me with your iniquities.
units.rightText: Thou hast bought me no sweet cane with money, neither hast thou filled me with the fat of thy sacrifices; but thou hast burdened me with thy sins, thou hast wearied me with thine iniquities.

units.leftText: I, yes I, am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake and remembers your sins no more.
units.rightText: I, even I, am he that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake; and I will not remember thy sins.

units.leftText: Remind Me, let us argue the matter together. State your case, so that you may be vindicated.
units.rightText: Put me in remembrance; let us plead together: set thou forth thy cause, that thou mayest be justified.

units.leftText: Your first father sinned, and your spokesmen rebelled against Me.
units.rightText: Thy first father sinned, and thy teachers have transgressed against me.

units.leftText: So I will disgrace the princes of your sanctuary, and I will devote Jacob to destruction and Israel to reproach.”
units.rightText: Therefore I will profane the princes of the sanctuary; and I will make Jacob a curse, and Israel a reviling.
leftNotes: 43:28 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering.

units.leftText: But now listen, O Jacob My servant, Israel, whom I have chosen.
units.rightText: Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant, and Israel, who I have chosen:

units.leftText: This is the word of the LORD, your Maker, who formed you from the womb and who will help you: “Do not be afraid, O Jacob My servant, Jeshurun, whom I have chosen.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah that made thee, and formed thee from the womb, who will help thee: Fear not, O Jacob my servant; and thou, Jeshurun, whom I have chosen.
leftNotes: 44:2 Jeshurun means the upright one, a term of endearment for Israel.

units.leftText: For I will pour water on the thirsty land, and currents on the dry ground. I will pour out My Spirit on your descendants, and My blessing on your offspring.
units.rightText: For I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and streams upon the dry ground; I will pour my Spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring:

units.leftText: They will sprout among the grass like willows by flowing streams.
units.rightText: and they shall spring up among the grass, as willows by the watercourses.
leftNotes: 44:4 Or poplars

units.leftText: One will say, ‘I belong to the LORD,’ another will call himself by the name of Jacob, and still another will write on his hand, ‘The LORD’s,’ and will take the name of Israel.”
units.rightText: One shall say, I am Jehovah’s; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe with his hand unto Jehovah, and surname himself by the name of Israel.

units.leftText: Thus says the LORD, the King and Redeemer of Israel, the LORD of Hosts: “I am the first and I am the last, and there is no God but Me.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, Jehovah of hosts: I am the first, and I am the last; and besides me there is no God.

units.leftText: Who then is like Me? Let him say so! Let him declare his case before Me, since I established an ancient people. Let him foretell the things to come, and what is to take place.
units.rightText: And who, as I, shall call, and shall declare it, and set it in order for me, since I established the ancient people? and the things that are coming, and that shall come to pass, let them declare.

units.leftText: Do not tremble or fear. Have I not told you and declared it long ago? You are My witnesses! Is there any God but Me? There is no other Rock; I know not one.”
units.rightText: Fear ye not, neither be afraid: have I not declared unto thee of old, and showed it? and ye are my witnesses. Is there a God besides me? yea, there is no Rock; I know not any.

units.leftText: All makers of idols are nothing, and the things they treasure are worthless. Their witnesses fail to see or comprehend, so they are put to shame.
units.rightText: They that fashion a graven image are all of them vanity; and the things that they delight in shall not profit; and their own witnesses see not, nor know: that they may be put to shame.

units.leftText: Who fashions a god or casts an idol which profits him nothing?
units.rightText: Who hath fashioned a god, or molten an image that is profitable for nothing?

units.leftText: Behold, all his companions will be put to shame, for the craftsmen themselves are only human. Let them all assemble and take their stand; they will all be brought to terror and shame.
units.rightText: Behold, all his fellows shall be put to shame; and the workmen, they are of men: let them all be gathered together, let them stand up; they shall fear, they shall be put to shame together.

units.leftText: The blacksmith takes a tool and labors over the coals; he fashions an idol with hammers and forges it with his strong arms. Yet he grows hungry and loses his strength; he fails to drink water and grows faint.
units.rightText: The smith maketh an axe, and worketh in the coals, and fashioneth it with hammers, and worketh it with his strong arm: yea, he is hungry, and his strength faileth; he drinketh no water, and is faint.

units.leftText: The woodworker extends a measuring line; he marks it out with a stylus; he shapes it with chisels and outlines it with a compass. He fashions it in the likeness of man, like man in all his glory, that it may dwell in a shrine.
units.rightText: The carpenter stretcheth out a line; he marketh it out with a pencil; he shapeth it with planes, and he marketh it out with the compasses, and shapeth it after the figure of a man, according to the beauty of a man, to dwell in a house.

units.leftText: He cuts down cedars or retrieves a cypress or oak. He lets it grow strong among the trees of the forest. He plants a laurel, and the rain makes it grow.
units.rightText: He heweth him down cedars, and taketh the holm-tree and the oak, and strengtheneth for himself one among the trees of the forest: he planteth a fir-tree, and the rain doth nourish it.
leftNotes: 44:14 Or pine or juniper or fir

units.leftText: It serves as fuel for man. He takes some of it to warm himself, and he kindles a fire and bakes his bread. He also fashions it into a god and worships it; he makes an idol and bows down to it.
units.rightText: Then shall it be for a man to burn; and he taketh thereof, and warmeth himself; yea, he kindleth it, and baketh bread: yea, he maketh a god, and worshippeth it; he maketh it a graven image, and falleth down thereto.

units.leftText: He burns half of it in the fire, and he roasts meat on that half. He eats the roast and is satisfied. Indeed, he warms himself and says, “Ah! I am warm; I see the fire.”
units.rightText: He burneth part thereof in the fire; with part thereof he eateth flesh; he roasteth roast, and is satisfied; yea, he warmeth himself, and saith, Aha, I am warm, I have seen the fire.

units.leftText: From the rest he makes a god, his graven image. He bows down to it and worships; he prays to it and says, “Save me, for you are my god.”
units.rightText: And the residue thereof he maketh a god, even his graven image; he falleth down unto it and worshippeth, and prayeth unto it, and saith, Deliver me; for thou art my god.

units.leftText: They do not comprehend or discern, for He has shut their eyes so they cannot see and closed their minds so they cannot understand.
units.rightText: They know not, neither do they consider: for he hath shut their eyes, that they cannot see; and their hearts, that they cannot understand.

units.leftText: And no one considers in his heart, no one has the knowledge or insight to say, “I burned half of it in the fire, and I baked bread on its coals; I roasted meat and I ate. Shall I make something detestable with the rest of it? Shall I bow down to a block of wood?”
units.rightText: And none calleth to mind, neither is there knowledge nor understanding to say, I have burned part of it in the fire; yea, also I have baked bread upon the coals thereof; I have roasted flesh and eaten it: and shall I make the residue thereof an abomination? shall I fall down to the stock of a tree?

units.leftText: He feeds on ashes. His deluded heart has led him astray, and he cannot deliver himself or say, “Is not this thing in my right hand a lie?” Jerusalem to Be Restored
units.rightText: He feedeth on ashes; a deceived heart hath turned him aside; and he cannot deliver his soul, nor say, Is there not a lie in my right hand?

units.leftText: Remember these things, O Jacob, for you are My servant, O Israel. I have made you, and you are My servant; O Israel, I will never forget you.
units.rightText: Remember these things, O Jacob, and Israel; for thou art my servant: I have formed thee; thou art my servant: O Israel, thou shalt not be forgotten of me.

units.leftText: I have blotted out your transgressions like a cloud, and your sins like a mist. Return to Me, for I have redeemed you.
units.rightText: I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions, and, as a cloud, thy sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed thee.

units.leftText: Sing for joy, O heavens, for the LORD has done this; shout aloud, O depths of the earth. Break forth in song, O mountains, you forests and all your trees. For the LORD has redeemed Jacob, and revealed His glory in Israel.
units.rightText: Sing, O ye heavens, for Jehovah hath done it; shout, ye lower parts of the earth; break forth into singing, ye mountains, O forest, and every tree therein: for Jehovah hath redeemed Jacob, and will glorify himself in Israel.

units.leftText: Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer who formed you from the womb: “I am the LORD, who has made all things, who alone stretched out the heavens, who by Myself spread out the earth,
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah, thy Redeemer, and he that formed thee from the womb: I am Jehovah, that maketh all things; that stretcheth forth the heavens alone; that spreadeth abroad the earth (who is with me?);

units.leftText: who foils the signs of false prophets and makes fools of diviners, who confounds the wise and turns their knowledge into nonsense,
units.rightText: that frustrateth the signs of the liars, and maketh diviners mad; that turneth wise men backward, and maketh their knowledge foolish;

units.leftText: who confirms the message of His servant and fulfills the counsel of His messengers, who says of Jerusalem, ‘She will be inhabited,’ and of the cities of Judah, ‘They will be rebuilt, and I will restore their ruins,’
units.rightText: that confirmeth the word of his servant, and performeth the counsel of his messengers; that saith of Jerusalem, She shall be inhabited; and of the cities of Judah, They shall be built, and I will raise up the waste places thereof;

units.leftText: who says to the depths of the sea, ‘Be dry, and I will dry up your currents,’
units.rightText: that saith to the deep, Be dry, and I will dry up thy rivers;

units.leftText: who says of Cyrus, ‘My shepherd will fulfill all that I desire,’ who says of Jerusalem, ‘She will be rebuilt,’ and of the temple, ‘Let its foundation be laid.’”
units.rightText: That saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure, even saying of Jerusalem, She shall be built; and of the temple, Thy foundation shall be laid.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says to Cyrus His anointed, whose right hand I have grasped to subdue nations before him, to disarm kings, to open the doors before him, so that the gates will not be shut:
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him, and I will loose the loins of kings; to open the doors before him, and the gates shall not be shut:

units.leftText: “I will go before you and level the mountains; I will break down the gates of bronze and cut through the bars of iron.
units.rightText: I will go before thee, and make the rough places smooth; I will break in pieces the doors of brass, and cut in sunder the bars of iron;
leftNotes: 45:2 DSS and LXX; MT level the terrain

units.leftText: I will give you the treasures of darkness and the riches hidden in secret places, so that you may know that I am the LORD, the God of Israel, who calls you by name.
units.rightText: and I will give thee the treasures of darkness, and hidden riches of secret places, that thou mayest know that it is I, Jehovah, who call thee by thy name, even the God of Israel.

units.leftText: For the sake of Jacob My servant and Israel My chosen one, I call you by name; I have given you a title of honor, though you have not known Me.
units.rightText: For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel my chosen, I have called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me.

units.leftText: I am the LORD, and there is no other; there is no God but Me. I will equip you for battle, though you have not known Me,
units.rightText: I am Jehovah, and there is none else; besides me there is no God. I will gird thee, though thou hast not known me;

units.leftText: so that all may know, from where the sun rises to where it sets, that there is none but Me; I am the LORD, and there is no other.
units.rightText: that they may know from the rising of the sun, and from the west, that there is none besides me: I am Jehovah, and there is none else.

units.leftText: I form the light and create the darkness; I bring prosperity and create calamity. I, the LORD, do all these things.
units.rightText: I form the light, and create darkness; I make peace, and create evil; I am Jehovah, that doeth all these things.

units.leftText: Drip down, O heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness. Let the earth open up that salvation may sprout and righteousness spring up with it; I, the LORD, have created it.
units.rightText: Distil, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness: let the earth open, that it may bring forth salvation, and let it cause righteousness to spring up together; I, Jehovah, have created it.

units.leftText: Woe to him who quarrels with his Maker— one clay pot among many. Does the clay ask the potter, ‘What are you making?’ Does your work say, ‘He has no hands’?
units.rightText: Woe unto him that striveth with his Maker! a potsherd among the potsherds of the earth! Shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it, What makest thou? or thy work, He hath no hands?
leftNotes: 45:9 Cited in Romans 9:20|ROM 9:20*

units.leftText: Woe to him who says to his father, ‘What have you begotten?’ or to his mother, ‘What have you brought forth?’”
units.rightText: Woe unto him that saith unto a father, What begettest thou? or to a woman, With what travailest thou?

units.leftText: Thus says the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, and its Maker: “Concerning things to come, do you question Me about My sons, or instruct Me in the work of My hands?
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah, the Holy One of Israel, and his Maker: Ask me of the things that are to come; concerning my sons, and concerning the work of my hands, command ye me.

units.leftText: It is I who made the earth and created man upon it. It was My hands that stretched out the heavens, and I ordained all their host.
units.rightText: I have made the earth, and created man upon it: I, even my hands, have stretched out the heavens; and all their host have I commanded.

units.leftText: I will raise up Cyrus in righteousness, and I will make all his ways straight. He will rebuild My city and set My exiles free, but not for payment or reward, says the LORD of Hosts.”
units.rightText: I have raised him up in righteousness, and I will make straight all his ways: he shall build my city, and he shall let my exiles go free, not for price nor reward, saith Jehovah of hosts.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says: “The products of Egypt and the merchandise of Cush, along with the Sabeans, men of stature, will come over to you and will be yours; they will trudge behind you; they will come over in chains and bow down to you. They will confess to you: ‘God is indeed with you, and there is no other; there is no other God.’”
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah, The labor of Egypt, and the merchandise of Ethiopia, and the Sabeans, men of stature, shall come over unto thee, and they shall be thine: they shall go after thee, in chains they shall come over; and they shall fall down unto thee, they shall make supplication unto thee, saying, Surely God is in thee; and there is none else, there is no God.
leftNotes: 45:14 That is, the upper Nile region

units.leftText: Truly You are a God who hides Himself, O God of Israel, the Savior.
units.rightText: Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour.

units.leftText: They will all be put to shame and humiliated; the makers of idols will depart together in disgrace.
units.rightText: They shall be put to shame, yea, confounded, all of them; they shall go into confusion together that are makers of idols.

units.leftText: But Israel will be saved by the LORD with an everlasting salvation; you will not be put to shame or humiliated, to ages everlasting.
units.rightText: But Israel shall be saved by Jehovah with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be put to shame nor confounded world without end.

units.leftText: For thus says the LORD, who created the heavens— He is God; He formed the earth and fashioned it; He established it; He did not create it to be empty, but formed it to be inhabited: “I am the LORD, and there is no other.
units.rightText: For thus saith Jehovah that created the heavens, the God that formed the earth and made it, that established it and created it not a waste, that formed it to be inhabited: I am Jehovah; and there is none else.

units.leftText: I have not spoken in secret, from a place in a land of darkness. I did not say to the descendants of Jacob, ‘Seek Me in a wasteland.’ I, the LORD, speak the truth; I say what is right.
units.rightText: I have not spoken in secret, in a place of the land of darkness; I said not unto the seed of Jacob, Seek ye me in vain: I, Jehovah, speak righteousness, I declare things that are right.

units.leftText: Come, gather together, and draw near, you fugitives from the nations. Ignorant are those who carry idols of wood and pray to a god that cannot save.
units.rightText: Assemble yourselves and come; draw near together, ye that are escaped of the nations: they have no knowledge that carry the wood of their graven image, and pray unto a god that cannot save.

units.leftText: Speak up and present your case— yes, let them take counsel together. Who foretold this long ago? Who announced it from ancient times? Was it not I, the LORD? There is no other God but Me, a righteous God and Savior; there is none but Me.
units.rightText: Declare ye, and bring it forth; yea, let them take counsel together: who hath showed this from ancient time? who hath declared it of old? have not I, Jehovah? and there is no God else besides me, a just God and a Saviour; there is none besides me.

units.leftText: Turn to Me and be saved, all the ends of the earth; for I am God, and there is no other.
units.rightText: Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth; for I am God, and there is none else.

units.leftText: By Myself I have sworn; truth has gone out from My mouth, a word that will not be revoked: Every knee will bow before Me, every tongue will swear allegiance.
units.rightText: By myself have I sworn, the word is gone forth from my mouth in righteousness, and shall not return, that unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear.
leftNotes: 45:23 Literally every tongue will swear; LXX every tongue will swear by God; cited in Romans 14:11|ROM 14:11*

units.leftText: Surely they will say of Me, ‘In the LORD alone are righteousness and strength.’” All who rage against Him will come to Him and be put to shame.
units.rightText: Only in Jehovah, it is said of me, is righteousness and strength; even to him shall men come; and all they that were incensed against him shall be put to shame.

units.leftText: In the LORD all descendants of Israel will be justified and will exult.
units.rightText: In Jehovah shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.

units.leftText: Bel crouches; Nebo cowers. Their idols weigh down beasts and cattle. The images you carry are burdensome, a load to the weary animal.
units.rightText: Bel boweth down, Nebo stoopeth; their idols are upon the beasts, and upon the cattle: the things that ye carried about are made a load, a burden to the weary beast.

units.leftText: The gods cower; they crouch together, unable to relieve the burden; but they themselves go into captivity.
units.rightText: They stoop, they bow down together; they could not deliver the burden, but themselves are gone into captivity.

units.leftText: “Listen to Me, O house of Jacob, all the remnant of the house of Israel, who have been sustained from the womb, carried along since birth.
units.rightText: Hearken unto me, O house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, that have been borne by me from their birth, that have been carried from the womb;

units.leftText: Even to your old age, I will be the same, and I will bear you up when you turn gray. I have made you, and I will carry you; I will sustain you and deliver you.
units.rightText: and even to old age I am he, and even to hoar hairs will I carry you; I have made, and I will bear; yea, I will carry, and will deliver.

units.leftText: To whom will you liken Me or count Me equal? To whom will you compare Me, that we should be alike?
units.rightText: To whom will ye liken me, and make me equal, and compare me, that we may be like?

units.leftText: They pour out their bags of gold and weigh out silver on scales; they hire a goldsmith to fashion it into a god, so they can bow down and worship.
units.rightText: Such as lavish gold out of the bag, and weigh silver in the balance, they hire a goldsmith, and he maketh it a god; they fall down, yea, they worship.

units.leftText: They lift it to their shoulder and carry it along; they set it in its place, and there it stands, not budging from that spot. They cry out to it, but it does not answer; it saves no one from his troubles.
units.rightText: They bear it upon the shoulder, they carry it, and set it in its place, and it standeth, from its place shall it not remove: yea, one may cry unto it, yet can it not answer, nor save him out of his trouble.

units.leftText: Remember this and be brave; take it to heart, you transgressors!
units.rightText: Remember this, and show yourselves men; bring it again to mind, O ye transgressors.

units.leftText: Remember what happened long ago, for I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is none like Me.
units.rightText: Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me;

units.leftText: I declare the end from the beginning, and from ancient times what is still to come. I say, ‘My purpose will stand, and all My good pleasure I will accomplish.’
units.rightText: declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times things that are not yet done; saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure;

units.leftText: I summon a bird of prey from the east, a man for My purpose from a far-off land. Truly I have spoken, and truly I will bring it to pass. I have planned it, and I will surely do it.
units.rightText: calling a ravenous bird from the east, the man of my counsel from a far country; yea, I have spoken, I will also bring it to pass; I have purposed, I will also do it.

units.leftText: Listen to Me, you stubborn people, far removed from righteousness:
units.rightText: Hearken unto me, ye stout-hearted, that are far from righteousness:

units.leftText: I am bringing My righteousness near; it is not far away, and My salvation will not be delayed. I will grant salvation to Zion and adorn Israel with My splendor.[’’]
units.rightText: I bring near my righteousness, it shall not be far off, and my salvation shall not tarry; and I will place salvation in Zion for Israel my glory.

units.leftText: “Go down and sit in the dust, O Virgin Daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground without a throne, O Daughter of the Chaldeans! For you will no longer be called tender or delicate.
units.rightText: Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon; sit on the ground without a throne, O daughter of the Chaldeans: for thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate.
leftNotes: 47:1 That is, the Babylonians; also in verse 5

units.leftText: Take millstones and grind flour; remove your veil; strip off your skirt, bare your thigh, and wade through the streams.
units.rightText: Take the millstones, and grind meal; remove thy veil, strip off the train, uncover the leg, pass through the rivers.

units.leftText: Your nakedness will be uncovered and your shame will be exposed. I will take vengeance; I will spare no one.”
units.rightText: Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and will spare no man.

units.leftText: Our Redeemer — the LORD of Hosts is His name — is the Holy One of Israel.
units.rightText: Our Redeemer, Jehovah of hosts is his name, the Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: “Sit in silence and go into darkness, O Daughter of the Chaldeans. For you will no longer be called the queen of kingdoms.
units.rightText: Sit thou silent, and get thee into darkness, O daughter of the Chaldeans; for thou shalt no more be called The mistress of kingdoms.

units.leftText: I was angry with My people; I profaned My heritage, and I placed them under your control. You showed them no mercy; even on the elderly you laid a most heavy yoke.
units.rightText: I was wroth with my people, I profaned mine inheritance, and gave them into thy hand: thou didst show them no mercy; upon the aged hast thou very heavily laid thy yoke.

units.leftText: You said, ‘I will be queen forever.’ You did not take these things to heart or consider their outcome.
units.rightText: And thou saidst, I shall be mistress for ever; so that thou didst not lay these things to thy heart, neither didst remember the latter end thereof.

units.leftText: So now hear this, O lover of luxury who sits securely, who says to herself, ‘I am, and there is none besides me. I will never be a widow or know the loss of children.’
units.rightText: Now therefore hear this, thou that art given to pleasures, that sittest securely, that sayest in thy heart, I am, and there is none else besides me; I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of children:

units.leftText: These two things will overtake you in a moment, in a single day: loss of children, and widowhood. They will come upon you in full measure, in spite of your many sorceries and the potency of your spells.
units.rightText: but these two things shall come to thee in a moment in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood; in their full measure shall they come upon thee, in the multitude of thy sorceries, and the great abundance of thine enchantments.

units.leftText: You were secure in your wickedness; you said, ‘No one sees me.’ Your wisdom and knowledge led you astray; you told yourself, ‘I am, and there is none besides me.’
units.rightText: For thou hast trusted in thy wickedness; thou hast said, None seeth me; thy wisdom and thy knowledge, it hath perverted thee, and thou hast said in thy heart, I am, and there is none else besides me.

units.leftText: But disaster will come upon you; you will not know how to charm it away. A calamity will befall you that you will be unable to ward off. Devastation will happen to you suddenly and unexpectedly.
units.rightText: Therefore shall evil come upon thee; thou shalt not know the dawning thereof: and mischief shall fall upon thee; thou shalt not be able to put it away: and desolation shall come upon thee suddenly, which thou knowest not.

units.leftText: So take your stand with your spells and with your many sorceries, with which you have wearied yourself from your youth. Perhaps you will succeed; perhaps you will inspire terror!
units.rightText: Stand now with thine enchantments, and with the multitude of thy sorceries, wherein thou hast labored from thy youth; if so be thou shalt be able to profit, if so be thou mayest prevail.

units.leftText: You are wearied by your many counselors; let them come forward now and save you— your astrologers who observe the stars, who monthly predict your fate.
units.rightText: Thou art wearied in the multitude of thy counsels: let now the astrologers, the star-gazers, the monthly prognosticators, stand up, and save thee from the things that shall come upon thee.

units.leftText: Surely they are like stubble; the fire will burn them up. They cannot deliver themselves from the power of the flame. There will be no coals to warm them or fire to sit beside.
units.rightText: Behold, they shall be as stubble; the fire shall burn them; they shall not deliver themselves from the power of the flame: it shall not be a coal to warm at, nor a fire to sit before.

units.leftText: This is what they are to you — those with whom you have labored and traded from youth— each one strays in his own direction; not one of them can save you.[’’]
units.rightText: Thus shall the things be unto thee wherein thou hast labored: they that have trafficked with thee from thy youth shall wander every one to his quarter; there shall be none to save thee.

units.leftText: “Listen to this, O house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel, who have descended from the line of Judah, who swear by the name of the LORD, who invoke the God of Israel — but not in truth or righteousness —
units.rightText: Hear ye this, O house of Jacob, who are called by the name of Israel, and are come forth out of the waters of Judah; who swear by the name of Jehovah, and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth, nor in righteousness

units.leftText: who indeed call yourselves after the holy city and lean on the God of Israel; the LORD of Hosts is His name.
units.rightText: (for they call themselves of the holy city, and stay themselves upon the God of Israel; Jehovah of hosts is his name):

units.leftText: I foretold the former things long ago; they came out of My mouth and I proclaimed them. Suddenly I acted, and they came to pass.
units.rightText: I have declared the former things from of old; yea, they went forth out of my mouth, and I showed them: suddenly I did them, and they came to pass.

units.leftText: For I knew that you are stubborn; your neck is iron and your forehead is bronze.
units.rightText: Because I knew that thou art obstinate, and thy neck is an iron sinew, and thy brow brass;

units.leftText: Therefore I declared it to you long ago; I announced it before it came to pass, so that you could not claim, ‘My idol has done this; my carved image and molten god has ordained it.’
units.rightText: therefore I have declared it to thee from of old; before it came to pass I showed it thee; lest thou shouldest say, Mine idol hath done them, and my graven image, and my molten image, hath commanded them.

units.leftText: You have heard these things; look at them all. Will you not acknowledge them? From now on I will tell you of new things, hidden things unknown to you.
units.rightText: Thou hast heard it; behold all this; and ye, will ye not declare it? I have showed thee new things from this time, even hidden things, which thou hast not known.

units.leftText: They are created now, and not long ago; you have not heard of them before today. So you cannot claim, ‘I already knew them!’
units.rightText: They are created now, and not from of old; and before this day thou heardest them not; lest thou shouldest say, Behold, I knew them.

units.leftText: You have never heard; you have never understood; for a long time your ears have not been open. For I knew how deceitful you are; you have been called a rebel from birth.
units.rightText: Yea, thou heardest not; yea, thou knewest not; yea, from of old thine ear was not opened: for I knew that thou didst deal very treacherously, and wast called a transgressor from the womb.

units.leftText: For the sake of My name I will delay My wrath; for the sake of My praise I will restrain it, so that you will not be cut off.
units.rightText: For my name’s sake will I defer mine anger, and for my praise will I refrain for thee, that I cut thee not off.

units.leftText: See, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have tested you in the furnace of affliction.
units.rightText: Behold, I have refined thee, but not as silver; I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction.

units.leftText: For My own sake, My very own sake, I will act; for how can I let Myself be defamed? I will not yield My glory to another. Deliverance Promised to Israel
units.rightText: For mine own sake, for mine own sake, will I do it; for how should my name be profaned? and my glory will I not give to another.

units.leftText: Listen to Me, O Jacob, and Israel, whom I have called: I am He; I am the first, and I am the last.
units.rightText: Hearken unto me, O Jacob, and Israel my called: I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.

units.leftText: Surely My own hand founded the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens; when I summon them, they stand up together.
units.rightText: Yea, my hand hath laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand hath spread out the heavens: when I call unto them, they stand up together.

units.leftText: Come together, all of you, and listen: Which of the idols has foretold these things? The LORD’s chosen ally will carry out His desire against Babylon, and His arm will be against the Chaldeans.
units.rightText: Assemble yourselves, all ye, and hear; who among them hath declared these things? He whom Jehovah loveth shall perform his pleasure on Babylon, and his arm shall be on the Chaldeans.
leftNotes: 48:14 That is, the Babylonians; also in verse 20

units.leftText: I, even I, have spoken; yes, I have called him. I have brought him, and he will succeed in his mission.
units.rightText: I, even I, have spoken; yea, I have called him; I have brought him, and he shall make his way prosperous.

units.leftText: Come near to Me and listen to this: From the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time it happened, I was there.” And now the Lord GOD has sent me, accompanied by His Spirit.
